docs.title: CTR2WUP
docs.text:
CI results

Documentation · Releases · Project · Contributing

CTR2WUP is an experimental 3DS-to-Wii U converter. Its goal is a Windows GUI that translates a 3DS game into an individual WUP title, with the top screen on the TV and the bottom screen, touch and controls on the GamePad.

Early development: commercial games, playable-game WUP conversion and the Windows GUI are not available yet. Current releases provide developer tools and original homebrew diagnostics. Super Mario 3D Land is the first planned compatibility target.

docs.title: Approach
docs.text:
The PC translates ARM game code ahead of time into C, which is compiled for Wii U PowerPC. A shared native runtime supplies the required 3DS services, graphics, input, audio and saves. The intended workflow is:

Select game → Configure title and artwork → Inject → Install WUP → Play

Support will expand as the shared runtime implements more game requirements. See architecture and compatibility for the supported subsets and current limits.

docs.title: Current capabilities
docs.text:
• Bounded 3DS/CXI/CIA inspection, optional local decryption with supplied keys, RomFS integrity checks and private asset preparation.
  • ARM/Thumb/VFP translation foundations, checked memory, guest threads and scoped 3DS services.
  • Original compiled homebrew with two-screen framebuffer output, input, SD save/reload and read-only assets, including reviewed Wii U test results.
  • Texture decoding, GX memory/display transfers, PICA configuration and vertex decoding. PICA draws, shaders and 3DS guest audio remain unfinished.
  • Reproducible RPX/WUHB diagnostics and original packaging fixtures. Actual WUP installation and full Windows conversion still require acceptance.

docs.title: Progress
docs.text: Development Project tracks the seven milestones and their implementation/evidence tasks. Completing a task does not accept a full milestone. See the roadmap and current status for scope and verification details.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
Download a matching development release and check its SHA256SUMS.txt. For Wii U diagnostics, copy the kit's sd-card/ contents to your SD root and launch the WUHB in Aroma. Follow its prompts; plain-text results are saved to sd:/ctr2wup/. Original diagnostics need no ROM or key. See getting started and console testing.

For development, use Python 3.12+, Make and a C compiler. The first SDK setup also requires Docker. From the repository root:

python3 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python3 -m pip install -e '.[packaging,decryption]'
bash tools/install-wiiu-sdk.sh
python3 -m host doctor
make check
python3 -m host build --target prototype --output "artifacts/my-diagnostic"

This builds an original RPX/WUHB diagnostic. Build instructions, Windows notes and compiled homebrew cover other workflows. Generated files stay under ignored artifacts/; local ROMs, keys and derived game data belong under ignored private/.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Focused fixes, original reference fixtures, documentation and reproducible console reports are welcome. Start with Contributing, open work items and the Project. Report bugs with build identity and relevant test results; keep game data and keys out of issues. Security reports follow SECURITY.md.

docs.title: License and acknowledgments
docs.text:
CTR2WUP source is MIT licensed. Dependencies retain their own licenses; see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES and the dependency audit. Builds use devkitPro, WUT and libctru. The planned injector workflow is inspired by UWUVCI AIO.

docs.title: Continuing CTR2WUP
docs.text:
Read STATUS.md and docs/milestones.md before making compatibility claims. The user-supplied requirements are in docs/project-brief.md. Build source in the existing isolated checkout; do not create a worktree unless asked.

  • Run make check for Python plus C tests/ASan/UBSan; make prototype for RPX/WUHB.
  • Toolchain setup: bash tools/install-wiiu-sdk.sh; optional host lifter: bash tools/install-translator.sh. Preserve signature/checksum/TLS verification.
  • Keep ROMs, assets, translated commercial code, saves, packages, traces and credentials under ignored private directories. Never include them in source bundles, logs or public artifacts. Synthetic fixtures must be original.
  • Never report console execution from compilation or desktop passes. Unsupported CPU/services/GPU states must fail visibly. Structural package validation does not establish authenticity or installer acceptance.
  • Maintain STATUS.md, milestone evidence, architecture/build/compatibility docs and versioned reports. Do not add a GUI before the execution pipeline works.
  • For Codex-generated commits, install the opt-in repository hook with python3 tools/codex-attribution.py install, then use git codex-commit. Preserve existing hooks and human attribution. See CONTRIBUTING.md for identity and authentication limits; never rewrite history solely to add attribution.

Maintained source: AGENTS.md · 1b14ea67cba6. GitHub source and issue links may require repository access.

docs.title: Contributing to CTR2WUP
docs.text: CTR2WUP targets a Windows GUI that converts an owned 3DS game into a playable Wii U WUP. Current builds are development tools and original diagnostics; the commercial execution pipeline and GUI are still being implemented. Read STATUS.md, the milestones and AGENTS.md before proposing compatibility or acceptance changes.

docs.title: Choose verifiable work
docs.text:
Check existing issues and the milestone checklist. For a bug, provide a minimal reproduction with original data. For a feature, describe the resulting behavior, its milestone and acceptance evidence. The issue forms also accept Wii U test results, including missing reports, failed storage checks and hangs.

Do not upload ROMs, key databases, personal keys, extracted game assets, saves, translated commercial code, game packages or credentials. Keep them under ignored private/ directories locally. Original diagnostic TXT files are useful after reviewing them for private paths or data. Use SECURITY.md for vulnerability reports instead of a normal issue.

docs.title: Build and check
docs.text:
Use Python 3.12+, Make and a C compiler. Install the verified Wii U SDK with the repository script; the first installation requires Docker. Optional encrypted input/packaging tests use the cryptography dependency. The target SDK uses devkitPro's devkitPPC, WUT and Wii U tools; the host compiler runs desktop tests.

python3 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python3 -m pip install -e '.[packaging,decryption]'
export CTR2WUP_SDK_ROOT="$PWD/../ctr2wup-sdk"
bash tools/install-wiiu-sdk.sh
export DEVKITPRO="$CTR2WUP_SDK_ROOT"
export DEVKITPPC="$DEVKITPRO/devkitPPC"
make check
make prototype

make check runs Python and portable C suites with sanitizer checks. make prototype builds RPX/WUHB diagnostics. Neither command proves physical Wii U behavior or WUP installation. An existing official devkitPro installation can be used by setting DEVKITPRO and DEVKITPPC to its SDK paths. For Windows, use devkitPro's MSYS2 environment and signed wiiu-dev packages; the extracted Linux SDK cannot run natively on Windows. Consult Windows build notes, upstream integration and the focused test suites for requirements specific to your change. SDK installation must preserve checksum, signature and TLS verification.

docs.title: Console evidence and diagnostic releases
docs.text:
Use the versioned original diagnostic build and instructions for the requested test round. Record its release tag or commit, displayed application version and artifact checksum where available. A newer source version does not establish that an older console result tested the new behavior.

For Aroma, copy a diagnostic kit's sd-card/ contents to the SD root; WUHB apps belong under sd:/wiiu/apps/. Matching RPX files require an RPX-capable launcher. These files are homebrew applications, not WUP installation directories. Follow guided testing for controls and the expected sd:/ctr2wup/ TXT results. Preserve failed-run reports and explicitly report when no new file appeared. Include exact firmware, Aroma and launcher versions when known, plus observed exit/Menu behavior.

Published diagnostic releases and CI build artifacts demonstrate only their documented original fixture/build checks. Commercial games, guest PICA rendering, guest audio and installed playable WUP output still have separate acceptance gates in the milestone checklist.

docs.title: Submit a pull request
docs.text:
Keep the change focused and explain the concrete before/after behavior. Link its issue or milestone, record relevant checks and identify unavailable prerequisites. Use the pull request template. Update affected status, architecture, compatibility and build documentation when behavior or evidence changes; do not claim console execution from compilation. Record evidence in versioned reports where the existing workflow calls for them.

New fixtures must be original and reproducible from source. Guest memory is little-endian even on big-endian PowerPC; avoid native guest-word loads and keep unsupported states explicit. Review licenses and notices before adding a dependency or redistributing an executable. Generated builds belong under ignored artifacts/; inspect release contents for private data before publication.

docs.title: Agent-assisted work
docs.text: Repository Copilot instructions and specialist profiles under .github/agents provide CPU/runtime, host-pipeline, graphics and console-evidence context. Supported clients can select them when Copilot access is available. These files do not turn on paid services or autonomous jobs. Agent changes receive the same review and validation as any contribution; their summaries must identify pending physical and commercial acceptance checks.

docs.title: Codex commit attribution
docs.text:
For work generated by Codex, install the opt-in hook in this checkout:

python3 tools/codex-attribution.py install
git codex-commit -m "Describe the concrete change"

The wrapper records Codex as author using the verified OpenAI-owned ChatGPT Codex Connector bot identity. The hook adds OpenAI's published trailer exactly once: Co-authored-by: Codex <noreply@openai.com>. The published Codex attribution source records the commit and PR formats used here. Add Generated with [Codex](https://openai.com/codex/). to the associated PR body.

Ordinary git commit retains your identity and message. Installation is local to this repository, preserves global configuration and refuses conflicting hooks or aliases. Use python if that is your Windows Python command. The public bot email identifies commit authorship; it supplies no bot login, signature or access. Pushes, PR creation and merges still use the connected account. Existing history is preserved; GitHub decides how bot authors appear in contributor statistics.

Maintained source: CONTRIBUTING.md · 1b14ea67cba6. GitHub source and issue links may require repository access.

docs.title: Security policy
docs.text: CTR2WUP processes local binary containers, private key material and generated artifacts. Reports involving out-of-bounds parsing, private data exposure, arbitrary host-path access or unsafe build/packaging behavior are security issues.

docs.title: Report privately
docs.text:
Use Security → Report a vulnerability on this repository if GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled. If that option is unavailable, ask the maintainer for a private reporting route in a normal issue without exploit details, affected private data or attachments. Do not assume an issue is private because repository access is currently restricted.

Include the affected commit/version, platform, impact and a minimal reproduction using original synthetic input. Do not submit ROMs, personal keys, key databases, commercial assets, saves, translated game code or credentials. Describe required private data by type instead of attaching it. If credentials or keys were exposed, remove shared copies and rotate credentials where possible before discussing the incident publicly.

docs.title: Support boundaries
docs.text:
The current development branch is the maintenance target. No production security support window or stable release series has been established. Prefer the latest development build when reproducing a report, and state when the problem also affects an older version. A reviewed fix and tests are needed before a report can be considered resolved.

Container hashes and package structure checks establish integrity within their documented scope; they do not establish signature authenticity, safe installation or compatibility with a commercial game. Preserve the private-input boundaries in AGENTS.md and the limitations in architecture.

Maintained source: SECURITY.md · 1b14ea67cba6. GitHub source and issue links may require repository access.

docs.title: CTR2WUP status
docs.text:
Updated October 13, 2026 (America/New_York) · v0.20.0. The target remains an UWUVCI-style Windows GUI: select an owned 3DS game, configure title/artwork, click Inject, install its individual WUP and play from Wii U Menu. Requirements, product plan, documentation and acceptance gates define scope.

Approximately 20% implemented; 0/7 full milestones accepted. This is a rough engineering estimate, not a test-count percentage or release-date prediction. No commercial profile, playable Mario build, PICA draw renderer or finished GUI is enabled. Current binaries are original homebrew diagnostics.

docs.title: v0.20.0 increment
docs.text:
All diagnostic variants initialize a fresh native AX context before running self-tests or waiting for input. An inherited same-process context is reset; owned voices are released before AX shutdown and foreground changes. Compiled apps acquire no tone voice. Failure states and lifecycle counters enter the small result and full trace. A two-step Audio Check asks whether launch music stopped and whether the original native tone played on both outputs. This is not 3DS guest audio, and physical silence remains pending.

The private physical round now verifies named TXT read-back, original fresh-launch save reload, embedded/SD RomFS and GX transfer/configuration. Correct pictures and Minus return have user confirmation; the launch-music defect remains separate. The save completion prompt now explicitly distinguishes a fresh app launch from an in-app Plus restart.

Project #2 population/overview/fields/views are verified using the Actions secret. Source tracking still cannot overwrite existing board values. Docs-only Pages publication and the dynamic chart use a reviewed trusted-main workflow; hosting must be verified before being reported live. Application source remains private.

Validation: 349 Python tests and 20 C suites passed before the hosting additions; report/guide has 603 assertions and AX lifecycle has 149. Current Audio Check and compiled GX RPX/WUHB cross-builds passed. Final hosting/chart checks are recorded with this increment's delivery receipts. Full milestone acceptance remains 0/7.

docs.title: v0.19.0 increment (historical)
docs.text:
An original bounded vertex-attribute decoder handles signed8, unsigned8, signed16 and finite little-endian float32 from explicit streams/input permutations. It checks complete layouts, ranges, capacity and aliases before publishing output. Lane defaults are explicit; fixed/index attributes, PICA loader-state adaptation, float24 arithmetic, shaders and draws remain unsupported. See the vertex contract. GCC and Clang normal/ASan/UBSan and emulated big-endian PowerPC Linux pass 166,547 original assertions each. The devkitPPC module compiles; its measured decoder stack frame is 64 bytes. This is not physical Espresso execution or a rendered scene.

Project #2 now owns tracking policy. Prepared tooling adds a preserved detailed Project overview, priority/work-type fields and filtered views, reads canonical board values, mirrors issue status/resources and exports safe aggregates for an interactive dashboard. Source sync carries requirements/evidence only, never existing tracking state. The README's static progress image is removed. Live population and hosted publication remain blocked: the secure personal requirement is saved, but the environment reports no saved binding and Project reads remain forbidden. No Project, website or token-enabled Actions run is falsely marked live.

The focused console handoff is in artifacts/delivery/console-focus-2026-10-12/. Its hash-verified ZIP combines GX/PICA setup 0.18.0, retained Save/RomFS result fixes 0.14.6 and optional SD assets 0.16.0; every app version is explicit. Existing reports/snapshot siblings are preserved. The tester is now at their Wii U; new console evidence remains pending until reviewed. No long native/input rerun is required solely for the version increment.

Reports: artifacts/reports/project-vertex-v019/ and the earlier vertex host receipt.

docs.title: v0.18.0 increment
docs.text:
The bounded native PICA command front end now executes finalized raw viewport/ scissor configuration through standard GX command 1. Masks, repeated/grouped writes, full-stream/counter validation, staged guest input and P3D completion are implemented. Unknown registers, draws, uploads and control flags fail before state/output changes, retaining pending queue work. See the contract.

Validation passes 306 Python tests and 18 C suites, normal and ASan/UBSan; the new PICA suite has 67,706 assertions and the integrated GX suite has 1,619. The independent pinned-libctru builder/C/Python matrix passes 353 original cases, with identical emulated big-endian PowerPC receipts. The compiled GX application executes 17 commands including one no-draw PICA list, exits after 1,489,172 instructions with zero fallback and retains exact prior transfer pictures. Native and compiled GX v0.18.0 RPX/WUHB cross-builds pass. Physical console behavior, actual draws/shaders and full M4 acceptance remain open.

The owner supplied Project #2. The tracking tool selects it directly and cannot create a duplicate on access failure. Direct Project reads still return Resource not accessible by integration; its fields/items and automated population remain unverified. Normal repository Git/issue/CI work continues.

Reports: artifacts/reports/pica-v018/. Earlier diagnostic kits remain preserved.

docs.title: v0.17.0 increment
docs.text:
The standard GSP command ring now executes DMA, triggered memory fills, unscaled equal-size display conversion, raw strided texture copy and cache-region checks. It commits commands in order and preserves a failing entry/later work; all ranges/permissions/allocations are checked before that command changes output. Staging handles guest overlap, relay aliases are protected, and bulk memory writes invalidate exclusive/code snapshots including executable storage aliases. PSC/PPF/DMA completions follow bounded ring behavior. PICA lists remain unsupported.

The original stock-libctru application uses 16 GX operations and verifies exact green/red/green TV images with blue GamePad pixels. Its sanitized AOT run exits after 1,487,784 instructions, zero fallback, with three deliberately unavailable startup services still recorded. Desktop PASS does not imply all services or Wii U rendering are implemented. The GX contract records alignment/size/format/layout limits and the optional two-step console guide.

Independent review found and corrected missing fill-trigger validation and signaling for dropped interrupts. Required make check passes 291 Python tests and 17 C suites, normal and ASan/UBSan. GX has 1,102 assertions; report/guide has 587. The transfer matrix has 400 original C/Python/reference color/layout comparisons and matching emulated big-endian PowerPC hashes. Reference color/ Morton primitives were tested; the external full transfer engine was not. Fresh Native and GX Transfers RPX/WUHB cross-builds carry v0.17.0.

Reports: artifacts/reports/gx-transfers-v017/. Delivery: artifacts/delivery/gx-github-0.17.0/, containing source/wheel, original Native/GX diagnostics, reference images, guides and checksum/manifest. The release record and CI provide repository-visible delivery/evidence; consult the actual Actions run status.

docs.title: GitHub development
docs.text:
Seven milestone issues and milestones group 35 focused work issues with acceptance criteria, dependencies and waiting resources. The overviews coordinate full gates rather than substituting for implementation tasks. Managed sections synchronize from docs/milestone-status.json; comments/manual notes are retained and no acceptance gate is auto-closed. Contribution/console-result forms, ownership, security reporting guidance and four specialist Copilot profiles support review. Exclusive status labels, priority/component tags and trusted API-only automation report issue, PR and associated branch state. This follows the requested Odysseus model; merged code never automatically accepts console or full-milestone gates.

Automatic CI covers Python 3.12/3.14, GCC/Clang sanitizers, Windows host/portable-C, workflow lint and immutable-SDK native Wii U artifacts. Required CI aggregates those checks. Deep Windows AOT/WPF and eligibility-gated CodeQL are manual; agent profiles do not enable a paid subscription or run unattended. Hosted main CI passed on source d280dad: all eight CI checks, including Python 3.12/3.14, GCC/Clang sanitizers, the Windows baseline and Wii U build. Windows runs 237 Python cases with three documented filesystem/privilege skips plus all 17 normal C suites. The separate Documentation build passed. Deep Windows validation passed, including real pinned external AOT, Unicode execution and .NET 10 WPF tooling. This verifies development tools; full Windows conversion and GUI remain unfinished. GitHub development explains artifacts, release policy and management operations still awaiting access.

The existing GitHub integration rejected Projects creation and repository administration/security-setting writes with Resource not accessible by integration. Issue/milestone writes work. Project board, About/topics/Discussions and security-setting changes need the relevant GitHub connection permissions; those features are not falsely marked enabled. Searchable documentation has a strict build, rendered-link checks, an offline HTML guide and a free public docs-only Pages export. The user confirms private Pages is unavailable on their free plan; application source remains private. The user explicitly declines branch protection for the private free-plan repository. Topic branches, reviewable PRs and passing CI are the maintenance policy. Local documentation builds do not establish live hosting. The connection rejected public docs-repository creation with HTTP 403, so its free hosted publication needs owner access. The standalone HTML reader and complete public export remain available for download. Future Codex commits use an opt-in attribution hook and verified public bot identity; normal commits and existing history retain their authors. No repository visibility or paid entitlement was changed.

docs.title: Console evidence and inputs still needed
docs.text:
Five new result files establish original Save, embedded RomFS, SD-file assets and GX transfer/configuration checks. The additional Save 0.14.6 full trace confirms reload in its first guest session after closing and reopening the app. All new guides complete without failures/skips; guest fallback/fault are zero. The user confirms correct screens and normal Minus return, but reports Wii U launch music continuing throughout. Raw uploads remain private and older failures are retained separately in the evidence review.

The tester reports latest U.S. firmware, Aroma and WUP Installer GX2; exact versions remain unknown. No console is attached.

  • Audio: run only Audio Check and GX Transfers 0.20.0 for launch silence, native tone and compiled stability/exit. No Save/RomFS or long controls-guide repeat is required solely for this version.
  • Platform: exact versions, Home/APT routes, recovery and installed original WUP evidence remain separate acceptance work.
  • Mario: supplied CIA exceeds the 32 MiB attachment limit; small intake has encrypted content and no executable. Prepare locally or use an already decrypted owned dump, then privately export the small executable intake. Keys remain local. Actual revision/assets/required services and gameplay are unverified.
  • Windows/install: full native devkitPPC conversion, actual WUP installation/Menu launch/audio/gameplay/save/reload and GUI acceptance remain separate gates. CI tooling success does not close them.

docs.title: Continuing work
docs.text:
Implement the PICA/GX2 features, services, modules/audio and retail saves exercised by original reference scenes and the selected title. Measure real Wii U costs before promising performance. Complete the proven Windows conversion engine, then implement the specified GUI. Generic work can continue, but cannot replace actual game requirements or physical acceptance. The remaining-gates page is the handoff for pending resources.

Earlier implementation details, source audits and versioned receipts are preserved in development history. The verified cloud toolchain uses the existing checkout, SDK and /workspace/ctr2wup-tools/environment/activate.sh; no real keys, private console files or commercial data enter published artifacts.

docs.title: External development tools
docs.text:
The optional compiler-built homebrew workflow links original applications with unmodified devkitPro/libctru at 9b55eda44cf80b971503991e0c78f9bc8fe50425, https://github.com/devkitPro/libctru, using its zlib-style permission in README.md. The complete notice is preserved at docs/licenses/libctru.txt. Library source and devkitARM remain external dependencies; their source/tool binaries are not included in the source bundle. The optional compiled interactive RPX/WUHB embeds that original application's ARM executable, including linked libctru and GCC/newlib support. Keep the libctru notice and existing runtime license texts with that artifact. The ARM compiler used in this workflow is GCC 15.2.0; the GCC exception/GPL texts are the same license versions preserved below, not a claim that it is GCC 16.1.0 or that the ARM and PPC newlib builds are identical. ARM newlib's complete collected notices are also preserved as docs/licenses/COPYING.NEWLIB.ARM (devkitPro/newlib devkitPro license-reference commit 57bd8e1ade3cf46d2e61a72516ac8bfaf8fdfd62). The linked 3DSX CRT is devkitPro/devkitarm-crtls under MPL 2.0. Its unmodified 3dsx_crt0.s, 3dsx.ld and 3dsx.specs source from commit 1c0c10257c44bbb5a433453bb6bba91582825492 is included at docs/licenses/devkitarm-crtls/, with the full MPL text at docs/licenses/MPL-2.0.txt. The rebuilt .crt0 section bytes and relocations match the installed ARM SDK object; whole-object hashes differ. These sources accompany the covered startup code in the optional compiled guest. They are not project-authored code or linked into the native PPC platform as assembly. See the audit receipt at docs/licenses/devkitarm-crtls/README.md. CTR2WUP's license does not replace their MPL.

The separate CTR2WUP-CIA-Intake Windows x64 utility bundles Microsoft's .NET 10.0.12 runtime and apphost under MIT plus the preserved third-party notices from the exact restored runtime/host packages. Their LICENSE.TXT and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.TXT are identical for those packages and accompany the helper distribution as LICENSE-DOTNET.txt and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES-DOTNET.txt. Copies are also at docs/licenses/dotnet-runtime-*.txt. This limited console helper is original intake code, not the final GUI/injector; no SDK, user game or credential is bundled. Runtime source: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime, v10.0.12.

Encrypted packaging optionally calls the external Python package cryptography 50.0.0, https://github.com/pyca/cryptography. Its Apache-2.0 OR BSD-3-Clause license permits the BSD-3-Clause grant selected here; the full notice is preserved at docs/licenses/cryptography-LICENSE.BSD. No cryptography, OpenSSL, CFFI or other native dependency binary is bundled in these source/diagnostic archives. A future Windows dependency distribution must retain all applicable package and native dependency notices.

Rust, Cargo, GCC/devkitPPC, newlib, elf2rpl and optional SDK packages remain external toolchain dependencies. This notice does not assert that their licenses are identical to WUT's. Redistributing a complete host application or toolchain bundle requires a dependency-by-dependency notice and source audit. No ROM, commercial game assets, Nintendo SDK, donor title or credential is included with this project.

docs.title: CTR2WUP documentation
docs.text:
CTR2WUP is developing an UWUVCI-style Windows GUI that turns an owned 3DS game into an individual playable Wii U WUP. Current releases contain original homebrew diagnostics and developer tooling. Commercial games and the injector GUI are not supported yet.

The single HTML guide in development releases can be downloaded and opened directly in a browser, with offline search, navigation and printing. The source guides below also remain readable in GitHub. See documentation hosting for the free docs-only site and build receipts.

docs.title: Evidence and history
docs.text:
Compatibility describes supported boundaries. Console evidence separates supplied logs from verbal reports. Original fresh-launch save/results/assets are verified; the focused launch-audio regression remains open. Development history preserves earlier implementation notes and receipts; its old pending statements are historical.

No desktop pass, CI badge or RPX build establishes commercial gameplay, hardware performance or successful WUP installation. Keep ROMs, keys, saves, game traces and extracted commercial assets private.

Maintained source: docs/README.md · 1b14ea67cba6. GitHub source and issue links may require repository access.

docs.title: Architecture and implementation boundaries
docs.text:
The attached development brief is the project requirements. The repository was empty at the start of this implementation. See foundation-audit.md for pinned candidate source, measured builds, and licensing/PowerPC constraints.

The host CLI is Python 3.12; inspection/runtime tooling uses the standard library and encrypted packaging optionally uses cryptography. It uses the same argument-list subprocess interface on Windows and Linux. Container parsing, inspection, build reports, and package inspection are separate from execution. Executable artifacts are the original native diagnostic and controlled guest RPXs, plus the separate .NET CIA intake console utility cross-published for Windows x64. An RPX is not an installable WUP directory.

The CIA intake path uses bounded signature-layout/TMD/bitmap/content checks and selects index-0 application NCCH with checked absolute file offsets. Its derived CXI view preserves ExeFS/exheader code identity while explicitly removing RomFS and header signature. The standalone .NET helper validates stored hashes; the shared Python engine also validates BLZ/decompressed revision. This private view supports analysis through a 32 MiB attachment constraint, not game execution or asset staging. See cia-intake.md for supported profile and limitations.

The portable C core stores guest addresses as 32-bit integers and accesses bytes through checked mappings. Guest memory is explicitly little-endian on every host. The initial interpreter and direct generated-C backend are bounded CPU subsets with explicit unsupported exits. host/loader.py extracts inspected NCCH segments; the portable loader allocates checked permissions/stack/TLS/BSS. A single-guest runtime implements bounded SVC sleep/events/handles/ticks/debug/exit. Version 0.6.0 adds user read-only CP15 TLS access, typed/refcounted session handles, checked TLS IPC transport and restricted SRV/CFG startup commands. Its original ARM probe reads configured region/model/language through all three execution paths; see shared-services.md. This is shared runtime code, not a game patch. Version 0.7.0 adds owned heap/linear CPU allocation, atomic partial free/protection and queries; guest-memory.md defines the bounded contract. Ordinary heap changes preserve AOT snapshots; executable writes/aliases and execute protection still invalidate them. GPU/DSP physical memory remains pending. The original ARM fixture writes both framebuffers and responds to input through an explicit harness contract. Neither implements complete ARM11/VFP, a full 3DS kernel, general IPC or game HLE. The pinned external lifter now generates C through an original host driver. An original ABI 4 implementation statically executes that code using checked little-endian callbacks and per-instruction state; see upstream-integration.md. Its desktop runtime is not a Wii U dependency.

The native WUT backend provides independent TV and GamePad diagnostic output, input, sound, process lifecycle, timing, and CPU self-test instrumentation. v0.14.6 reserves a separate fixed-size 4 KiB result TXT independently of WHB trace handlers. Every update checks the reserved identity, writes, closes and reads back all bytes; named guide outcomes persist in the result even if the full trace fails. First errors are sticky; result-storage failure pauses guest input/execution, while full-trace failure is reported independently. Result writes happen at startup/self-tests/guest/checkpoint/guide/save/periodic/cleanup boundaries. Guest state is captured before close so cleanup cannot erase its final stats. Final result writes precede system transition.

The longer trace retains v0.14.5 fflush/fsync, checked close, mounted-volume flush and existing-file reopen. Handler registration is now checked. WUT owns the SD mount; the diagnostic releases its extra FSA client before transition. Neither exact read-back nor desktop abrupt-exit tests establish SD power-loss durability. The user reports successful v0.14.5 Native/Guarded/Compiled runs but no new logs; the uploaded text reports are older. Cause is unknown. See console-evidence.md.

v0.14.4 caches bounded nearest-neighbor coordinate maps and reuses scaled rows, with byte-order-independent RGBA output, checked source/output capacity and black borders/padding. The native backend flushes/invalidates the produced GX2 surfaces. The guide waits for a fresh decoded green frame after input before offering R, and records A-to-green delay separately from user visual confirmation. AOT execution returns a missing-block fault after 64 consecutive dispatches with no guest instruction progress, so empty/unwinding entries cannot consume unlimited host time without spending their budget. This guard cannot recover GPU/platform hangs and has not been attributed to the console freeze. Varied-clock live-input replay checks original compiled red/green transitions and exit on desktop. v0.14.3 polls ProcUI directly, suspends input/rendering outside foreground and releases guest/owned AX/GX2/report resources before ProcUIShutdown. On Minus it cleans up, clears stale graphics callbacks while retaining save acknowledgement, requests Menu and polls to EXITING; HBL relaunch follows cleanup/shutdown. WUT's devoptab owns SD mounting. Checked TXT records include lifecycle states and bounded input/guest/render checkpoints; end-of-report does not establish menu return. Native AX ownership is explicit; compiled apps do not use AX. The guarded AOT comparison uses a call limit of two instead of the standard 64, with the existing unwind/dispatcher. Exact desktop frames/input/exit match; depth, unwinds and frame-boundary stack headroom are diagnostic evidence, not proof of a console stack fault. See console-retest.md. All diagnostic builds also contain the original TLS/SRV/CFG startup self-test with a visible result and SD log. Unsupported cache operations fail visibly instead of inheriting the external emitter's no-op behavior. All builds also embed the original ARM heap lifecycle self-test and its SD log. Version 0.8.0 adds shared/mutex/semaphore objects and wait-any/all, with mapping/ wait ownership independent of handles. kernel-objects.md defines its single-thread scope. Its original ARM self-test is also embedded. Version 0.9.0 exposes standard read-only HID pad/touch rings and events. An independent original ARM consumer in each Wii U build reads live VPAD input through that service; hid-input.md defines its bounds and absent motion support. Version 0.10.0 adds checked direct GSP framebuffer submission and portable rotated RGBA8/BGR8/RGB565/RGB5A1/RGBA4 conversion. A separate original ARM guest reads HID, writes RGB565 and displays through this interface in all Wii U builds; see gsp-display.md. Version 0.11.0 adds one local GSP relay/shared framebuffer page, diagnostic VBlank and atomic queued presentation; see gsp-queues.md. The standard display guest uses this queue. Version 0.17 adds scoped synchronous GX commands; see gx-transfers.md. PICA rendering remains absent. Its guest mode presents completed ARM-written raw framebuffers through the same GX2 copying path. It is separate from PICA/GSP emulation; see guest-fixture.md. Version 0.12 adds checked user-mode ARM/Thumb multiple-register/stack transfers and BLX calls, with an embedded original nested-call self-test and independent ARM1176 reference checks; see cpu-stack.md. Compilation proves toolchain integration. Only physical console results can prove rendering, input, sound, guest semantics on PowerPC, or performance.

Version 0.13 adds eight single-core guest contexts with strict priorities, instruction quanta, CPU/TLS/raw VFP/FPSCR isolation and retained wait/stack ownership. Thread joins, owner-aware locks, address arbiters and local quota queries support normal compiled libctru threads/startup. BSS shares the final DATA page correctly; a read-only synthetic kernel configuration page supplies explicit HLE policy. See guest-threads.md for supported SVCs and limits. compiled-homebrew.md records normal devkitARM CRT/newlib/libctru applications, checked three-frame CPU display, standard input and a fourth interactive Wii U build. The v0.13 path left APT/FS startup requests visibly unavailable; v0.14 adds explicit standalone APT and platform-owned private FS volumes with checked archive/file sessions and snapshot commits. Guest filenames never address the host filesystem. The original compiled test proves save/read/fresh-process reload; see filesystem.md for supported commands and remaining commercial boundaries. It does not execute PICA or supply commercial compatibility.

v0.14.6 adds an explicit borrowed 64-bit read-only current-process Level-3 RomFS view. Checked FSFILE transport exposes bytes; unmodified libctru resolves nested and Unicode names/directories in guest code. Lifetime and read publication are checked, with no host path exposure. v0.16 adds canonical NCCH/IVFC verification and asset preparation; signature authentication and commercial asset integration remain open; see romfs-assets.md.

Save publication reserves .pending, moves a validated primary to absent .previous, publishes into the vacant primary name, then removes the backup. Failed publish attempts rollback; absent-primary load can recover a validated backup. Corruption and ambiguous siblings remain visible failures. This avoids requiring FSA rename replacement; it is not a concurrent-writer/power-loss guarantee.

A read-only shared time page at 1ff81000 uses two banks and a published sequence, explicit synthetic Unix-zero epoch, guest-clock progression and matching 268111856 Hz ticks. It is separate from kernel policy/TLS and counts as an additional 4 KiB backing allocation. ARM single-data byte/halfword/word accesses use checked little-endian U=1/A=0 unaligned semantics; other instruction classes stay strictly aligned. Defined lowest-base STM writeback is supported. Reference and generated original/external AOT checks are recorded in cpu-stack.md.

renderer/ contains bounded command inspection and small format/presentation references. Capturing PICA register writes does not execute a draw. An explicit exception reports the absent shader/texture/TEV/GX2 translation path.

packaging/ inspects original/supplied package structure and title identities. Content structure, cryptographic authenticity, and installer acceptance are different checks. There is no bundled common key and no unlicensed packer. Original stage-title metadata/artwork is a packaging prerequisite. Its output is explicitly not an installable package. Version 0.4.0 implements scoped encrypted FST/content/TMD/ticket construction with user-local inputs, and a separate streaming decrypting verifier. The original four-content profile has no authentic signatures and awaits installer/console acceptance. No key or certificate is bundled; offline proof uses temporary synthetic inputs only.

Generated artifacts are ignored by Git. User ROMs, saves, extracted assets, translated commercial code, keys, and packages must stay under ignored private directories. Synthetic fixtures are original instructions/data generated from source; no commercial assets are distributed.

docs.title: Execution gates
docs.text:
1. Native RPX compile and desktop tests can be completed in this environment.
  2. Physical RPX screen/input/audio/exit tests and PowerPC CPU results are pending.
  3. Checked loading and bounded guest-thread/kernel services now execute original compiled libctru CPU/input/framebuffer applications. Console stability, physical interface evidence and wider APT/FS/GX service semantics are needed.
  4. PICA rendering, required services/modules, filesystem/save/audio semantics, and exact-ROM revision profiles must precede a commercial conversion.
  5. License-cleared packing plus locally configured keys and actual install/menu launch tests must precede a WUP conversion claim.
  6. The Windows GUI follows a demonstrated execution pipeline; it is deferred.

The interpreter implements ARMv6 SXTB/SXTH/UXTB/UXTH register extensions, ROR

docs.title: 0/8/16/24, conditional execution and destination/source aliasing without flag
docs.text:
changes. PC operands and adding/paired forms remain unsupported. Unit/sanitizer checks and 2,048 Unicorn ARM1176 cases validate this scope. Full compiled libctru interpreter startup still stops on STRD, so no interpreter comparison is shipped. For the optional reference, install unicorn==2.1.4 in a developer Python environment, then run python3 tools/reference-extend.py --output NEW_DIRECTORY.

v0.15.0 adds input preparation ahead of container inspection. A bounded local key provider loads selected 16-byte file references in-process, with redacted failures/repr. Plaintext support-file imports create a separate explicitly private store. CIA AES-CBC main-content hashes are checked before inner NCCH decryption; NCCH v2 primary/secondary CTR, seed/key derivation and extents are checked before publishing a derived CXI. Output includes the main RomFS, but not other contents, tickets or key files. Input/output identities and lack of signature authentication are explicit; v0.16 verifies the full canonical IVFC tree when RomFS is present. Read-only sources, bounded chunks, input-change checks and atomic non-overwriting publication reuse the existing host boundaries. The validated decrypted CXI enters the unchanged loader/lifter pipeline; key values never reach generated C, runtime binaries or WUP staging. See encrypted-input.md for profiles and pending hardware/Windows checks.

v0.16 separates validated asset preparation from execution. The host verifies NCCH's anchored RomFS superblock, the complete canonical IVFC tree, every file hash and the bounded Level-3 directory/hash metadata. It atomically exports one Level-3 romfs.bin plus a manifest, never host paths derived from guest names. The file provider streams SHA-256 once at open, checks the configured expected hash and lends a read-only view to existing FS transport. It uses standard-C fseek/ftell, so the Wii U/32-bit limit is LONG_MAX, and requires immutable backing during execution. It owns no extra SD mount/client. Guest teardown releases mounts/references before provider close and system transition.

The portable texture decoder converts bounded base-level PICA tiles to explicit RGBA bytes without native guest-word loads. It preflights compressed blocks, lengths and aliases before publication. The Python/reference tools and emulated PPC checks establish decoder behavior, not GX2 upload/sampling or draw execution. See romfs-assets.md and renderer-status.md for the supported contracts.

v0.17.0 adds a standard client-0 GSP GX ring dispatcher and synchronous CPU-backed operations. DMA/fill/display conversion/raw copy stage source/outputs and validate all spans before command mutation; output cannot touch retained relay backing through any guest alias. Complete-range bulk memory APIs copy adjacent mappings, reject host/guest backing alias and update exclusive/code generations correctly. Successful commands advance and signal only enqueued completions; errors preserve the failing entry and later work while retaining an already committed prefix. PICA command lists, physical/VRAM translation and asynchronous GPU coherency are outside that contract. gx-transfers.md records accepted wire flags/dimensions.

GitHub now separates source-reviewed runtime evidence from hosted CI and physical testing. Managed milestone issue sections derive from checked-in status data; PR/check/artifact/release records never automatically close hardware acceptance. Repository instructions and agent profiles preserve the same boundaries.

Maintained source: docs/architecture.md · 1b14ea67cba6. GitHub source and issue links may require repository access.

docs.title: Batch CIA 3DS Decryptor investigation
docs.text: Reviewed October 12, 2026 for CTR2WUP 0.16.0. Its decryption methods can fit CTR2WUP's input-preparation stage. Retain the project's original checked engine; accept independently validated decrypted output as an additional input route. Decryption alone does not translate ARM, provide 3DS services, render PICA draws on GX2 or produce a playable Wii U WUP.

docs.title: Sources reviewed
docs.text:
Project Pinned source Finding matiffeder's original batch script af35b08a94f1662bd4ad23ccb35d2ab52f18712d MIT script; orchestrates external decrypt, ctrtool and makerom executables Redux 2fb1ac549a4006dd5261b8545e943527960ceeff Rewritten batch wrapper; bundled binaries/seed DB; no license file in reviewed tree Source-based ctrdecrypt fork 1763c5ebf04de24e8cdd672a391aae84dc45eef3 GPL-3.0; readable AES/container/seed implementation ctrdecrypt upstream a0d170c2153fe4054bd241ef4605ea64c1f3cc99 GPL-3.0 source, referenced by later batch packages rcyggdra rewrite 9984cd001bcd249af04d19eb9d015fd2ab742d76 MIT root label, but its two Rust decryption files match the GPL fork byte-for-byte

The original release thread is linked by the reviewed README; it was not used as executable provenance. Original decrypt.exe is opaque in the reviewed packages. Reading later Rust sources does not establish the exact behavior/source of those Windows binaries. Repository text and tree metadata were inspected; no bundled executable, seed/key database, downloader or actual game was downloaded or run. Source literals were redacted from the local audit excerpts. No external implementation or credential constant was incorporated into CTR2WUP.

docs.title: What the software actually does
docs.text:
The original script loops over CIA/3DS inputs. ctrtool inspects CIA title/content metadata, a separate decrypt engine produces decrypted NCCH partitions, and makerom rebuilds decrypted CIA or NCSD/CCI output. Base-game CIA conversion commonly ends in a .cci, not a CXI. .cci and .3ds can both contain NCSD; the magic/layout, rather than renaming, identifies the format. makerom's -ignoresign does not create authentic Nintendo signatures or a Wii U package.

The readable later engine uses CIA AES-CBC ticket/title-key/content decryption, NCCH AES-CTR section counters, hardware-style KeyX/KeyY derivation, primary versus secondary ExeFS keys, and optional SHA-256 title-seed checks/derivation. It includes shared platform/common-key constants; it does not require a unique personal console key for every ordinary retail title. Some input types still need a particular title key or seed. The exact required material depends on the dump.

That engine also tries Nintendo seed endpoints when a seed is missing locally, logs derived key-related data, and supports forms outside CTR2WUP's current base-title scope. Those behaviors have not been adopted. CTR2WUP's current route uses explicitly local file imports, redacted diagnostics and no automatic key/ seed download. The final GUI will expose local preparation using that same engine.

docs.title: Fit with CTR2WUP
docs.text:
Mechanism Current CTR2WUP position Decision CIA outer AES-CBC and ticket/title key Implemented with local file references and full TMD plaintext-content hash checks Keep existing original implementation NCCH section AES-CTR / mixed ExeFS keys Implemented for v2 and standard/1/0a/0b methods Same method; no need to launch the batch wrapper Seed DB / seed-derived KeyY Local import, seed verification and derivation implemented Keep local/private source; GUI import remains planned Decrypted NCSD/CCI output Accepted by magic; main NCCH preparation and asset checks available Useful optional handoff from a user-run decryptor Rebuilding a CIA/CCI with makerom Unnecessary for the injector's main executable/asset preparation Do not add a dependency just to repack the source Batch convenience Can inform eventual queued input/progress handling Use controlled engine jobs, structured results and isolated outputs Fixed-key or NCCH v0/v1, updates/DLC/system/DSi titles Unsupported in CTR2WUP's current preparation profile Separate implementation/evidence needed; no new compatibility claim Windows executables Not run in this Linux/cloud audit Native Windows/source-build/provenance tests remain pending

The original batch performs broad wildcard deletion of NCCH intermediates in its working directory. Redux documents non-ASCII filename limitations and cleanup of decrypted CIAs even when CCI conversion fails. These are concrete integration problems for a GUI that must preserve user inputs and support spaces/ Unicode. CTR2WUP already uses bounded parsing, isolated staging, immutable source checks and atomic non-overwriting publication.

docs.title: Reuse and licensing decision
docs.text:
The original MIT wrapper can be adapted with its notice, but adds little to the existing orchestration. Bundling decrypt.exe as an unexplained binary would leave source/provenance and behavior unresolved. Redux's reviewed tree does not supply a blanket redistribution grant for its wrapper and bundled dependencies. The readable Rust engine is GPL-3.0; use would require the applicable source/ license obligations and an explicit integration design. A fork's MIT badge is not evidence that inherited GPL code was relicensed: the reviewed main.rs and ctrutils.rs match the GPL fork's full SHA-256 hashes. This audit does not make a legal conclusion about the publisher; it records why that label is insufficient for choosing a dependency.

Recommended adaptation: keep CTR2WUP's original decryption/preparation code, use published crypto/layout facts as cross-checks, and validate a user's already prepared CIA/CCI/CXI through the same inspection/full-IVFC/revision path. A future source-built external backend is technically possible, but no integration need or licensing/provenance resolution is established by this audit.

docs.title: Verified handoff and remaining proof
docs.text:
An original synthetic decrypted .cci passed inspection -> prepare-rom -> full IVFC -> prepare-assets -> executable-only intake. The prepared blob matched its original bytes, the executable revision survived and the source stayed unchanged. This verifies the supported NCSD/CCI handoff, not execution of Batch Decryptor or its Windows binaries, and not an actual Mario dump.

A local handoff can use:

python -m host prepare-rom "MyGame-decrypted.cci" --output "private/prepared"
python -m host prepare-intake "private/prepared/game.cxi" --output "private/intake"
python -m host prepare-assets "private/prepared/game.cxi" --output "private/assets"

The standalone v0.5 Windows CIA helper expects CIA; a .cci is handled by the Python engine above, not by renaming it to CIA. When resources are available, the small private intake can be supplied without uploading keys or a full asset blob. Actual user-key exports, Mario input, Windows execution and console gameplay remain unverified. No further resource is needed from the user while away.

Audit receipts: artifacts/reports/assets-textures-v016/decryptor-audit/, including source pins, license/source comparisons and cci-interoperability.json. External source excerpts, binaries and key databases are excluded from delivery.

Maintained source: docs/batch-decryptor-audit.md · 1b14ea67cba6. GitHub source and issue links may require repository access.

docs.title: Build on Windows
docs.text:
Windows development tooling is verified. The finished injector GUI, native Wii U conversion and playable WUP output remain under development.

The hosted baseline passes Python fixtures and all 17 normal C suites on Windows Server 2022, including Unicode guest compilation/execution. Three filesystem/privilege-specific Python tests are explicitly skipped; their platform behavior remains unverified. The deep Windows run also passes real pinned external ARM/Thumb/VFP generation, 14 execution probes, runtime API checks, Unicode output and a .NET 10.0.401 WPF tooling build. The WPF probe verifies the SDK; it is not CTR2WUP's final application.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.12 or newer and Git.
  • MSYS2 UCRT64 with native GCC and Make for host-generated C and portable tests.
  • Official devkitPro Windows tooling with devkitPPC/WUT for Wii U RPX/WUHB builds.
  • Rust 1.95.0 for the optional audited external lifter.
  • .NET SDK 10.0.401 for the separate CIA intake helper and WPF tooling probe.

The Linux Docker SDK installer does not produce native Windows dependencies. Use the official Windows SDK route and preserve download/signature verification. Native gcc executes host fixtures; the PowerPC cross-compiler cannot run them. Keep the two compilers distinct in PATH.

docs.title: Source CLI and original fixtures
docs.text:
Run these commands from the repository root, using python or your local Python launcher. Install the declared crypto extras before exercising encrypted inputs:

python -m pip install '.[packaging,decryption]'
python -m host --help
make check-python PYTHON=python
make check-c-portable
python -m host make-fixture --output "artifacts/Windows fixture 日本語"
python -m host run-fixture "artifacts/Windows fixture 日本語/ctr2wup-guest.cxi" --output "artifacts/Windows frames 日本語"

Run Make commands in UCRT64 with native GCC available. make check-c-portable runs normal C suites; Linux ASan/UBSan results are separate evidence. Generated fixtures are original and require no ROM, console key or commercial asset. See encrypted inputs for private local key handling.

The Python wheel contains the CLI, translator and preparation modules. It does not bundle the SDK, GUI or native runtime/build recipes. Extract the matching source distribution for Wii U builds; CTR2WUP_PROJECT_ROOT can point an installed CLI to that distribution.

docs.title: Optional external generation
docs.text:
In PowerShell, use tools/install-translator-windows.ps1. It builds the audited source pin with Rust 1.95.0 and writes a provenance receipt. Then use the native GCC/Make environment:

python tools/validate-upstream.py --service-api --heap-api --kernel-api --hid-api --gsp-api --relay-api --fs-api --apt-api --thread-api --multiple-api --output artifacts/windows-upstream
python -m host run-fixture "artifacts/Windows fixture 日本語/ctr2wup-guest.cxi" --backend upstream --output "artifacts/Windows AOT frames 日本語"

The manual Windows development validation workflow reproduces these checks and the WPF SDK probe, preserving logs as Actions artifacts. Upstream integration records ABI, pin and notice limits. Optional Unicorn/Zakuro/reference comparisons require their own pinned tools; the Windows baseline is not evidence that those optional comparisons ran there.

docs.title: CIA intake helper
docs.text: The v0.5.0 CTR2WUP-CIA-Intake console utility has a separate self-contained Windows x64 bundle. It needs no Python/SDK/runtime installation and exports private analysis data. See CIA intake for controls, build pins and its user-machine acceptance check. It is separate from the planned injector GUI.

docs.title: Remaining Windows acceptance
docs.text:
Full native devkitPPC conversion, personal decrypted/keyed inputs, untested filesystem/privilege behavior, installer acceptance and the complete GUI need their own evidence. The end-to-end product must convert the selected title, install its WUP, launch from Wii U Menu and support gameplay/audio/save/reload. Original synthetic packing checks and development SDK probes do not close these gates. Follow milestones and GitHub development for the current record.

docs.title: Smallest local step on Windows
docs.text:
The separate CTR2WUP-CIA-Intake console utility is an engineering intake helper; it does not inject, install or run a game. The Windows x64 distribution includes its .NET runtime, licenses and third-party notices. It requires no Python, SDK, separately installed .NET, donor title or encryption key.

  1. Extract CTR2WUP-CIA-Intake-Windows-x64-0.5.0.zip into a folder.
  2. Drag your CIA onto CTR2WUP-CIA-Intake.exe. Alternatively, open the EXE and paste the CIA's local path when prompted.
  3. Upload the resulting CTR2WUP-intake.zip, found in the new <original CIA filename>.ctr2wup-intake folder beside the CIA.

The helper reads the original without modifying it and refuses existing outputs. It hashes the source and validates CIA bounds/bitmap/TMD groups/content digests, ticket-title agreement and executable NCCH/ExeFS stored hashes. It exports a derived executable-only CXI and a JSON receipt into an archive smaller than 32 MiB. It omits RomFS/plain/logo assets, the ticket, certificates and keys. ExeFS contains the private executable and may include game icon/banner material; keep this archive private. The derived header is unsigned and explicitly has no RomFS. It is an analysis view, not a complete or playable ROM.

If outer CIA or inner NCCH encryption is declared, the archive contains only the small report with the specific blocking layer. Do not infer encryption from .legit or any filename. A report-only export does not unlock executable analysis; fully decrypted executable data will then be required. No decryption or credential collection is performed. Malformed/unsupported files fail visibly. The executable view limit is 30 MiB; metadata allocations are bounded and content hashing is streamed. The full original file remains needed locally for later RomFS assets/module investigation and eventual conversion.

The helper's .NET logic passes original-fixture tests on Linux. Its Windows x64 self-contained EXE is cross-published; native Windows execution remains unverified. No user game byte or credential is included in the utility bundle.

docs.title: Shared Python engine
docs.text:
For developers with Python 3.12+:

python -m host inspect "private/game.cia"
python -m host prepare-intake "private/game.cia" --output "private/game-intake"
python -m host analyze-title "private/game-intake/executable-view.cxi" --lifter --output "private/game-analysis"

The engine supports standard 0x2020 type-0/version-0 CIA, SHA-256 signed-header layouts, version-1 TMD tables, sparse content bitmaps, exact ticket/TMD identity, and content-index-0 executable selection. Update/DLC/system titles are outside the first-title route. CIA metadata inspection can report declared encryption; full executable intake rejects encrypted content. TMD/section hashes establish integrity, not authentic signatures or support for the game.

The Python export performs BLZ/code-revision inspection and verifies the derived CXI preserves the original executable revision. The .NET exporter validates stored ExeFS bytes; cloud host intake performs the subsequent decompression, segment and revision checks. Both exporters produce identical derived CXI bytes for the original tested fixtures. Neither exports credentials or RomFS payloads.

docs.title: Reproduction and evidence
docs.text:
tests/test_cia.py covers 16 original cases: decrypted/sparse contents, both encryption layers, damaged hashes/bitmap/bounds, identity mismatch, missing executable, update refusal, output preservation and RomFS-free export. tools/validate-cia-helper.py executes 13 .NET cases, including a >32 MiB original RomFS placeholder and compressed code, and checks byte-for-byte agreement with the Python engine. No commercial test material is used.

Build the helper with .NET 10.0.401, using intermediate/output paths outside the source tree. Windows publishing is pinned to the .NET 10.0.12 runtime:

dotnet build tools/CiaIntake/CiaIntake.csproj -c Release -p:BaseIntermediateOutputPath=/absolute/artifacts/cia-obj/ -p:OutputPath=/absolute/artifacts/cia-linux/
python tools/validate-cia-helper.py --helper /absolute/artifacts/cia-linux/CTR2WUP-CIA-Intake.dll --output artifacts/cia-helper-report
dotnet publish tools/CiaIntake/CiaIntake.csproj -c Release -r win-x64 --self-contained true -p:PublishSingleFile=true -p:EnableCompressionInSingleFile=true -p:IncludeNativeLibrariesForSelfExtract=true -p:BaseIntermediateOutputPath=/absolute/artifacts/cia-win-obj/ -p:PublishDir=/absolute/artifacts/cia-windows/

The .NET Windows runtime is MIT with additional preserved third-party notices, copied from the exact restored runtime package. The helper archive includes LICENSE-DOTNET.txt and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES-DOTNET.txt; the SDK is not bundled. CIA layout facts were checked against the pinned lifter's src/rom.rs and documented container offsets. The reader/exporter code is original.

docs.title: Compiler-built homebrew evidence
docs.text:
The optional v0.14 developer workflow builds original C applications with the normal devkitARM 3DSX CRT/newlib and clean unmodified libctru source pinned at 9b55eda44cf80b971503991e0c78f9bc8fe50425. It does not replace __appInit, library startup, locks, threads or input functions with test stubs. The trusted original ELF segments are placed in an original synthetic NCCH for the existing checked loader; this is not a general ELF or 3DSX importer.

source /workspace/ctr2wup-tools/environment/activate.sh
bash tools/install-arm-fixtures.sh
python3 tools/validate-libctru.py --output artifacts/reports/libctru-local
python3 tools/validate-libctru.py --application interactive --wiiu \
  --output artifacts/reports/libctru-console
python3 tools/validate.py --compiled-homebrew

The source path defaults to ../ctr2wup-deps/libctru; use --libctru-source and --devkitarm elsewhere. The tool verifies a clean pin, builds a temporary library. install-arm-fixtures.sh extracts devkitARM from the same immutable official SDK image, verifies its compiler hash and checks out the clean library pin without replacing existing dependencies. CTR2WUP_SDK_ROOT and CTR2WUP_LIBCTRU_SOURCE can select other setup paths. The validator builds a temporary library, and preserves compiler logs, hashes, generated AOT and guest results under the requested new output directory. It also supports --sanitize, --cc-prefix, --run-prefix and emulated PPC Linux --static. Dependencies stay external. Console compilation stages generated sources under controlled relative paths so chosen output and checkout paths can contain spaces/Unicode; RPX/WUHB are checked before copying them to the requested location. A future native Windows toolchain setup needs its own validation.

The applications test:

  • boot: normal CRT/library startup, reaching main and orderly process exit.
  • threaded: real threadCreate/threadJoin/threadFree, LightLock, a 1,024-count shared result and initialized C __thread data isolated between contexts.
  • graphics: real libctru graphics/event thread, CPU-linear double buffers, checked cache flush, shared GSP queue and VBlank waits. Three full RGB565 frames must decode to green/red/green on top and blue below; six PPMs are preserved.
  • input: real hidScanInput, held/down/up edges, signed Circle Pad and touch coordinates, including release, through three standard shared-ring updates.
  • filesystem: normal savedata mount and newlib file I/O, Japanese UTF-16 path, delete, explicit commit, fresh-process reload and independently checked snapshot bytes. Corrupt snapshots are rejected and preserved. Its optional RPX/WUHB writes only an original private diagnostic save.

  • interactive: standard input drives three exact top-screen colors, bottom touch pixels at (17,23)/(319,239), release and the guest's own B-button exit. Its optional RPX/WUHB uses live VPAD input and the same checked AOT/GSP runtime.

  • romfs: ordinary root/nested/Unicode file reads, seek/EOF, directory listing, write denial and unmount through unmodified libctru's Level-3 parser. Its current-process view contains only original assets; see romfs-assets.md.

  • transfer: standard GX DMA, fill, tiled display transfer, raw texture copy and cache commands with checked pixels, padding and event waits; see GX transfers.

The default validator now runs all eight applications. The current console kit includes Native, interactive, guarded interactive, Save and RomFS variants. The RomFS guest also passes under ASan/UBSan and emulated big-endian PPC Linux; this does not establish physical Wii U execution.

All require a real guest PASS, ExitProcess and zero interpreter fallback. Pixel checks inspect every pixel, not only a debug message. Input tests use the public HID producer; no host writes a private application result or skips guest code. The interactive program includes a 1 ms sleep per frame to expose boundaries and avoid polling between presentation and the next input sample.

v0.14 explicitly enables standalone APT and mounts an empty read-only private virtual SDMC for these applications. Normal APT initialization, wakeup/event thread, Old-family model query, FS initialization/archive mount and APT exit now run successfully. The boot checks its active state and aptMainLoop. Use --application boot --trace-startup to capture every request. The remaining startup lookup failures are APT:S, APT:A and optional ptm:sysm. Privileged/system services and general applets are not supplied. See filesystem.md for exact state, ownership, persistence and limits. No NCCH/IVFC authentication or retail save integration, DSP/audio, CRO, PICA commands, GPU physical addresses or commercial compatibility is claimed. Native diagnostic tone remains platform audio; v0.14.5 interactive/guarded completion is user-reported. New independent result files, save updates, RomFS and native Windows acceptance remain pending. Do not enable a commercial profile from these homebrew passes.

The original source is under tests/homebrew. Optional locally generated guest images link external libctru/newlib/compiler support. The library's full license is preserved at licenses/libctru.txt; retain this and the existing runtime notices when distributing the compiled interactive artifact. The MPL 2.0 3DSX CRT's corresponding unmodified assembly/linker/spec sources, full license and section/relocation audit are supplied under licenses/devkitarm-crtls/. No ROM, game assets, keys, certificates or proprietary SDK is part of this workflow.

docs.title: Historical guarded 0.14.3 report
docs.text:
The uploaded report identifies compiled-guarded 0.14.3. Its complete shutdown and guide results match the user's first, delayed-green run. It does not capture the second launch that froze; the user confirms that launch saved no partial file.

Observation Recorded evidence Initial picture User confirmed PASS A input One press; held A reached the standard HID publication Button-response guide User marked FAIL; this remains a failure Guide completion Cancelled during touch step: 1 passed, 1 failed, 6 unfinished Embedded checks All nine returned PASS Post-input checkpoints 64 complete ordered frames, including two pixel-decode pairs Guest execution 6,029,629 instructions, no interpreter fallback or guest fault Display Five matched presentations; no reported device failure or dropped IRQ Host-frame timing Average 285,194 us, range 261,544–326,732 us; about 3.5 frames/s Guarded AOT Maximum call depth 2; 24 recorded unwinds Shutdown Resource cleanup, RELEASE_FOREGROUND, EXITING, ProcUI/WHB shutdown and main_return checkpoints

The user separately confirms launcher return. A main_return marker alone does not prove that the Wii U Menu finished loading. The log has three IPC request failures, so zero guest faults must not be described as zero service failures. Frame-boundary stack headroom is not a measurement at the deepest native call.

The long host-frame time supports investigating response delay. This version does not log decoded frame colors or A-to-green latency, so the exact delay and green-frame timing cannot be derived from these counters. Continued execution in this run cannot identify the cause of an intermittent failure on another run.

v0.14.5 adds checked file sync/close and mounted-volume sync before continuing past critical checkpoints. Desktop process-termination tests verify scoped recovery, and SDK builds verify the actual imports. SD controller durability, FSA behavior during a console freeze, and the original freeze remain unverified. That earlier retest request is superseded by the latest feedback and v0.14.6 save/result-file round above.
