docs.title: Physical Wii U test checklist
docs.text:
Current workflow: use the v0.14.6 kit and follow console-retest.md: Compiled Save, then the automatic Compiled RomFS test if exit works. The user reports Native/Guarded/Compiled completion without errors on 0.14.5, but no new TXT reports. Supplied text logs are older; the valid snapshot proves initial writing and the later save step failed. Independent result-*-0.14.6-*.txt files now retain named outcomes and are closed/ read-back verified. Upload them and the snapshot/siblings in this chat. No long native/input repetition is needed. The manual checklist below is historical reference for deeper acceptance rounds; guided-testing.md describes current controls and reporting.

No console is attached to this environment. Full physical acceptance remains open despite the scoped native results. Cross-compilation, host tests and RPX headers do not establish console behavior.

v0.14 adds CTR2WUP-libctru-filesystem-0.14.0.zip. Launch its WUHB/RPX with an accessible mounted SD card; the existing diagnostic creates its ctr2wup directory on the WUT-owned SD mount. A fresh diagnostic save must show/log CTR2WUP compiled filesystem SAVE 1 PASS and state=exited. Press Plus: it must reload, update and show RELOAD PASS. Exit with Minus and relaunch to test another fresh process. Preserve the private diagnostic snapshot and logs on failures; do not discard a corrupt snapshot or stale .pending / .previous files. Its path, atomic-publication limits and detailed procedure are in filesystem.md. The fifth build executes standard libctru/newlib savedata code, not a Mario save. Native SD exclusive-write/rename behavior and stability are unverified.

The v0.14 compiled interactive build also enables standalone APT startup/exit and an empty private virtual SDMC, with no host SD-card exposure. Boot tracing now records only privileged APT:S/APT:A and optional ptm:sysm lookup failures; all scoped APT/FS startup requests succeed. The v0.13 notes below describe that older artifact's unavailable APT/FS path. Use current bundles for new hardware evidence.

v0.13 adds GUEST THREAD SCHEDULER PASS CODE 0 in native mode and thread_selftest PASS result=0 in the SD log. Record its 345 instructions/eight switches, or the exact failure. This compares original interpreter/AOT contexts, per-thread TLS, owner-aware locks, waits and exit; no ROM is needed.

The separate CTR2WUP-libctru-interactive-0.13.0.zip supplies ctr2wup-libctru-interactive.rpx/.wuhb, a real original compiled libctru program. It starts in standard GSP display mode: top red, A held turns it green; bottom blue, a valid GamePad touch marks the corresponding white pixel. B is consumed by the ARM application itself and exits its graphics thread/process. Plus restarts; Y switches between its display and native diagnostics; Minus exits the host. Check all native self-test rows as well. This build has no custom ARM framebuffer mode and no guest PICA/audio/FS implementation.

Record CTR2WUP INTERACTIVE READY, increasing paired GSP swaps, zero fallback, touch corners/release, the guest CTR2WUP compiled interactive PASS and state=exited after B. Startup currently records eight failed IPC requests (six APT lookups, one FS lookup and one invalid session); preserve the IPC logs rather than interpret these as successful APT/FS initialization. Test ten-minute stability, repeated Plus restarts and clean host shutdown. Do not compare its diagnostic instruction budget with commercial performance or claim graphical-game compatibility from these frames.

docs.title: Artifacts and launch
docs.text:
Use artifacts/wiiu/ctr2wup-prototype.rpx with an RPX-capable homebrew launcher, or the .wuhb with a compatible Aroma environment. For Aroma, place the WUHB under sd:/wiiu/apps/ following that environment's homebrew application guidance. Record the precise homebrew environment, firmware and launcher versions used. These are diagnostic applications, not WUP installation directories. Do not attempt to install the RPX/WUHB through a WUP installer.

Current v0.14.0 delivery is CTR2WUP-diagnostic-0.14.0.zip; it contains the native RPX/WUHB, the instructions and direct/shared display reference PPMs. The separate original/external-guest bundles contain the other starting modes.

Version 0.2.0 also includes ctr2wup-guest-fixture.rpx/.wuhb, which starts in controlled guest mode. All current builds contain three modes; Y cycles native, custom-I/O ARM guest, standard HID/GSP ARM guest, then native. Use the native mode for the original checks below, then run the guest checks.

Version 0.3.0 also supplies ctr2wup-upstream-guest.rpx/.wuhb. Run the same guest checks with this build: it executes the actual external lifter's code through the checked portable ABI. The embedded CPU self-test remains the original bounded test; collect the guest instruction/frame/fault logs for this adapter. Neither the RPX/WUHB nor the separate title-staging ZIP is an installable WUP.

Version 0.6.0 embeds the original TLS/SRV/CFG startup probe in all three builds. In native mode, record TLS/SRV/CFG STARTUP PASS CODE 0 and the corresponding service_selftest PASS result=0 SD log, or the exact FAIL code. This compares an 89-instruction ARM service sequence in interpreter/original AOT, without a ROM. The separate external-AOT service probe has desktop/emulated PPC evidence only.

Version 0.7.0 embeds the original ARM heap lifecycle probe in all builds. Record GUEST HEAP LIFECYCLE PASS CODE 0 in native mode and heap_selftest PASS result=0 in the SD log, or the exact FAIL code. It compares 151 instructions across interpreter/original AOT: heap/linear CPU allocation, queries, protection, partial free/hole reuse and complete release. No ROM is required. GPU/DSP physical memory and commercial startup remain untested.

v0.8.0 embeds the shared-memory/synchronization probe. Record SHARED/SYNC LIFECYCLE PASS CODE 0 and kernel_selftest PASS result=0, or FAIL codes. Its 148 ARM instructions/27 SVCs check aliases, mutex/semaphore/event waits and ownership release. v0.13 separately embeds the multi-thread test below.

v0.9.0 adds HID ARM CONSUMER PASS CODE 0 / hid_selftest PASS result=0. Native GamePad rows show ARM-read HID buttons, packed signed Circle Pad XY, packed touch XY/validity and an increasing snapshot count. Compare these with the native VPAD rows while holding/releasing A/B/L/R/directions, moving the left stick and touching corners/center/borders. Touch release must clear position and validity; border touches must remain invalid. SD HID live logs must show waiting between samples, increasing snapshots, fallback0 and no fault; shutdown should report exited. Motion and C-stick are absent. Host Y/Plus/Minus controls are reserved for diagnostics. No commercial dump is needed for this test.

v0.10.0 adds HID/GSP RGB565 DISPLAY PASS CODE 0 and gsp_selftest PASS result=0. This compares an original ARM standard-HID/GSP graphics program through interpreter/original AOT, including rotated RGB565 pixels and cleanup. The external translator comparison is separate desktop/ emulated-PPC evidence, even in the external-guest RPX/WUHB build.

docs.title: Requested evidence
docs.text:
1. Launch and photograph both independent screens together. TV shows moving colored bands at logical 400×240; GamePad shows a distinct checkerboard at 320×240. Verify centered aspect-preserving borders on your actual outputs.
  2. Both sticks and held buttons update on the GamePad. Confirm VPAD errors are absent under normal input. Press A several times: a short 440 Hz tone should play from TV and GamePad, with the tone counter increasing.
  3. Touch the guest image's corners and center; the crosshair should match. Touch the black side borders: no guest touch should be accepted. The code calibrates using VPAD's selected 1280×720 coordinate space then maps into the queried GX2 surface dimensions; logs record both dimensions and viewport.
  4. CPU ARM/Thumb AOT self-test should show PASS, result0. It executes an original 40-instruction fixture in interpreter and generated paths and compares their registers, flags, little-endian data, and counts. Report FAIL codes exactly.
  5. X repeats the 64 KiB aligned allocation/write/read diagnostic. Leave it running for ten minutes and record hangs, frame-time changes, glitches and logs.
  6. Minus should return cleanly to the launcher/homebrew environment. Also test normal HOME/lifecycle handling supported by your environment. Record any failure to exit or audio continuing after exit.

The older v0.14.0 builds write sd:/ctr2wup/native-*.log; v0.14.1 uses named native-*.txt, compiled-interactive-*.txt, and compiled-save-*.txt reports. Optional WHB UDP logging uses port4405 (UDP_LOG=1 developer build); it is off by default in v0.14.2. SD TXT logging remains enabled. Supply the log and the two-screen photo, test duration and console environment. The log includes CPU outcome/timing, pointer bits, output surface dimensions, allocation, input/touch/tone events, frame timing and shutdown. These timings include CPU software image scaling and GPU copy/synchronization; they are not game timings.

docs.title: Controlled ARM guest checks
docs.text:
See guest-fixture.md for the contract and desktop reference images. No ROM is needed: this build embeds only the original generated ARM fixture.

  1. Enter guest mode with Y or launch the guest build. Confirm completed guest frame count increases; the TV background starts blue and GamePad starts teal. Record state/counters and any fault. Each guest frame needs multiple display iterations because execution is limited to 50,000 instructions per iteration.
  2. Hold A through the next complete guest frame: the top changes to green. Hold touch inside the bottom viewport: the next bottom frame changes to purple and draws a white guest pixel at the touch position. Check corners and center; touches in black borders must not enter guest input. Record latency.
  3. Press B: the guest should show exited after completing its current frame; the host remains responsive. Plus restarts it and its frame counter. Y cycles into the standard HID/GSP mode and then native diagnostics. Minus exits the entire application.
  4. Leave guest mode running for ten minutes. Collect both-screen images and SD logs with guest_open, debug/SVC events, increasing frames/instructions, fallback0 and no faults. Include your test duration and firmware/launcher.

Guest pixels are ARM-generated; the status overlay is host-generated. Success would establish this controlled fixture's PowerPC/input/presentation behavior, not stock 3DS graphics, PICA/HID/GSP or commercial compatibility.

v0.11.0 also adds GSP QUEUE/VBLANK PASS CODE 0 and gsp_relay_selftest PASS result=0, checking mapped queues, delayed presentation, IRQ delivery and cleanup through the original interpreter/AOT paths.

v0.12.0 adds ARM/THUMB STACK CALLS PASS CODE 0 and stack_selftest PASS result=0, checking 47 original instructions, nested ARM/Thumb calls, stack/register restoration and cleanup. Include that line in your SD log and native-screen results. This is original interpreter/AOT console evidence; external and Unicorn results remain separate developer checks.

docs.title: Standard HID/GSP queued guest checks (0.11.0)
docs.text:
1. Cycle Y until CTR2WUP HID / GSP QUEUE / VBLANK is shown. Completed frame count must increase without faults or fallback. This guest reads HID shared memory/events and submits both RGB565 screens through the GSP shared queue, then waits for VBlank and drains IRQs.
  2. Top should be blue, or green while holding A. Check the corner markers: white top-left, red top-right, green bottom-left, blue bottom-right. The host status overlay is in the middle so every corner remains visible.
  3. Bottom should be cyan; valid touch changes it to magenta with a white pixel at the guest touch coordinate. Check center/corners and border rejection. Release must restore cyan. ARM fills run over several bounded host slices, so record visible latency rather than assuming one display-frame response.
  4. B exits this guest; Plus restarts both graphics guests. Cycle all three modes, leave the GSP mode running for ten minutes and test Minus/HOME lifecycle. Return both-screen photos and SD gsp_selftest, gsp_relay_selftest, GSP relay, GSP guest, gsp_guest_shutdown logs, duration and firmware/launcher environment.

Compare with shared-display-reference/frame-{1,2}-{top,bottom}.ppm in the native diagnostic bundle: frame1 holds A/touch at 100,80, frame2 releases both. These reference images have no host status overlay. Success establishes the scoped CPU/shared framebuffer bridge and relay on the diagnostic clock. It does not establish stock libctru initialization, real 3DS timing or PICA. Check registered=1 while running, increasing VBlank and swap counters, no device faults or dropped IRQs, and registered=0/clean exit after B. Record coalesced intervals and input latency; slow CPU fills can legitimately coalesce host ticks.

docs.title: Packaging prerequisite checks
docs.text:
Version 0.4.0 supplies an experimental original encrypted writer, not a packaged installable diagnostic. Its offline proof uses synthetic key/certificates and deletes that temporary package. Use the local-input contract in packaging.md only after establishing your own inputs and console/installer environment. Never try to install the synthetic test fixture.

A separately generated original homebrew package needs recorded installer acceptance, Wii U Menu icon/boot artwork, launch into both screens, input/audio, clean exit and removal. Record the title ID and installed-title inventory; confirm no existing title was replaced. FST/ownership/COS metadata and the nonhashed content/ticket policy may need corrections from those results. No console installation, replacement or removal is automated by these tools.

docs.title: ARM/Thumb stack and register transfers (0.14.6)
docs.text:
The shared CPU runtime now executes ordinary function stack frames and transfers of multiple registers. This is ROM-independent work toward M2/M3/P3; it does not enable a commercial profile or the GUI Inject-to-WUP pipeline. Guest threading is implemented separately in guest-threads.md.

Supported instructions:

  • User-mode ARM LDM/STM in IA, IB, DA and DB addressing modes, with checked optional base writeback and ascending register/address order.
  • ARM LDM of PC, including stack returns, with ARM/Thumb interworking.
  • Thumb16 PUSH/POP of low registers and optional LR/PC; POP PC interworks.
  • Thumb16 LDMIA/STMIA. LDM with its base in the list suppresses writeback; STM with its base in the list is supported only when the base is first.
  • Register BLX calls in the bounded original translator, matching existing interpreter support. The target is captured before LR changes, including BLX LR, and Thumb callers receive an odd return address.

The interpreter decodes these forms into a checked word-transfer helper. Original AOT emits constant decoded parameters and never calls the interpreter. Condition skips preserve registers/memory while consuming one instruction. Transfers preserve flags except the execution-state bit on a loaded-PC return. Address arithmetic wraps at 32 bits; every word still enforces mapping, alignment and read/write permissions. No guest address becomes a host pointer.

An access fault keeps the faulting instruction PC and the original base; earlier successful register loads or memory stores remain visible. These CPU operations are not atomic service publications. The external emitter writes an ARM LDM base early; the checked ABI captures and restores that base on a memory fault. It clears that abort bookkeeping at subsequent instruction/execution boundaries. CPU logs contain the failed address/opcode; guest fault detail retains the PC.

v0.13 supports ARM STM's PC source as PC+8, checked independently against ARM1176. Empty lists, PC as base, Thumb stores of PC, user register banks/SPSR returns and ARM loads with writeback and base-in-list, or stores with a lower listed register, are rejected before effects. v0.14.6 permits the defined ARM STM writeback form when its base is the lowest listed register: it stores the original base then writes back, including GCC __aeabi_ldivmod stack entry. Thumb STM with a non-first base and BLX PC are rejected. The external instruction guard rejects the same empty/unpredictable transfer forms, including empty Thumb operations that the emitter otherwise turns into successful no-ops. This is an explicit safe subset, not a claim to implement every ARM11 abort/unpredictable behavior. Thumb long-immediate calls and broader ARM/VFP/privileged behavior remain open.

The original checked NCCH (host/stack_fixture.py) calls an ARM function, then a Thumb function that calls ARM again. It saves/restores register frames, stores and reloads register groups, skips one conditional transfer from an unmapped base, returns to ARM, checks a restored stack and exits. Its 47 instructions and one SVC produce independent golden data, with zero fallback and matching CPU/ mapped bytes across interpreter, original AOT and the real external lifter at uneven budgets. Separate external cases compare six partial-word fault paths and reject six empty/unpredictable Thumb forms without effects.

make -C tests/multiple check sanitize checks golden modes, interworking, partial word faults, permission/alignment failures, unsupported forms, wrapped addresses and the interpreter/original-AOT nested call self-test. python3 tools/validate-upstream.py --multiple-api --output artifacts/my-stack runs eleven external probes plus this API (24 checks).

tools/reference-multiple.py --output artifacts/my-reference independently compares 944 instruction cases through interpreter and original AOT with pinned Unicorn 2.1.4 configured as ARM1176. It checks all registers, CPSR and all 4096 data bytes, then verifies the nested program's 47-instruction trace, golden output and restored stack. Unicorn and a native GCC/shared-library toolchain are optional developer requirements; production has no Unicorn dependency. In the managed environment, set PYTHONPATH=/workspace/ctr2wup-tools/reference-python for this optional tool. The reference report is artifacts/reports/console-results-v0146/arm1176-data-validated/report.json. The reference uses ARM1176 SCTLR U=1/A=0. Checked bytewise unaligned halfword/word single-data accesses are supported across fully validated ranges; failed ranges produce no partial stores. Instruction fetch, multiple-register, exclusive and FP accesses retain strict alignment. The checked external ABI selects this policy per instruction; raw span shortcuts remain disabled. Preindexed ARM register-offset halfword forms used by unmodified romfsUnmount are supported. This is a fixed userspace policy, not a privileged SCTLR implementation.

All Wii U builds embed ARM/THUMB STACK CALLS and stack_selftest. Compilation, reference checks and emulated PPC prove only the stated checks. Workload speed, full physical PowerPC acceptance, commercial startup and the user's selected Mario revision remain unverified. Scoped normal compiled homebrew has separate desktop/sanitizer/emulated-PPC evidence.

Maintained source: docs/cpu-stack.md · 1b14ea67cba6. GitHub source and issue links may require repository access.

docs.title: Portable CPU and AOT evidence
docs.text:
This is original C11 code, independent of desktop threads, a flat 4 GiB host reservation, SIMD, or host byte order. Addresses remain guest uint32_t values. Mapped read/write/execute permissions, end-of-address-space overflow, alignment, aliasing, capacity and overlap faults are explicit. Writes invalidate code snapshots through executable aliases. The exclusive model supports one deterministically scheduled guest CPU, and invalidates its monitor on writes; it is not a multicore ARM memory-model implementation.

Interpreter subset: ARM conditions, data-processing ALU/shifts/flags, branch and link/exchange, MUL/MLA, immediate/shifted-register byte/word transfers, unsigned immediate preindexed LDRH/STRH without writeback (v0.10), word LDREX/STREX, user read-only CP15 TLS MRC (Rd other than PC) and observable SVC exits; Thumb16 shifts/ALU, high-register operations, branch/exchange, selected loads/stores/SP-relative operations and SVC exits. Version 0.12 adds checked user-mode ARM LDM/STM, Thumb16 PUSH/POP/LDMIA/STMIA and original-AOT register BLX calls; see cpu-stack.md for scope and reference evidence. Unaligned transfers fault deliberately. Exception-return/general VFP arithmetic, Thumb long calls, ARM user-bank/exception-return multiple forms, other halfword transfers and privileged instructions are unsupported. The supported subset is research code, not a complete ARM11.

translator/aot.py specializes a smaller flat-executable subset into direct C instruction blocks. It fails with guest PC/opcode context for unsupported code. Version 0.11.0 also specializes word LDREX/STREX directly, with the same bounded monitor/generation/fault behavior as the interpreter. The queued GSP probe checks successful updates and a device publication forcing retry across execution paths. Each block is instruction-budgeted. The dispatcher keys address plus ARM/Thumb state, records missing blocks with module hash and PC, and permits explicit interpreter fallback. Invalidated code cannot execute a stale translated block. The dispatcher binary-searches strictly increasing block-address tables and retains linear lookup for unsorted or duplicate-address tables.

make -C tests/cpu check sanitize exercises explicit golden values, randomized integer carry/overflow against widened arithmetic, permissions/faults/aliases, exclusive monitoring, branching, condition skips, SVC state/logging, budget, fallback and invalidation. ASan/UBSan are enabled for a separate run. Python tests verify generator reproducibility and rejection behavior. The original translator also specializes this TLS read. v0.6.0's separate 89-instruction original startup probe matches interpreter/original/external AOT state and memory through actual SRV/CFG SVCs; see shared-services.md. v0.13 adds user CP15 ARMv6 DMB/DSB ordering, UADD8/USUB8/SEL with GE flags, SMLAxy with signed halfwords and sticky Q, FPSCR transport and checked scalar VLDR/VSTR word transport. See guest-threads.md. Other CP15/cache operations remain unsupported, including emitter no-ops. General interpreter VFP arithmetic remains absent; external arithmetic rejects unsupported controls. v0.7.0's 151-instruction heap lifecycle probe executes allocation, permissions, partial free and queries through all three backends with zero fallback. Data mapping changes preserve AOT; executable mapping/protection and alias writes still invalidate it. Protected/unmapped stores preserve the exact fault PC across backends; see guest-memory.md.

The original fixture has ten ARM and three Thumb instructions. A loop computes 10, stores/reloads it through guest memory, branches to Thumb, computes 8 and exits on SVC127. Interpreter and generated execution take 40 guest instructions, and compare registers, flags, memory and instruction counts. Both paths are linked into the RPX; it logs the result on actual console launch.

The separate 85-instruction NCCH guest exercises a checked executable loader, SVC handling, long ARM framebuffer loops, input and orderly process exit. It matches interpreter/AOT registers, flags and full data/BSS memory after two frames. See guest-fixture.md; this adds single-guest sleep/event scheduling, not full kernel/service emulation. v0.13 separately adds bounded single-core multi-thread scheduling and conventional compiled libctru evidence.

Desktop timing is reported separately from console results. Its combined tiny self-test time includes setup/interpreter/generated execution and cannot predict game performance. Actual PowerPC correctness/timings, VFP/reference differential testing, interrupt/wait scheduling, complete exclusive behavior and broader arithmetic/memory/branch/VFP/dispatch/fallback benchmarks are outstanding.

translator.upstream adds validated-container, pinned-source external analysis using the audited lifter. It does not use its native-endian desktop ABI as a PowerPC backend and does not distribute that tool or its incomplete notices.

Maintained source: docs/cpu-subset.md · 1b14ea67cba6. GitHub source and issue links may require repository access.

docs.title: Remaining acceptance gates (0.20.0)
docs.text:
The product remains a Windows GUI that converts owned 3DS games into individual Wii U WUP titles. Current diagnostics do not provide commercial gameplay. Approximately 20% implementation and 0/7 accepted full gates remain the assessment.

Reviewed physical reports establish original fresh-launch saves, named TXT collection, embedded/SD assets and GX transfer/configuration; pictures and Minus return have user confirmation. Evidence preserves older failures separately. No repeat Save/RomFS round is requested.

Current external requirements:

  1. Launch-audio regression: run only Audio Check and GX Transfers 0.20.0. Return their new TXT results and a note on music/Minus return.
  2. Platform acceptance: record exact firmware/Aroma/installer versions and complete native recovery/Home/APT and installed-original-WUP checks.
  3. Mario input: privately prepare the exact owned revision with local decryption or an already decrypted dump, then supply the small executable intake. Actual assets and exercised CPU/services/PICA/audio requirements remain unknown. Keys stay local.
  4. Renderer/runtime: implement actual PICA/GX2 draws, shaders, modules, guest audio and retail save behavior, then measure physical scenes/gameplay.
  5. Conversion/GUI: prove the full native Windows conversion and WUP install/rebuild/save continuity, then complete the planned GUI acceptance.

Independent development can continue. It cannot replace title bytes, physical console observations or full Windows/install acceptance. Project #2 is populated through the repository Actions secret; public docs/dashboard deployment has its own operation receipts and must be verified before being called live.

docs.title: Next actions
docs.text:

Upload their new result-*-0.14.6-*.txt, any full traces, and the snapshot/siblings as described in console-retest.md. No long native/input repeat is needed. Reviewed Windows CI and validation workflows are included and authorized for publication; their actual hosted results must establish Windows acceptance.

docs.title: CTR2WUP status
docs.text:
Updated October 12, 2026 (America/New_York); report filenames use UTC. Requirements: docs/project-brief.md; product plan: docs/development-plan.md; GUI workflow: docs/gui-workflow.md. The user resumed implementation and selected Super Mario 3D Land as the first title candidate. The target remains an UWUVCI-style Windows GUI: select a game (decrypted or locally prepared with imported 3DS material), configure title/artwork, click Inject, install its per-game WUP and launch from Wii U Menu. The CLI is the shared engine, not the final product.

Overall implementation estimate: approximately 20%, reassessed against the v0.16.0 GUI-to-playable-WUP target on October 12, 2026. This is a rough engineering judgment, not measured task completion. 0/7 full milestones are accepted. See the completion assessment for its basis, remaining work, and external testing gates; the README provides a concise progress overview.

Version 0.16.0 advances asset preparation and texture decoding while the user is away. These are shared foundations for the GUI's future injection/runtime pipeline. No commercial profile, PICA draw renderer, Mario build or installed WUP is enabled. The earlier verbal console successes remain usable reported evidence; no new physical run is claimed. No ROM or key upload is requested now.

  • Full RomFS preparation: canonical NCCH IVFC header/master anchoring and every hash/data block are verified, including final padding. Bounded Level-3 metadata validates Unicode names, hash/parent/sibling chains, duplicates, cycles/orphans and file extents. prepare-rom now applies this when RomFS is present; prepare-assets exports a private romfs.bin and manifest containing source/code identity and file/blob hashes. Publication refuses replacement and preserves the source. Virtual filenames never address host extraction paths. Integrity is distinct from signature authenticity; unsupported layouts fail.
  • File-backed runtime assets: original portable SHA-256 and immutable file provider require the configured blob hash before mounting into existing read-only guest FS transport. Guest paths remain virtual. Live views/handles block close; teardown closes guest ownership before the file. The standard-C provider is limited to LONG_MAX (2 GiB minus one on 32-bit Wii U) and checks integrity at open, assuming immutable backing. Console I/O cost is unmeasured.
  • Texture foundation: original C/Python decoding of all 14 base formats, 8×8 Morton tiles, packed channels, luminance/alpha, RG8/HILO, ETC1/ETC1A4. Base dimensions are powers of two in 8..1024. Byte order is explicit; buffers, aliases and invalid compressed differential blocks are preflighted before output changes. Sampling/mips/cache/GX2 upload/draws remain unfinished.

Validation is preserved under artifacts/reports/assets-textures-v016/:

  • Required make check: 206 Python tests, including 16 new RomFS and six texture cases, plus sixteen C suites normally and with ASan/UBSan. New provider/SHA suite: 3,467 assertions; texture suite: 7,959 checks.
  • New C suites pass Clang normal/sanitizer and emulated big-endian PPC checks. The texture matrix compares 42 original images byte-for-byte with Python; 39 also match pinned external Zakuro. HILO is explicitly excluded because CTR2WUP follows Azahar's RG8 convention. The emulated PPC matrix has identical source/output hashes to all 42 host vectors. No external emulator code is linked or included in runtime/delivery.
  • The sanitizer-compiled original normal-CRT/libctru program reads identical RAM/file-backed assets, exits after 49,550 instructions with zero fallback, and rejects a corrupt blob before execution while preserving it. Three intentionally unavailable startup IPC requests remain recorded; a PASS does not claim all services are implemented.
  • The original encrypted CIA -> local ROM preparation -> complete IVFC -> private asset blob -> actual compiled guest read pipeline passes with unchanged source, original asset bytes and transient synthetic keys. No game patch or commercial content is involved.
  • Required make prototype and the optional Asset Files RPX/WUHB cross-build carry v0.16.0. The installed wheel verifies preparation/assets/texture imports outside the checkout with Unicode/space paths. Windows execution is pending.

Delivery: artifacts/delivery/assets-textures-0.16.0/, with source, wheel, Native/Asset Files RPX/WUHB, original SD blob, guides and checksum/report manifest. The Asset Files diagnostic uses sd:/ctr2wup/romfs-test.bin and the existing short guided TXT report flow. Its console run is pending. When available, return result-compiled-romfs-file-0.16.0-*.txt and any full trace together in a ZIP. The earlier v0.14.6 Save/RomFS round remains pending; no completed long input round must be repeated for this host/runtime increment.

The requested Batch CIA 3DS Decryptor investigation is recorded in docs/batch-decryptor-audit.md. Its published AES/seed methods fit the existing preparation engine; original decrypted CCI -> full verification/assets/intake passes with unchanged revision/source. Original MIT script, unlicensed Redux wrapper tree and GPL readable engine have distinct grants. A MIT-labelled fork contains byte-identical GPL-upstream decryption files, so it is not adopted on that label. No Windows binary/key database/network seed fetching is incorporated. The development plan retains the original local-key backend and validated external-output handoff; actual tool/game/Windows acceptance remains pending.

This advances M3/M4/M6 foundations. Approximately 20% implementation; 0/7 full milestone gates accepted. Actual Mario executable/assets and required services, PICA scenes, guest audio/retail saves, Wii U SD/timings/install acceptance and native Windows/GUI remain the main unfinished work. See docs/romfs-assets.md and docs/renderer-status.md for precise limits.

Previous version 0.15.0 added local encrypted-input preparation and key/seed import. The user expands the final GUI's scope to accept decrypted dumps or encrypted dumps using material obtained from their own 3DS. This amends the original brief's decrypted-only input scope without altering that historical document. The PC side now supplies prepare-rom and import-rom-keys; the GUI import wizard, protected Windows storage and device extraction/helper remain planned. No console key, bootrom or Nintendo key database is bundled or used.

The host decrypts supported CIA outer main content with a local title key or common key/ticket, verifies its full TMD plaintext hash, then prepares supported NCCH v2 exheader/ExeFS/RomFS bytes. Standard/1/0a/0b crypto methods, unseeded primary versus secondary keys, seed verification/derivation, mixed ExeFS keys and unaligned bounded CTR chunks are supported. Existing checked hashes/code inspection precede non-overwriting atomic publication. game.cxi preserves main RomFS bytes; auxiliary contents, tickets and key files are not exported with it. That release did not verify full IVFC; v0.16.0 adds canonical full-tree verification. Authentic signatures and commercial compatibility remain unverified.

Plaintext AES-key database NCCH retail KeyX records, seeddb and explicitly declared decrypted title-key DB records can be imported into an explicitly private local store. Field/range/count/duplicate checks and redacted errors/repr are tested. Wrong/missing keys or seeds and unsupported forms fail; input and existing output remain unchanged. Fixed-key/v1 NCCH, encrypted key databases, boot9/aes_keys.txt import, raw SD/NAND, updates/DLC and ticket depersonalization remain unsupported. A personalized ticket needs a previously recovered local title key. Actual user-console exports and native Windows behavior are pending. See encrypted-input.md.

The user is again away from desktop/Wii U and authorizes continuing independent milestones with earlier verbal confirmations. Their U.S. console, latest firmware, latest Aroma and latest WUP Installer GX2 are recorded as reported; exact build numbers are unknown. Earlier v0.14.5 Native/Guarded/Compiled successes remain positive user evidence. No new physical execution or installation is claimed. The private receipt is private/console-environment-20261012.json. The existing v0.14.6 five-app kit remains the pending Save/RomFS result round; this release does not require repeating the completed long input guides.

Verification is under artifacts/reports/rom-preparation-v015/ and artifacts/reports/rom-preparation-workflow-v015/:

  • 184 Python tests (29 new key/preparation cases) and all fourteen existing C suites pass normally and with ASan/UBSan. No test is skipped in this environment. Known NIST CBC/CTR vectors, a separate bit/carry scrambler implementation, all four NCCH methods/seed routes, both CIA layers, mixed ExeFS/padding, compressed code, >1 MiB streaming, import formats, malformed/wrong data and publication races are exercised. No real key or commercial byte is used.
  • The original doubly encrypted execution fixture completes prepare → validate/ small intake → actual external AOT → desktop guest execution → Wii U RPX/WUHB. Its prepared bytes match the original fixture, executable revision survives intake, two frames complete, guest exits after 1,382,494 instructions with zero fallback, and source remains unchanged. Synthetic key files are transient/private and removed.
  • Required make check and make prototype complete. Make object dependencies now include the recipe so version/build-recipe changes cannot silently retain old compiled app identities. Fresh native/external-fixture builds carry 0.15.0.
  • The pure-Python wheel and matching source/development artifacts are under artifacts/delivery/rom-preparation-0.15.0/; no real private receipt/key is included. Installed-wheel local preparation is checked outside the checkout.

This advances P2 input preparation and P4/M6 engine foundations. Mario's actual executable/assets, commercial HLE/PICA/audio/retail-save work, verified WUP installation and native Windows/GUI acceptance still need implementation/evidence. Approximately 20% overall implementation; 0/7 full milestone gates accepted.

Version 0.14.6 reviews the latest evidence and advances shared RomFS support. The user reports Native, Guarded and Compiled completed without errors on 0.14.5, but no new TXT reports were found and Save failed. These observations are recorded separately from the supplied text headers, which identify 0.14.0–0.14.3. The six originals and SHA-256 receipt remain under ignored private/console-followup-20261011/; none is bundled/published. The 88-byte snapshot is CRC-valid with both expected visit-1 records. It proves initial persistence, not a successful later update or reload. A private desktop copy now reloads and advances both records to visits 2 and 3 with zero fallback while the original stays unchanged. See docs/console-evidence.md.

A separate fixed-size result-<app>-0.14.6-<session>-<suffix>.txt now bypasses the full trace handler. Exclusive launch identity, checked write/flush/close and exact 4 KiB read-back precede RESULT VERIFIED. Named guide outcomes/evidence, self-tests, guest state/PC/fault/fallback, save status/errno, green latency and full-trace errors are retained independently. Missing/replaced files fail visibly without recreation; first errors pause guest execution. Handler registration is checked. Guest statistics are captured before cleanup, and result writes finish before system transition. Existing trace sync/close/volume commits and WUT mount ownership remain. Read-back is not a physical power-loss durability guarantee. The exact cause of the missing v0.14.5 logs is unknown.

Save publication no longer depends on rename replacing a destination: it stages exclusively, validates/moves the old primary to .previous, publishes into the vacant primary, and removes the backup after success. Failed publication attempts rollback; missing-primary load can recover validated .previous. Corrupt primary, stale .pending and ambiguous backup fail visibly and remain preserved. Tests model no-overwrite rename, repeat updates, rollback failure and abrupt interruption. This corrects an identified WUT/FSA assumption; it is not a confirmed diagnosis of the user's exact console save failure. The guest names its failing phase. See docs/filesystem.md.

New current-process read-only Level-3 RomFS transport advances M3 without a ROM/game patch. An original ordinary devkitARM/libctru/newlib application reads root/nested/Unicode assets, seeks/checks EOF, lists directories and rejects writes. Library parsing runs unchanged in guest code. Provider lifetimes, copied file handles, whole-buffer bounds/permissions, IPC aliases, >4 GiB length/offsets and failed-read atomicity are checked. Signature authentication, commercial asset integration, encrypted cartridge access and commercial asset integration remain unfinished.

That actual program required a synthetic read-only shared time page, defined lowest-base ARM STM writeback and ARMv6 U=1/A=0 unaligned single-data access. These are shared implementations with strict alignment retained for fetch/multiple/ exclusive/FP operations, not library patches. The time epoch is explicitly synthetic; no actual RTC/timezone accuracy is claimed. See docs/romfs-assets.md, docs/cpu-stack.md and docs/guest-memory.md.

v0.14.6 verification is under artifacts/reports/console-results-v0146/:

  • Required make check: 155 Python tests and fourteen C suites, normal and ASan/UBSan. Each mode includes 51,796 CPU, 1,892 filesystem, 574 report/guide, 200 multiple-transfer and 19 no-progress-guard assertions. Required make prototype and the fresh native builder complete successfully.
  • upstream-final/report.json: fourteen external AOT probes, 28 checks, all compile/run successfully; real faults, alias invalidation and bounded resume remain tested. arm1176-data-validated/report.json: 944 independent Unicorn ARM1176 cases plus the original 47-instruction nested ARM/Thumb program.
  • interactive-final/report.json: exact guest frames, guarded depth-2 comparison and eight live-input timing replays pass. filesystem-final/report.json: initial/fresh-process save/reload passes; corrupted snapshot rejection exits with expected status 5, preserving bytes.
  • romfs-complete/report.json and romfs-sanitized/report.json: the new original guest passes and exits after 49,550 instructions, zero fallback, with three unavailable optional/privileged startup requests still reported. The same program passes QEMU emulated big-endian PPC Linux in romfs-powerpc/.
  • final-source-builds.json: all four compiled variants rebuilt from recorded current source; native rebuilt separately. Packaged RPX/WUHB headers, hashes, ZIP CRC and source bytes are checked. Earlier failed diagnostic logs are preserved; only the completed final runs support these claims.

Delivery: artifacts/delivery/console-results-0.14.6/, containing the five-app console testing kit, matching source ZIP, notices, build receipts and hashes. The current kit includes Native, Compiled AOT, Guarded AOT, Save and RomFS; older raw/custom ARM diagnostic variants remain available from earlier artifacts. The short retest now requests Save, then RomFS and their new result TXT/snapshot. No long native/guarded/compiled repeat is needed. Result persistence, save update/reload and RomFS acceptance on Wii U are pending. Mario's decrypted executable/assets, PICA-to-GX2, guest audio/retail saves, actual WUP installation, native Windows and the final GUI remain unfinished. Approximately 20% implementation; 0/7 full acceptance milestones.

docs.title: Earlier checkpoints (historical)
docs.text:
Version 0.14.5 hardens reports after a freeze left no file. The uploaded v0.14.3 guarded TXT matches the first run: picture confirmed, A response marked failed, guide cancelled with six steps unfinished, 64 complete input/guest/render checkpoint frames, nine embedded checks passed, zero guest faults/fallback and completed shutdown through main_return. Host frames averaged 285,194 us (about 3.5/s); the old report does not record pixel colors or exact A-to-green latency. It cannot locate the second run's freeze. The user confirms that run saved nothing, so no further old report is requested. Raw evidence and its hashed review remain under ignored private/console-20261011/.

Report checkpoints now request fsync, close the file, flush the mounted SD volume, and reopen the existing report without recreating a missing file. Startup, guest start, the bounded input/guest/render trace and periodic summaries commit this way. Storage failures pause guest execution and show the failing operation, errno and FSA status. The helper owns only its extra FSA client, releases it before system transitions and never remounts/unmounts WUT's SD volume. Late exit checkpoints sync/close the file without opening extra FSA clients. Desktop tests cover abrupt process exit, ordering, failure retention and missing-file preservation; cross-builds use the actual SDK's fsync/FSA imports. Physical power-loss recovery and intermittent-freeze resolution remain unverified. Sync I/O adds diagnostic overhead and does not measure game performance. Follow docs/console-retest.md for one short guarded retest; native/save/standard-AOT tests remain deferred. Implementation remains approximately 20%; no full milestone is closed.

Version 0.14.4 follows confirmed native exit and inconsistent guarded A input. The user confirms Minus now returns normally. The first v0.14.3 guarded run produced green late, after L/advancement, and exited; a second launch froze the whole console while holding A. This is a delayed response plus an intermittent stability failure, not a successful guarded acceptance test. At that point both TXT files were requested; the first is now reviewed above and the frozen run saved nothing. Save testing remains deferred. Feedback is saved privately; no new ROM/intake or installation evidence exists.

Cached nearest-neighbor coordinate maps/repeated rows remove per-pixel 64-bit scaling divisions and preserve all RGBA bytes/borders/padding in desktop tests. The guide requires a fresh decoded green frame after A before enabling R and logs response delay; user confirmation remains separate from pixel evidence. The old AOT engine can dispatch forever without charging an instruction budget; a 64-idle-dispatch guard now yields a visible missing-block fault. The old engine fails a deadline regression and the new engine passes. This has not been linked to the console freeze. Eight live-input timing replays of the original compiled guest (standard/guarded, 1 ms to 1 s clocks, 10,000/50,000 budgets) complete repeated red/green transitions and exit. At 285 ms host pacing the response takes about 7.1 s; initial blank frames are counted separately, with no mixed frames in these cases. No physical performance improvement or freeze resolution is claimed.

Native exit is positive scoped evidence for v0.14.3. v0.14.4 code/build validation does not establish console stability. Implementation remains approximately 20% and all seven full milestone gates stay open.

Version 0.14.3 corrects shutdown ordering and adds a compiled-input comparison. The user clarifies that Minus reaches the Menu splash and keeps playing its music, but never reaches the actual menu. This is a transition stall, not a complete console freeze. The compiled app still freezes the whole system when holding A, without green; no tone played in the newer run. Latest-run TXT files have not been supplied. The first v0.14.1 native report remains positive scoped evidence for ten guided steps/nine embedded checks and resource cleanup. Save testing remains deferred. Feedback/received logs remain under ignored private/.

The previous helper could shut ProcUI down before app resource cleanup. The app now polls ProcUI directly, pauses input/rendering outside the foreground, cleans owned guest/audio/GX2/report resources, clears stale graphics callbacks, preserves save acknowledgement, then requests Menu and waits for EXITING before ProcUI shutdown. HBL relaunch also follows cleanup/ProcUI shutdown. Native AX ownership is tracked across foreground changes; compiled apps never initialize/quit AX.

A new guarded compiled-AOT app limits native call nesting to two instead of 64, using the existing unwind/dispatcher. It runs the same original guest with exact matching frames/input/exit and recorded depth/unwinds on desktop. App menu names show 0.14.3. Checkpoints include call depth, unwinds, frame-boundary stack headroom and lifecycle states; they do not identify the cause of the console freeze. Follow docs/console-retest.md: native Minus first, guarded A next only if exit works, then standard AOT if guarded succeeds. Full console resolution remains awaiting retest; rough implementation stays 20% and no full gate is closed.

The interpreter comparison exposed missing startup instructions. ARMv6 SXTB/SXTH/UXTB/UXTH rotations/conditions/aliases now pass 2,048 independent Unicorn ARM1176 cases and unit/sanitizer checks. Full compiled-interpreter startup still stops visibly on unsupported STRD; no interpreter app is delivered or claimed.

Version 0.14.2 attempted the first console corrections; follow-up failures are above. The received v0.14.1 native TXT records ten passing guided steps, nine passing software self-tests, zero input errors/faults and completed resource cleanup. The user reports a freeze after Minus, requiring reboot. This is partial physical evidence, not successful launcher return. The newer compiled run reportedly shows red/blue and freezes after A's native tone; its run log was not supplied. The older uploaded v0.14.0 .log identifies compiled-interactive and records a guest PASS; it must not be attributed to the newer failed run. Save testing was not attempted. Uploaded raw logs and receipts remain under ignored private/.

Menu launches now request SYSLaunchMenu and poll ProcUI until exit; HBL/Mii Maker routes retain their relaunch path. WUT owns the SD mount, with no duplicate WHB mount/unmount. UDP is optional/off by default. Compiled apps do not initialize or stop AX or play native tones; A is guest input only. Bounded input/guest/render checkpoints, visible progress counters and closed-file exit stages support the next diagnosis. Local checks passed, but the user's follow-up reports both failures persisting. Current v0.14.3 steps are in docs/console-retest.md; defer long guides and the save app. No full milestone is closed.

Version 0.14.1 made console testing guided and recorded readable TXT reports. The native, compiled-interactive and compiled-save apps prompt for inputs and controller confirmations, record completed/failed/skipped steps, and show report filenames and upload instructions. Button/stick/touch samples, guest PASS/exit, save reload, diagnostic timing and an explicit session summary are recorded. Exclusive per-launch files preserve previous reports; checked writes expose SD errors. Interrupted/cancelled tests remain incomplete, and subjective visual/audio confirmations are labeled as user evidence. See docs/guided-testing.md. This improves test collection; the implementation estimate remains roughly 20% and all seven full acceptance gates remain open. Partial console results and remaining failures are recorded above.

October 11 private intake: a valid report-only ZIP was received. The helper reports encrypted_cia_content for the Mario executable; no executable view or game assets were supplied. The original CIA bytes were not independently inspected. The user is preparing hardware tests; decrypted executable intake remains needed.

Version 0.14.0 adds bounded private FS saves and standalone APT lifecycle. Normal compiled libctru/newlib code writes, rereads and commits original save data, uses a Japanese filename, deletes a temporary file, exits, then reloads and updates both records in a fresh process. Guest paths never become host paths. Checked archive/file ownership, access/buffer bounds, read-only mounts and CRC-checked snapshot publication support shared filesystem work without a game patch. Standalone APT runs its real library event thread, wakeup and process shutdown; the boot checks aptIsActive/aptMainLoop. The only remaining traced startup lookup failures are privileged APT:S/APT:A and optional ptm:sysm. A fifth RPX/WUHB supplies an original persistent-save console diagnostic. FS has 1,387 normal/sanitized assertions and APT has 671; see docs/filesystem.md. ROMFS/assets/retail save integration, applets, GX/PICA/audio, Mario execution, installer and Windows GUI remain unfinished. Physical acceptance remains open.

Version 0.13.0 runs original compiler-built libctru applications through normal CRT/newlib startup and checked external AOT, with zero interpreter fallback. Boot, real libctru threads/LightLock/C TLS, standard HID edges/Circle Pad/touch, and actual graphics-thread/shared-GSP RGB565 display are verified on desktop. All three exact two-screen frames are checked pixel by pixel. An additional interactive RPX/WUHB is built for live console input, touch display and guest exit. Eight guest thread slots preserve CPU/TLS/VFP/FPSCR context; address arbitration, quota queries, BSS layout and the kernel configuration page supply shared startup prerequisites. CPU media/FPSCR/scalar FP transport/ARMv6 barriers/SMLAxy have independent ARM1176 evidence (870 cases). See docs/guest-threads.md and docs/compiled-homebrew.md. The v0.13 startup recorded eight failed IPC requests (six APT lookups, one fs:USER lookup and one invalid-session request); no complete service or commercial boot is claimed.

Version 0.12.0 added checked ARM/Thumb stack and register-transfer operations. An original 47-instruction nested ARM → Thumb → ARM call program preserves registers and restores its stack through interpreter/original/external AOT. Independent Unicorn ARM1176 checks pass 220 instruction cases and the full trace. Partial-fault and unsupported-encoding probes validate the external ABI. All Wii U builds embed ARM/THUMB STACK CALLS/stack_selftest; see docs/cpu-stack.md.

Version 0.11.0 adds shared GSP framebuffer queues and a VBlank relay. An original ARM guest now registers/maps the GSP page, queues both RGB565 screens, waits for the relay and drains its IRQ ring with exclusive updates. It matches interpreter/original/external AOT even when a host VBlank interrupts LDREX/STREX. See docs/gsp-queues.md. The queued guest replaces direct submission in the standard HID/GSP diagnostic mode; direct-display tests and all five decoders remain. The earlier pause was an acceptance-evidence gate, not a block on all development. Shared runtime work resumed without the ROM. Physical Wii U results and actual Mario executable intake are still required; see docs/current-roadblock.md.

Version 0.7.0 added the checked heap/linear CPU backing lifecycle; see docs/guest-memory.md.

Version 0.6.0 added shared TLS/SRV/CFG startup and its original ARM self-test; see docs/shared-services.md.

Version 0.5.0 adds CIA intake and a self-contained Windows executable export helper. The user supplied the Mario CIA, but its attachment exceeds the workspace's 32 MiB transfer limit; no commercial bytes were inspected. docs/cia-intake.md explains the small private export workaround. Version 0.4.0 adds original encrypted homebrew packaging and independent decryption/FST/file verification to v0.3.0's external-lifter C generation and checked static execution/linking, title staging and private revision intake. Commercial conversion and the Windows GUI remain incomplete. Installer acceptance is unverified; no milestone requiring physical-console evidence is complete.

docs.title: Verified implementation
docs.text:
• Normal devkitARM/libctru/newlib boot reaches main and exits after 12,416 instructions/35 SVCs. Real libctru threads/LightLock/initialized C TLS pass in 19,989 instructions/40 SVCs. Standard input passes 40,539 instructions/38 SVCs. Graphics and input-driven interactive guests produce all expected pixels in 3,653,198/3,653,794 instructions, with zero fallback; unavailable APT/FS lookups remain explicit. The interactive application also matches on emulated PPC Linux; real compiled threads pass Clang. The scoped native physical results and remaining compiled/save/exit gates are recorded above.

  • Eight process-local thread slots have separate CPU/TLS/raw FP state and waits, strict priority/32-instruction quanta, retained handles/joins, stack pins, recursive mutex ownership and exit cleanup. Address arbiters/local quota output preflight are checked. The thread API has 310 normal/sanitized assertions; the original three-thread probe has 2,694 external boundary assertions, and FP contexts have a separate 61-assertion external arithmetic probe. All native diagnostics embed GUEST THREAD SCHEDULER/thread_selftest.

  • User-mode ARM LDM/STM, Thumb16 PUSH/POP/LDMIA/STMIA and original-AOT register BLX calls use checked word access and interworking. Base writeback occurs after successful transfers; partial faults preserve earlier words and the original base. Empty/user-bank/unpredictable forms fail visibly; v0.13 implements ARM STM's PC+8 source value. 160 API assertions plus the nested-call self-test pass; the external comparison has 352 normal/fault assertions and 48 invalid-Thumb assertions. The independent reference has 220 instruction cases and a 47-instruction full-program trace. Thumb long-immediate calls, complete ARM/VFP and actual PowerPC timings remain open.

  • GSP relay registration returns a retained read/write shared page and client0. Framebuffer updates commit both screens atomically at the diagnostic VBlank; IRQ2/3 wrap/full/coalesced cases, exclusive invalidation, source faults and typed resource/lifetime rollback are checked. All Wii U builds embed the relay self-test and queued original-AOT display guest. 762 API assertions and the original self-test pass normally and with sanitizers. The external comparison has 11,541 assertions, 1,383,167 instructions and 34 SVCs per path, zero fallback and four reference images; GCC/sanitizers, Clang and emulated PPC pass. No complete stock service startup, real interrupt timing, physical execution, GX commands or PICA is claimed.

  • Standard direct GSP acquire/release/force-black/SetBufferSwap checks rights, modes and readable source extents before state changes. Presentation handles rotated RGBA8/BGR8/RGB565/RGB5A1/RGBA4, padding and adjacent mappings; invalid source leaves host output unchanged. 508 API assertions (including v0.13 checked coherent CPU cache flush/invalidation) and the original HID/GSP graphics self-test pass normally and under sanitizers. The external display comparison has 3,603 assertions including four reference PPMs, and passes Clang/emulated PPC. All Wii U builds embed the self-test and original AOT display guest. GX commands, physical/VRAM translation, PICA and stock GPU rendering remain absent. Scoped compiled CPU-framebuffer startup is now verified separately. No console run or gameplay is claimed.

  • Checked unsigned immediate preindexed ARM LDRH/STRH without writeback works in interpreter/original AOT and is exercised by the external graphics probe. Conditions, golden halfwords, alignment/permissions, fault PCs and unsupported forms are checked; this does not complete ARM transfer semantics.

  • HID GetHandles returns checked shared/event copies; shared input is guest read-only. The original ARM consumer maps, waits, reads pad/circle/touch and unmaps/closes/exits through standard interfaces. 858 external boundary and 336 API assertions cover state/bytes/lifetimes, transitions, wrap timestamps, invalid input and capacity rollback. GCC/sanitizers, Clang and emulated PPC checks pass. All Wii U builds embed its self-test and a live original-AOT VPAD-to-ARM consumer. Physical input, timing and shutdown remain unverified; motion/New-family controls remain absent; compiled libctru HID input is now verified separately.

  • Shared/mutex/semaphore handles share the generation-tagged table. Mappings and waits retain objects independently of handles. Heap-backed shared objects pin their source allocation; aliases enforce rights and report Shared state. Shared backing shares the 64 MiB budget. Wait-any selects the first ready object; wait-all consumes nothing until every distinct object is ready. Close/stale/invalid/timeout/resource failures are checked. This does not implement cross-process ownership or priority inheritance. v0.13 adds the separate bounded guest-thread scheduler and owner-aware locks.

  • The original 148-instruction ARM shared/sync probe matches state/memory across interpreter/original/external AOT with 639 boundary assertions and zero fallback. The 197 kernel API assertions and probe pass GCC, sanitizers, Clang and emulated PPC Linux. All three RPX/WUHB builds embed its original SHARED/SYNC LIFECYCLE and kernel_selftest result. Console/native Windows acceptance remains pending.

  • ControlMemory/QueryMemory enforce page bounds, ownership and permissions, with zero-filled first-fit heap/Old-family linear CPU backing. Partial free/ protection preflight mappings and capacity atomically. Loader image/stack/TLS cannot be freed or reprotected. Guard/write-only permissions, holes, resource limits and retained-backing release are tested. Limits are 16 allocations, 32 fragments and 64 MiB total retained backing. Linear GPU/DSP physical-address translation remains absent; local shared aliases are now implemented.

  • The original heap probe executes 151 instructions, 14 memory SVCs and exit. External/original AOT and interpreter CPU/mapping/backing match at 1/7/23 budgets; 1,778 assertions cover lifecycle and protected/freed guest-store fault PCs with zero fallback. Ordinary data mapping changes preserve AOT snapshots; executable mapping/protection and executable-alias writes still invalidate. The current 306 heap API assertions pass GCC, sanitizers, Clang and emulated PPC Linux. All three RPX/WUHB builds embed GUEST HEAP LIFECYCLE/heap_selftest results; physical Wii U and native Windows acceptance remain pending.

  • ARM user read-only CP15 TLS access works in interpreter/original/external AOT. The external ABI refreshes TLS on execution entry and rejects unsupported cache operations even when the pinned emitter would erase them. v0.13 explicitly implements user ARMv6 DMB/DSB ordering for checked CPU backing.

  • Typed, reference-counted service sessions share the generation-tagged handle table. Checked ConnectToPort/SendSyncRequest supports SRV registration/CFG lookup and configured region/model/language reads. It rejects malformed messages, unsupported commands, wrong handles and invalid/aliased output. The Old2DS model ID is verified against libctru (3; New3DS2 is rejected).

  • The original 89-instruction ARM startup probe executes five IPC requests/nine SVCs with matching state/memory through all three backends. 297 external boundary assertions include TLS changed after attach; 35 CP15 assertions cover conditional skips and explicit cache/DMB/DSB/ISB failures. These and the 1,001 service API assertions pass on Clang and emulated big-endian PPC Linux/QEMU. All three RPX/WUHB builds embed the original interpreter/AOT service self-test and native-mode/SD-log result. Physical service execution remains unverified.

  • Original bounded CIA parsing verifies metadata tables, ticket/TMD identity, sparse bitmap/content extents and plaintext hashes; selects executable index 0 and rejects base-title/encryption failures explicitly. Checked loader offsets and external lifter analysis/C generation work for original CIA fixtures.

  • prepare-intake creates a small derived executable CXI/receipt ZIP, omitting RomFS/tickets/certificates/keys and preserving decompressed executable revision. Encryption produces a report-only archive. Source and prior outputs are preserved.

  • The separate .NET console helper produces identical derived CXI bytes for tested inputs, including compressed code and >32 MiB original placeholder data. It passes 13 Linux .NET cases; the self-contained Windows x64 EXE is cross-published with its .NET 10.0.12 runtime/notices. It needs no separate Python/SDK/runtime installation. Native Windows execution remains unverified; it is an intake utility, not the final GUI/injector.

  • The clean pinned fearkov/3dsrecomp checkout is called through an original Rust generation-only driver. A build receipt checks source/driver/binary hashes. Generated C is adapted to an original ABI 4 implementation; the upstream header and tool binary are not bundled. Missing upstream redistribution notices remain an external-tool bundling issue.

  • The checked C engine uses fixed-width guest addresses, explicit little-endian callbacks, executable hash checks, per-instruction state/budget boundaries, precise fault PCs, SVC unwinding to the existing scheduler, invalidation through writable aliases and visible bounded fallback. CROs and unsupported FP modes fail; complete ARM/VFP semantics are not claimed.
  • Actual external AOT execution of the original framebuffer NCCH matches the interpreter's registers/flags and every mapped memory region across uneven budgets. Two touched/button frames execute 1,382,534 instructions, four SVCs, zero fallback and orderly exit. Framebuffer files match byte-for-byte.
  • A separate original 30-instruction ARM/Thumb/scalar-VFP probe checks single and double arithmetic, flags, stack transfers, state switching and one-instruction resume. Its registers/VFP words match Unicorn 2.1.4 independently.
  • External integration passes 566 boundary/frame assertions +34 ABI probe +297 service-startup assertions +35 CP15 assertions +1,778 heap assertions +639 shared/sync +858 HID +3,603 direct HID/GSP display assertions, plus the v0.11 relay probe under GCC, ASan/UBSan, Clang and emulated 32-bit big-endian PowerPC Linux/QEMU 750. Emulation does not establish Wii U behavior or useful speed.

docs.title: CTR2WUP product development plan
docs.text: Finalized 2026-10-07 following the user's request to realign with the supplied preview of “Evaluate 3DS Emulation Viability”, project-brief.md, and the user's UWUVCI AIO GUI workflow clarification. gui-workflow.md specifies the reviewed reference, screens, Inject action, output and acceptance criteria. The referenced conversation supplies product context; its feasibility scores, upstream coverage percentages and compatibility claims are not verified results. The original brief remains the requirements document, with the October 12 user amendment accepting optional local encrypted-input preparation described in encrypted-input.md. This plan corrects the execution priorities and preserves its hardware, correctness and licensing gates.

docs.title: Product and completion target
docs.text:
Deliver a Windows GUI, CTR2WUP.exe, with an UWUVCI-style 3DS Inject page:

Select ROM → configure title/artwork/settings → choose WUP output → Inject → install the resulting WUP on Wii U → launch from the Wii U Menu.

The GUI runs this conversion sequence behind its Inject action:

  1. Select a user-owned Old 3DS .3ds, .cxi or supported base-application .cia. Use decrypted input directly, or prepare encrypted input locally using material imported from the user's 3DS; validate the recovered executable/assets. No key is bundled or uploaded. Device extraction and GUI import help remain planned.
  2. Detect the title/revision and report its actual support status.
  3. Analyze and translate its ARM/Thumb/VFP code on the Windows PC.
  4. Compile translated code and the reusable Wii U HLE runtime with devkitPPC; stage the game's required assets and shader/state data.
  5. Generate original Wii U metadata and a stable per-game title identity, then produce a validated installable WUP directory and build report.
  6. Install on the documented homebrew Wii U environment and launch from the Wii U Menu, with top screen on TV and bottom screen/touch on GamePad.

The first MVP supports one exact commercial Old 3DS revision. Completion requires conversion by the Windows GUI, actual WUP installation/Menu launch, repeatable interactive gameplay, input/touch as required, audio, save/reload, rebuild/save continuity and measured useful performance on physical Wii U. Record the supported revision, installer/environment and known limitations. Broad compatibility follows that proof. The CLI remains the shared build engine and an engineering tool. The finished user product is the GUI; normal injection requires no manual shell commands.

docs.title: Foundation and scope correction
docs.text:
The version 0.2.0 baseline at commit f42d449 contains useful container inspection, build orchestration, checked guest memory, original CPU tests and native/guest Wii U diagnostics. Commercial build currently stops at an unsupported-profile error; its external lifter adapter performed analysis only. Version 0.3.0 now integrates external C generation and checked static linking/execution; see upstream-integration.md. There is no PICA renderer, commercial runtime or Windows executable distribution. Version 0.4.0 implements an original scoped encrypted writer and independent decrypting verifier; installer acceptance and the commercial pipeline remain unverified. packaging.md defines its exact limits and local-input contract.

Keep those foundations and use the synthetic guest as a regression test for the conversion/runtime boundary. Direct development effort toward integrating the audited lifter, reusing suitable HLE behavior, producing WUPs and running the selected title. Expand fixtures and CPU/service coverage to resolve concrete adapter, title or console failures. Measure progress by working conversion stages and supported game behavior, with test counts as supporting evidence.

The planned foundation is the pinned fearkov/3dsrecomp host lifter and license-cleared Zakuro CPU/HLE components or selected behavior ported into a WUT-compatible C/C++ runtime. The current Rust/Vulkan desktop runtime is not a validated Wii U target. Define an explicit portable generated-code ABI and port the required pieces; retain checked little-endian memory and controlled guest scheduling. Normal guest execution uses AOT code, with observable, correct fallback for supported misses. Adopt upstream implementations only after their licenses and target suitability pass the existing audit gates.

docs.title: Ordered implementation plan
docs.text:
Phase Work and concrete deliverable Acceptance / original milestone mapping P1: Resolve conversion foundations Extend the pinned lifter adapter from analysis to C generation and static linking; normalize its 32-bit ABI, little-endian fast memory paths, SVC/resume state and fallback boundary. Resolve lifter redistribution notices. In parallel, choose a license-cleared WUP packaging route and stage original code/content/meta for the existing native app. Original ARM/Thumb/VFP tests execute through the adapted lifter on desktop and PowerPC; report code size, build/memory costs and fallback timing. Original homebrew WUP is generated and physically installed/launched/exited. Advances M1/M2 and establishes M6 packaging prerequisites. P2: Select and analyze the first title Compare a small candidate set using reproduced upstream evidence and service/GPU/module demands. Obtain one user-owned decrypted revision when its private inspection is needed. Extract code, RomFS and required module metadata; create an exact-hash profile and feature/test-route matrix. A selected revision, traceable requirements, repeatable gameplay/save route and explicit unsupported features. Sets the scope for M3–M5. Title analysis can proceed while P1 console tests are pending. P3: Run that title through the Wii U runtime Implement or adapt only the required kernel/SVC/IPC/APT/FS/HID/CFG/GSP behavior, guest scheduling and memory layouts. Implement the required PICA-to-GX2 draws, shaders, textures/TEV/transfers/coherency with reference tests. Add exercised CRO relocation/dispatch, DSP/audio and save/extdata behavior. Use targeted redistributable fixtures for each interface. Adapted guest fixture works on console; selected game progresses through boot → menu → gameplay → save/reload. Produce a manually staged per-game WUP through P1 packaging and verify Menu launch. Record physical CPU/GPU/fallback timings, memory, accuracy and stability. M3/M4/M5 acceptance remains evidence-based. P4: Automate the Windows injection engine Connect all proven stages to the existing host pipeline: detect encryption → optional local decrypt/validate → profile → extract → translate → compile → shader/cache preparation → link/stage → metadata/title ID → pack → validate → publish. Provide real internal build/rebuild/import-trace/validate-package, versioned GUI requests/progress events, cancellation, revision-aware caches, stable saves/IDs and actionable diagnostics. A clean Windows machine converts the selected ROM into the functioning per-game WUP through the engine without hand edits. Verify install/Menu launch, rebuild/save continuity and uninstall behavior. Completes M6 after its console checks; the CLI alone does not complete the product. P5: Deliver the Windows GUI injector Build the C# WPF front end on a supported .NET LTS release over the verified engine, following gui-workflow.md. Provide the UWUVCI-style 3DS Inject page, ROM/compatibility detection, game name and artwork previews, settings/WUP destination, one Inject action, responsive progress/cancellation, completion/SD-install guidance and saved-project rebuild. Package or provision actual prerequisites through documented setup. CTR2WUP.exe performs the supported injection on clean Windows without manual shell commands. Its WUP installs, launches from the Menu and passes the agreed physical-console gameplay/save test. Completes M7 and the first MVP.

P1 has two independent work streams: translator/runtime portability and packaging. Resolve packaging early so installer, metadata, certificate and key requirements are known before completing the game runtime. P2 supplies the evidence for P3's feature priorities. The GUI workflow is specified now; its implementation follows the demonstrated conversion pipeline. Every engine stage supports the final GUI-driven Inject action.

docs.title: Packaging and reuse decisions
docs.text:
The audited nuspacker/CNUS_Packer checkouts have no identified license grant; their certificate templates also lack established redistribution provenance. Find an applicable grant or a suitable licensed alternative. If neither is available, implement an original scoped packer from documented formats with license-cleared cryptographic dependencies. Record the selected route and actual installation evidence before treating packaging as solved.

Complete 3dsrecomp's missing redistribution notices before bundling its executable or ABI support. Its existing local invocation can support research while this is resolved. Preserve applicable notices for adopted Zakuro code; validate each ported subsystem against the portable ABI and target toolchain. A wholesale desktop emulator port is outside the selected architecture.

Keys and any required certificate material use documented user-managed local configuration with redacted diagnostics. ROMs, extracted assets, translated commercial code, saves and per-game packages remain private. A structural package pass is separate from signature/installer policy and successful installation.
