docs.title: Local encrypted-ROM preparation (0.16.0)
docs.text: On October 12, 2026 the user expanded the intended injector to accept either already-decrypted dumps or encrypted dumps with locally supplied material from their own 3DS. This amends the original brief's initial decrypted-only input scope; the original brief is preserved. The final product remains a Windows GUI that converts a supported revision into a playable per-game Wii U WUP.

docs.title: What is implemented
docs.text:
The shared Python engine now supplies prepare-rom and import-rom-keys. They are developer commands; the Windows GUI and on-console extraction helper are not implemented. Decryption is local preparation before the existing checked loader/translator. No platform key values, console dumps or commercial assets are bundled. Already-decrypted input requires no keys or crypto dependency.

Input layer Implemented behavior CIA outer content AES-CBC with a local plaintext title key, or a local normal common key plus the ticket's wrapped title key; content-index IV and full main-content TMD SHA-256 check NCCH v2 Exheader/access descriptor, ExeFS header/files/padding and RomFS AES-CTR; primary and secondary key selection, unaligned stream offsets and 1 MiB bounded chunks NCCH crypto methods Standard KeyX slot 2c, and methods 1 / 0a / 0b using slots 25 / 18 / 1b; seeded secondary KeyY derivation and seed check NCSD cartridge Bounds/overlap checks and extraction of main partition 0; other partitions are not exported or fully inspected Local key imports Plaintext AES key database retail NCCH KeyX records; seeddb base-title seeds; explicitly declared decrypted title-key database base-title records

The prepared private output contains game.cxi and preparation-report.json. It preserves the main executable and RomFS bytes; CIA auxiliary contents, tickets and key files are not copied into that output. The existing inspector validates exheader/section/file hashes and code decompression before atomic publication. A small executable-only upload can then be made with prepare-intake. Source files and existing destinations remain unchanged; failed staging is removed.

Wrong/missing keys or seeds, damaged content, malformed ranges, overlaps and unsupported modes fail visibly. Integrity checks do not authenticate Nintendo signatures. RomFS superblock and canonical three-level IVFC verification are implemented. All declared hash/data blocks, final padding and bounded Level-3 metadata are checked before preparation is published. Unsupported layouts fail explicitly; commercial asset/runtime integration remains unfinished. A derived CXI is not a playable Wii U game or a complete reconstruction of every cartridge/CIA content.

docs.title: A key set, rather than one personal master key
docs.text:
CIA wrapping and NCCH encryption are different layers. The necessary material can include platform KeyX components, a CIA common/title key and a title-specific seed. Some platform keys are shared across consoles. A console-specific SD key such as movable.sed is not sufficient by itself for these standalone game files. The key scrambler is an implemented public algorithm, not a bundled platform key. 3DS input keys and Wii U packaging inputs are separate configurations.

Exporting data requires work on a homebrew-enabled 3DS. A normal Windows USB connection to a stock console does not provide access to its keys. Existing GodMode9 can decrypt game images on-console and export support data; its documentation covers support-file creation and bootrom access. CTR2WUP imports already obtained files. It does not install a console exploit, dump boot9/OTP/NAND, fetch key databases or currently supply a companion.

The local AES-key importer requires decrypted aeskeydb-format records and imports only standard retail NCCH KeyX slots with empty identifiers. It rejects encrypted databases, ambiguous duplicates and malformed metadata; unrelated and devkit-only records are ignored. It does not extract keys from boot9.bin or aes_keys.txt. seeddb uses little-endian title IDs; decrypted title-key records store title IDs in the ticket's big-endian byte order. Database plaintext declaration is not cryptographically authenticated: the recovered CIA must still match its TMD.

A console-bound/personalized ticket needs an already recovered local title key; EC ticket depersonalization is not implemented. Fixed-key NCCH, v1 counters, unknown crypto methods, raw encrypted SD/NAND, updates and DLC are unsupported. Actual user-console exports and native Windows behavior remain untested.

docs.title: Developer workflow
docs.text:
Keep all real dumps, keys, prepared games and derived code under private local storage. The import output is a key store and must remain on the user's PC; do not upload it. Only file paths are accepted as key configuration; reports, repr and commands never contain key values. Keys are read in-process and are not passed to compilers or included in Wii U output. The current private store uses local files; Windows protected credential storage is a later GUI requirement.

python -m pip install '.[decryption]'
python -m host import-rom-keys --aeskeydb "private/aeskeydb.bin" \
  --seeddb "private/seeddb.bin" --decrypted-titlekeys "private/decTitleKeys.bin" \
  --output "private/3ds-key-store"
python -m host prepare-rom "private/owned-game.cia" \
  --keys-config "private/3ds-key-store/keys.json" --output "private/prepared-game"
python -m host prepare-intake "private/prepared-game/game.cxi" \
  --output "private/small-intake"

Each optional database argument can be omitted. Missing material is named by role/title rather than silently substituted. Advanced schema-1 JSON supports ncch_key_x_files, cia_common_key_files, cia_title_key_files and title_seed_files; map slot/index/title identity to a local 16-byte binary file path. A decrypted input can go directly through prepare-rom without --keys-config.

docs.title: Verification and remaining acceptance
docs.text:
Original synthetic fixtures cover all four NCCH methods, seed/no-seed, both CIA layers, mixed ExeFS keys, padding, compressed code, Unicode paths, chunk boundaries, wrong inputs and non-overwriting publication. NIST AES CBC/CTR vectors and a separate bit-string/byte-carry scrambler reference check the crypto primitives. No user key or game is used in these tests.

The original encrypted execution fixture runs through decrypt → inspect → small intake → external AOT → desktop execution → Wii U RPX/WUHB cross-build. The original guest completes its frames and exits; this is a pipeline check, not commercial execution or console acceptance. Run:

python3 tools/validate-rom-preparation.py --wiiu \
  --output artifacts/reports/my-encrypted-pipeline

Binary-format facts were reviewed in GodMode9 commit f3b9ec7a50b8c8459f62b87bfd7b7214b6f6bda2 (ncch, keydb, ticket, ticketdb and seedsave sources) and the existing audited loader sources. No GodMode9 code, bundled key database or executable was incorporated. An actual locally exported key set and owned encrypted dump, clean Windows execution and broader integrity profiles remain acceptance work. PICA, guest audio, retail saves and installable commercial WUP conversion remain separate unfinished milestones.

Use prepare-assets on the recovered CXI to prepare a private checked Level-3 blob and manifest. Guest filenames remain virtual; no archive filenames are extracted onto host paths. See romfs-assets.md.

Batch CIA 3DS Decryptor investigation compares its methods, licenses and input/output handoff. Supported decrypted .cci (NCSD) can enter the same checked pipeline; no batch executable is bundled or executed.

docs.title: Private filesystem and standalone application lifecycle (0.14.6)
docs.text:
This is shared runtime implementation, independent of any game patch. The original compiled program uses normal libctru/newlib fopen, fread, fwrite, fflush, fseek, ftell, fclose, unlink and the standard save-archive commit request. It creates a record, rereads it, uses a Japanese filename, deletes a temporary file, commits, exits, then reloads and updates the record in a fresh process. The host independently checks both saved files and their exact second-run bytes. Corrupt snapshots are refused and preserved, rather than replaced with empty saves.

The portable runtime opens fs:USER, initializes its session and supports:

Interface Commands FSUSER Initialize / InitializeWithSdkVersion; OpenArchive / CloseArchive; OpenFile; CreateFile / DeleteFile; GetFreeBytes; ControlArchive(commit); scoped read-only OpenFileDirectly FSFILE Read / Write; GetSize / SetSize; Flush / Close Explicit archives Savedata (4), private virtual SDMC (9), and current-process read-only RomFS view (3), supplied by the platform

No guest path names a host file. The platform owns a volume until guest teardown; mounts and file sessions retain its lifetime. Archive IDs are generation checked and bound to their service session. File sessions survive archive closure and are retained across kernel-handle duplication. Closing a file session invalidates all copies; final kernel-handle close also releases it. Deleting a live file is explicitly refused in this bounded profile. Archive/file/handle exhaustion rolls back ownership, including a create request when a file session cannot be allocated.

Volumes have 16 root files, at most 1 MiB per file and 4 MiB total data. Request buffers are limited to 1 MiB. ASCII and valid UTF-16 paths are decoded to exact, case-sensitive UTF-8 names; traversal, nested directories, device syntax, separators and invalid Unicode are refused. Sparse extensions are zero filled; reads clamp at EOF without truncating 64-bit offsets. Read/write rights and read-only volumes are enforced. Guest buffers are checked across the entire requested range, including physical aliases of IPC storage, before file or guest output changes. Unsupported wire formats and commands fault visibly.

Writes change the buffered volume. Flush and commit succeed for a writable volume only when its platform persistence callback succeeds. A failed flush can leave dirty buffered data but does not claim a successful save. The original snapshot adapter uses explicit little-endian framing, bounded whole-input validation and a CRC32 corruption check. CRC32 provides no authenticity. It publishes through an exclusive sibling .pending file. v0.14.6 validates any existing primary, moves it to an absent .previous, then renames the stage into the vacant primary name. Successful publication removes the old backup. A failed publish attempts rollback; if rollback fails, both siblings remain available. This avoids relying on POSIX replacement semantics: WUT passes rename directly to FSA. The exact console failure stage is unknown; a no-overwrite filesystem model reproduces the assumption and exercises the corrected publisher.

If the primary is missing, a validated .previous can be loaded with the explicit RECOVERED status. A corrupt primary is never masked by a backup or reset. Stale .pending or ambiguous existing backup blocks another update visibly; preserve both for investigation. There is no concurrent-writer or power-loss durability guarantee. Failure/abrupt-process/rollback/recovery cases run under sanitizers.

The user's uploaded snapshot is CRC-valid, with /progress.dat and /記録.dat at visit 1. A private copy advances to visits 2 and 3 in the updated desktop runner while the original remains unchanged. Console update/reload acceptance is pending. The guest now names its failing phase; the independent result TXT records guest message, load status and persistence errno even if full tracing fails.

Read-only Level-3 RomFS assets are implemented separately; ordinary libctru handles nested names and directory listing in guest code. See romfs-assets.md. NCCH/IVFC extraction/authentication, cartridge assets, generic FSUSER directories, rename/subfiles, extdata, secure values, retail save formatting and commercial integration remain unfinished.

docs.title: Standalone APT
docs.text:
The platform explicitly enables one standalone application (APPID_APPLICATION, 0x300). Only APT:U is advertised; privileged APT:S/APT:A remain unavailable. GetLockHandle returns copied handles to a retained recursive mutex. Initialize returns two real retained events; Enable queues one empty wakeup and signals the resume event. NotifyToWait, GlanceParameter and ReceiveParameter run the checked local state machine. Glance preserves the pending parameter, Receive consumes it. Checked static descriptors support the shell-open query and enable-transition unlock. CheckNew3DS returns the configured Old-family policy. PrepareToClose / CloseApplication terminate the process; Finalize unregisters it while copied objects retain their lifetime. This lets the unmodified libctru event thread, LightEvent/arbitration waits, normal initialization and exit code actually run.

The original boot checks aptIsActive, aptShouldClose and aptMainLoop in guest code. A single-instruction trace captures successful APT and FS requests; remaining lookup failures are exactly APT:S, APT:A, and optional ptm:sysm. The compiled runner explicitly mounts an empty read-only diagnostic virtual SDMC. This is not access to the user's SD card. There is no shell lid, HOME menu, sleep, cross-title launch, shared font, applet, CPU-time quota or New 3DS implementation. Unsupported operations fail; complete_service_startup remains false in reports.

docs.title: Build and console check
docs.text:
make -C tests/filesystem check sanitize
make -C tests/apt check sanitize
python3 tools/validate-libctru.py --application filesystem --wiiu \
  --output artifacts/reports/my-save-test
python3 tools/validate-libctru.py --application boot --trace-startup \
  --output artifacts/reports/my-startup-trace

The additional ctr2wup-libctru-filesystem.rpx / .wuhb executes the same original ARM program through external AOT. Launch with an accessible mounted SD card; the existing diagnostic creates its ctr2wup directory on the WUT-owned SD mount. On a fresh diagnostic save it must display/log SAVE 1 PASS and state=exited. Plus restarts from the snapshot and must display/log RELOAD PASS; exit/relaunch must also reload. The private path is sd:/ctr2wup/filesystem-test.snapshot. Keep the existing file and any .pending / .previous for investigation if the test fails; never replace a failed load with an empty save. Minus exits the host. This is an original diagnostic save and RPX/WUHB, not a Mario save or an installable WUP. The initial snapshot is received; successful physical update/reload is pending. Use the current console retest and return its new result TXT.

docs.title: Evidence and requirements to investigate
docs.text:
The pinned Zakuro source provides concrete leads rather than a compatibility guarantee. At commit 76f17bf76cd9ea238a94f37d389fe701ab05a673:

  • zakuro-core/src/services/mod.rs and services/mii_selector.rs include tests explaining that the game's saved Mii must agree with its CFG console identity. APT/Mii selection, CFG identity and save/reload must therefore be consistent; an empty generic applet response is unsuitable.
  • zakuro-gpu/src/raster/hardware.rs notes small color-buffer CPU readbacks while loading a course. GPU completion and guest-visible memory coherence need real handling, beyond presenting a final framebuffer.

These are source observations that have not been reproduced using the user's revision. The desktop Vulkan implementation is not a GX2 implementation. No upstream executable/assets/caches or implementation from these locations was copied into CTR2WUP.

Area Intake/implementation evidence needed Revision NCCH/NCSD identity, region/version, input/executable hashes and module inventory CPU ARM/Thumb/VFP coverage, CP15/TLS, exceptions, exact generated-code/RSS/memory costs; measured fallback Kernel/IPC Required SVCs, threads/synchronization, srv: routing and traced command shapes Declared services Read the private dump's extended-header allowlist; confirm actual use by tracing Input/display HID shared memory/events, GSP/GX2 command/state translation, TV/GamePad mapping GPU Vertex shaders, textures/TEV/depth/stencil and color-buffer readback/coherency needed by observed scenes Filesystem/modules RomFS assets, save archive operations and CRO/CRS use if present Audio Required DSP protocol/voices and console output; compare against game behavior APT/CFG/Mii Repeatable console/Mii identity, applet completion and save continuity Packaging Original encrypted WUP, install/Menu launch, stable identity across rebuild, uninstall

docs.title: Private intake
docs.text:
Keep a fully decrypted .cia, .3ds or .cxi under ignored private/; no keys are needed for already decrypted input. Avoid update/DLC merging for the first exact revision. The following produces metadata and declared capabilities, not a supported or playable conversion:

python3 -m host analyze-title private/game.cxi --lifter --output private/first-title-intake

The report preserves exact hashes, segment/stack/BSS layout, declared service access and section inventory. The external lifter analysis remains private. Do not infer implemented/observed IPC from the service allowlist. Later extraction and module/shader analysis will use this revision to prioritize concrete runtime work. The synthetic intake commands and CIA/executable-export fixtures are verified; actual commercial intake remains pending the smaller private export.

Proposed manual route, to agree after identifying the dump: cold boot, title menu, start a new save, enter/play the first course, test movement/jump/touch as used, finish/save, exit and relaunch, then rebuild the same title ID and confirm save continuity. Record firmware, homebrew environment, installer, screen/audio behavior, frame/instruction timings and fault/fallback logs. This route is not claimed to have been executed.

While private executable intake is pending, v0.7.0 adds shared heap/linear CPU allocation, free/protection/query and an original three-backend ARM probe. These are reusable startup interfaces, not an inferred Mario patch/profile. Its actual memory needs, thread/shared-memory behavior and GPU/DSP mappings still require the supplied revision and runtime evidence. See guest-memory.md.

docs.title: Foundation audit
docs.text: Audited 2026-10-07 against source obtained through the existing authenticated Git transport. Every requested repository was reachable. Sources are outside this project at /workspace/ctr2wup-deps; none of the seven candidate source trees was vendored into CTR2WUP. Hashes below identify the inspected source, rather than an unpinned README or release claim.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Use fearkov/3dsrecomp as a pinned, external host lifter candidate, with Zakuro's MIT CPU and HLE interfaces as the primary runtime port candidate. The lifter and small CPU package both reproduce successfully on this machine. Keep generated code, guest memory and scheduling behind a C/C++ runtime boundary; compile Wii U code with WUT/devkitPPC. The first prototype must remain independently executable without a game dump.

This selection establishes a host-side foundation. It does not establish that Zakuro's Rust desktop runtime can run on Wii U, that its entire CPU/VFP behavior is correct, or that a game can be lifted into a working Wii U program. A full HLE runtime and PICA-to-GX2 backend are still implementation work. Before distributing 3dsrecomp code or its emitted ABI header, resolve the missing copyright/license-notice file described below. An external local tool invocation avoids silently vendoring an incomplete notice.

Do not adopt mtrdrgz/3ds_recompiler, nuspacker, or CNUS_Packer implementation until an applicable license grant is identified. Public source access is not permission to redistribute it. Azahar is a useful semantic reference and an explicitly GPL-covered alternative; incorporating its implementation would require a compatible project licensing/distribution decision.

docs.title: 3dsrecomp
docs.text:
The host lifter has real ARM, Thumb and VFP emitters, interpreter callbacks for unsupported instructions, an instruction budget and SVC exits, module-aware discovery/relocation analysis, and generated code identity checks. src/lib.rs exposes generation separately from compilation; build::Options can select a compiler. src/compile.rs defaults to desktop shared-library flags and must be adapted for RPX/static linking rather than assuming port outputs a Wii U project.

Guest registers/addresses are fixed-width uint32_t. The C ABI uses host page pointers rather than casting guest addresses directly to host pointers; this is a useful boundary, but its current fast path is not big-endian-safe. In abi/recomp.h:168–206, 16/32-bit guest loads and stores use native-endian memcpy. The generated multiple-transfer span path in src/codegen/mod.rs:81–120 calls load32/store32, which also use native-endian memory representation. Merely fixing fallback callbacks will leave mapped fast-page and span accesses wrong. A Wii U adapter must replace the guest-word helpers or disable those fast paths and provide explicit little-endian callbacks.

VFP double bit assembly in the C header numerically joins low/high words before bit copying, which avoids one common big-endian lane mistake. Floating arithmetic still uses host float/double. The emitter explicitly leaves some conversions to the interpreter, and compiler flags disable FMA contraction, but exhaustive FPSCR rounding, NaN/denormal, signed-zero, exception and conversion correctness is unproven. Exclusive monitors, invalidation, aliases, page permissions, ABI offsets and 32-bit pointer sizes need targeted checks. The existing C/Rust layout test only ran on this host.

docs.title: Zakuro
docs.text:
zakuro-cpu is a small, useful interpreter candidate with a Bus interface and u32 guest state. zakuro-core/src/memory/mod.rs:627 uses explicit little-endian guest reads/writes. zakuro-cpu/src/vfp.rs:49 constructs double bit patterns from numeric low/high words. Those design choices fit a portable runtime better than a flat host address reservation.

The whole runtime is substantially less portable: zakuro-core/Cargo.toml:14 unconditionally enables Vulkan; GPU code uses wide::f32x8, Rayon, native worker threads and desktop window/GPU loading. Raw page pointers and unsafe Send appear in memory/mod.rs:78; recompiled.rs:260 passes pointer-backed page tables through the C ABI. Wii U thread, allocator, filesystem, timing, renderer and static-link boundaries must be supplied. No devkitPPC-compatible Rust target/runtime has been validated.

VFP operations use native f32/f64; upstream explicitly leaves strict default-NaN propagation for future work in vfp.rs:639. Ninety-two passing host instruction tests are useful regression evidence, not a complete ARMv6K/VFP oracle. Reuse the test ideas and compare against trusted references, then run on actual big-endian PowerPC before allowing broad instruction support.

docs.title: mtrdrgz/3ds_recompiler
docs.text:
The source contains a Python ARM/Thumb/VFP lifter, C++ HLE runtime, interpreter fallback, software PICA renderer and desktop/WebGPU paths. Important source hazards are independent of its license blocker: rt/mem.h reserves 4 GiB on native hosts and maps guest VA by g_base + va; read/write helpers use native-endian memcpy. A 32-bit Wii U address space cannot provide that native 4 GiB reservation. WASM selects a different 512 MiB path, which does not establish PPC support.

The shader fast path uses __m128/SSE2; ARM64 builds use sse2neon, not PowerPC. Host FP control mappings target x86/ARM64, with an alternate software path requiring separate validation. Kernel scheduling creates a host thread per guest thread. README acknowledges missing dynamic CRO loading, services, and generic-success service stubs. Its author reports a playable retail title on desktop/Web; that result was not reproduced here.

docs.title: Azahar
docs.text:
Azahar is a broad emulator and useful HLE/PICA semantic reference, but its documented host platforms are 64-bit x86-64/ARM64 desktop/mobile systems. src/core/CMakeLists.txt:552 selects Dynarmic only for x86-64/ARM64; GCC/Clang generic builds choose computed-goto FastInterp. This does not establish PowerPC correctness.

Concrete big-endian hazards remain in FastInterp: fastinterp.cpp:642–695 copies guest bytes directly to native 16/32-bit words and back; handlers/arm_vfp.inc:18–26 copies adjacent low/high u32 words into a native double. Azahar's normal memory access and endian wrappers do not fix these bypass paths. GPL-covered implementation reuse must preserve applicable notices and corresponding-source obligations; no such source has been copied into CTR2WUP.

docs.title: WUT and sample suitability
docs.text:
WUT directly targets Espresso/PowerPC EABI with hard float (share/wut_rules: -mcpu=750 -meabi -mhard-float) and exposes OS, GX2, VPAD, audio and RPX/RPL support. This is the appropriate native console SDK candidate. The sample source demonstrates orderly WHB startup/shutdown and actual GX2 APIs rather than emulated desktop equivalents. samples/cmake/gx2_triangle expects pos_col_shader.gsh in SD content; its presence is a sample dependency, not evidence that arbitrary PICA shaders can be compiled for Latte.

SDK/library source review does not itself produce a valid RPX. The platform prototype's separate build report records the actual toolchain setup and compile result. Physical Wii U dual-display, touch, audio and exit acceptance remains awaiting console tests.

docs.title: Packaging investigation
docs.text:
Both audited NUS packers require staged Wii U code/content/meta, package metadata and local key configuration. Neither is a direct .3ds converter. nuspacker/README.md:5 explicitly requires patched IOSU; packaging does not make a title installable on an unmodified retail console.

The implementations create TMD/ticket/content/hash structures, but do not generate authentic Nintendo signatures. Java/C# TMD code uses zero RSA signature fields; ticket code uses random signature bytes. Content and H3 hashes concern content integrity and do not establish authenticity or installer acceptance. Certificate templates also need independent provenance/license review.

Both upstream entry points echo supplied encryption keys (Starter.java:186–187, Program.cs:188–189); never pass secrets through logged commands. A tracked Java encryptKeyWith placeholder exists, but no credential value was printed, adopted or copied. Keep keys in user-managed local configuration, redact diagnostics, and obtain only credentials actually required by the selected future packer.

Actual source-only build errors: javac: command not found and dotnet: command not found, both exit 127. No packer executable was run, no WUP was produced or installed by this audit, and no source license gate was bypassed. Continue with an original structural validator and staging/reporting support; choose a licensed packer or obtain an explicit upstream grant before integration. A structural validation pass alone must not be reported as a successfully installed title.

docs.title: Remaining gates
docs.text:
Resumed 2026-10-08: v0.3.0 integrates the pinned external generation driver with the original checked ABI; v0.4.0 implements original scoped encrypted packaging with independent decrypt/FST/file checks. cryptography 50.0.0 uses its BSD-3-Clause grant, preserved in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES/docs/licenses. Offline packaging uses original synthetic credentials only; the real WUT RPX passes staging/packing/decryption comparison. No packer candidate implementation or certificate template was adopted. See packaging.md for the current contract; installer acceptance, certificate provenance/trust and Menu launch remain gates.

  • Complete 3dsrecomp's redistribution notices; validate the original packaging profile on console.
  • Replace/verify little-endian fast helpers, 32-bit ABI layouts, guest permission/alias handling, exclusive access and invalidation.
  • Validate ARM/Thumb/VFP semantics differentially, including unsupported-instruction failure visibility and state at SVC/yield boundaries.
  • Establish a supported Wii U interpreter/HLE platform port; the desktop Zakuro runtime is not a ready-made RPX runtime.
  • Implement and measure PICA-to-GX2, guest services, CRO behavior, audio and save semantics required by a controlled fixture.
  • Run physical-console platform diagnostics and PowerPC benchmarks; use those measurements before choosing a commercial game revision or promising performance.
  • Validate Windows installation/builds and a complete original homebrew packaging path with a suitable installer; then request the smallest specific console evidence or user-owned dump needed for subsequent milestones.

docs.title: v0.16 asset/texture layout review (October 12, 2026)
docs.text:
Read-only format references: GodMode9 f3b9ec7a50b8c8459f62b87bfd7b7214b6f6bda2 (arm9/source/game/romfs.c and romfs.h), the already pinned Azahar texture/color sources, and Zakuro 76f17bf76cd9ea238a94f37d389fe701ab05a673 texture/format modules. Canonical NCCH IVFC physical/logical layout and Level-3 metadata facts informed original bounded host verification. No GodMode9 code or bundled key database was adopted, read for key material or redistributed. Its GPL license remains in its separate read-only reference checkout; it is not a runtime/build dependency.

The original base texture decoder has independent golden vectors and a Python reference. A test-only Rust wrapper compiles the clean pinned Zakuro modules in that external checkout, compares original images, and remains outside source/ delivery binaries. The known HILO channel-layout difference is documented in renderer-status.md rather than hidden in a blanket comparison claim. No Azahar implementation is copied or linked. These checks do not prove GX2 rendering, real-game assets or Wii U performance.

Maintained source: docs/foundation-audit.md · 1b14ea67cba6. GitHub source and issue links may require repository access.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: CTR2WUP currently runs original diagnostic applications, not commercial 3DS games. The final Windows GUI and playable-game WUP conversion are still being developed. Choose a diagnostic release only when you want to help test the runtime. Native .wuhb/.rpx diagnostics are different from installable WUPs.

docs.title: Download a matching release
docs.text:
Use the repository's development releases. Read its release notes and SHA256SUMS.txt; keep the kit, source version and instructions together. CI builds are available from each successful Actions run, with the source commit in their artifact names. Hosted builds are structural/test evidence.

The focused 0.20.0 kit contains Audio Check and GX Transfers original diagnostics. See the short launch-music check for its purpose and prompts. Earlier 0.14.6 contains the Save/RomFS follow-up kit; 0.16.0 adds Asset Files. Use the kit requested by the relevant testing guide. Do not replace/delete save snapshots or old reports while investigating a failure.

docs.title: Wii U prerequisites
docs.text:
The diagnostic launch route targets a homebrew Wii U with Aroma and an SD card. The current tester reports a U.S. Wii U using latest firmware/Aroma/WUP Installer GX2; exact version numbers have not been recorded. This is a reported environment, not a promise for every setup. Follow your homebrew environment's own installation instructions; CTR2WUP does not install or update console firmware. WUP Installer is not needed to launch the diagnostic WUHB files.

  1. Extract the kit and copy the contents of sd-card/ to the SD root.
  2. WUHBs go under sd:/wiiu/apps/. Launch the named app from Aroma.
  3. Follow the app's controller prompts. Minus saves the current result and requests exit; tell us if the launcher/Menu return fails.
  4. Collect results from sd:/ctr2wup/. ZIP the named result-*.txt files and any full traces requested by the guide, then attach the ZIP to a console-result issue or the current development conversation.

An RPX launcher can use the kit's rpx/ files instead. RPX launch and Aroma WUHB launch can follow different lifecycle paths; record which you used.

For GX Transfers 0.17.0, see the two-step guide. It needs no ROM, key or extra asset file. For Asset Files 0.16.0, the original blob must also be present at sd:/ctr2wup/romfs-test.bin. Save/result testing follows console-retest.md. Completed long input guides need not be repeated merely because a newer source version exists.

If a result is missing or the app hangs, use troubleshooting.

docs.title: Build from source
docs.text: See CONTRIBUTING.md for Python, host compiler and verified devkitPro/WUT setup. make check runs the regression suites; make prototype produces original RPX/WUHB diagnostics. Windows has a separate native toolchain route and CI baseline; Linux SDK executables do not run on Windows.

docs.title: Your owned game input
docs.text:
The future GUI will accept decrypted dumps or locally prepared encrypted inputs. Current engineering commands can prepare supported inputs locally and export a small private executable intake. Their success does not enable game execution. Do not attach keys, full ROMs, saves or commercial asset blobs to GitHub issues. The first selected game is Super Mario 3D Land; its actual revision and requirements still await private analysis.

Maintained source: docs/getting-started.md · 1b14ea67cba6. GitHub source and issue links may require repository access.

docs.title: GitHub development
docs.text: Project #2 is the authority for status, waiting resources and reviewed acceptance. GitHub also records source, reviewable changes, milestone issues, CI logs/artifacts and versioned original diagnostic releases. Keep the product goal and current limits visible; no badge establishes commercial gameplay or physical-console acceptance.

docs.title: Roadmap and evidence
docs.text:
Each of the seven milestones has an overview tracker and five focused work issues. The 35 work issues carry acceptance criteria, prerequisite links and required evidence; the seven overviews coordinate full milestone acceptance. Area and waiting labels identify CPU/runtime/graphics/host work and console, input or Windows gates. Checked foundations and open full-acceptance items are separate. Add test evidence in comments; maintainers update the versioned source assessment after reviewing it.

docs/milestone-status.json supplies versioned requirements and evidence for managed milestone descriptions, overviews and work-issue sections. Its state fields seed empty values at initial setup; existing Project states and waiting resources always win. The Project tracking workflow updates evidence sections on trusted main without deleting comments or manual notes, duplicating trackers or automatically closing acceptance gates. To preview or explicitly apply a source update with normal gh authentication:

python3 tools/sync-github-progress.py
python3 tools/sync-github-progress.py --apply

docs.title: Labels and branch status
docs.text:
Labels Meaning status:planned Defined work awaiting implementation or triage. status:in-progress Active/partial work, a draft PR or checks still pending. status:blocked Missing prerequisites or current failed checks. status:awaiting-evidence Scoped implementation awaits required evidence; also an explicit PR hold. status:ready-for-review Current PR head has passing Required CI and Documentation checks; maintainer review remains. status:done A Project task was reviewed as Done, an unmanaged task completed, or a PR merged. status:accepted A Project overview was explicitly Accepted after full-gate evidence review; never a task or merged PR. status:closed A task was abandoned or a PR closed without merging. area:*, documentation, bug, enhancement Component and kind of work. needs-console, needs-input, needs-windows Specific waiting resources. p0 / p1 / p2 / p3 Emergency / urgent / normal / low triage priority.

Managed roadmap issues mirror Project Status and recognized Waiting resource categories. Edit the board fields to change them; an issue closure or manual label does not change canonical Project state. PRs and unmanaged issues retain their lifecycle/check-based status automation. Other labels, priorities and manual notes are preserved. Closing a task or merging code never accepts a full milestone. Use status:awaiting-evidence to hold a PR for missing validation; CI does not remove that hold. Record runtime and visual evidence in the issue/PR, using original reference frames, browser captures or guided console TXT observations.

The Work-item statuses workflow responds to issue/PR lifecycle, deliberate status-label changes and completed CI/Documentation runs. It skips Project-managed roadmap issues and leaves their mirrors to Project tracking. It executes trusted immutable main code and reads API data; it never executes a contributor's branch or downloads untrusted build artifacts. Status writes touch only managed status labels. Current merge checks must include the actual PR head, so old results cannot mark newly pushed code ready. The Actions summary/artifact reports branch names, associated PRs, states, checks and reasons.

python3 tools/sync-github-status.py --output artifacts/github-status.json
python3 tools/sync-github-status.py --number 12 --status awaiting_evidence --apply

GitHub labels apply to issues and PRs. Use focused names such as feature/m4-pica-commands, fix/m1-result-write or docs/testing-guide; their status is visible through the linked PR, CI checks and the workflow report. Release Git tags identify versions and remain separate from task status.

The structure adapts Odysseus's coordination milestone, label taxonomy and review template: focused tasks, explicit blockers/evidence, triage priority and reproducible review. CTR2WUP's acceptance criteria remain specific to Wii U execution and the planned injector; unavailable console/game tests stay pending. The user's GitHub Free, private-source and no-branch-protection choices remain in force.

docs.title: Pull requests and CI
docs.text:
Use a topic branch and the PR template for reviewable problem/behavior/validation changes. CODEOWNERS identifies the maintainer. Required CI summarizes:

  • workflow lint with checksum-pinned actionlint;
  • Python 3.12 and 3.14 fixtures and installed-wheel smoke checks;
  • GCC and Clang portable tests with ASan/UBSan;
  • native Windows host and normal portable C fixtures;
  • Wii U RPX/WUHB build using the official immutable devkitPro SDK image.

Actions are pinned by commit, permissions are scoped per workflow/job, fork PRs receive no repository write access, logs survive failures and concurrency avoids unneeded duplicate PR runs. Test/build artifacts include the source commit; Wii U artifacts include checksums, provenance and notices. Dependency update PRs cover actions and Python dependencies. Review them; they are not auto-merged.

The separate manual Windows workflow validates real external AOT/Unicode execution and WPF tooling. CodeQL is manual-only and requires confirming existing scanning eligibility. This setup does not buy or enable Advanced Security. Read each run's actual result; workflow publication is not proof that hosted checks succeeded.

docs.title: Releases
docs.text:
Development releases are prereleases with explicit diagnostic scope, source tag, notes, checksums and matching source/wheel/console artifacts. Do not call an RPX/ WUHB a WUP or label a diagnostic release playable. No real game, key, seed DB, save, private trace or extracted commercial asset belongs in an Actions artifact or release. Preserve older requested test kits and their versioned instructions.

The 0.17.0 kit contains Native and GX Transfers. Its release also includes a single offline HTML guide and generated public docs-only site bundle. The 0.14.6 kit remains the Save/RomFS follow-up. Getting started explains SD layout, Aroma/RPX launch and report delivery.

The Publish development diagnostics workflow is dispatched explicitly from main with the version in pyproject.toml. It runs required checks, verifies SDK/ lifter/libctru pins, executes the original GX application with sanitizers, builds RPX/WUHB and smoke-tests the wheel. The packager checks reported binaries/frames, source and wheel module equality, ZIP CRCs and SHA-256 sums. A separate job with contents: write publishes the matching prerelease with GitHub's native token; a failed upload leaves a draft. Published versions cannot be replaced by different artifacts. This route also avoids the cloud connection's rejected upload-host authentication. It does not close console or commercial acceptance gates.

docs.title: Agent support
docs.text:
Shared instructions, Copilot guidance and four specialist profiles cover CPU/runtime, host conversion, graphics and read-only console-evidence review. Use supported Copilot clients when the account has access. Profile files do not activate a subscription or automatically assign work to an external service. Current development also used independent parallel runtime and workflow/documentation reviews; actual findings were corrected and checks rerun.

Codex work uses the repository's opt-in commit attribution hook. Its verified public bot author and standard Codex co-author trailer provide visible credit while normal Git/PR authentication continues through the connected account. It does not impersonate a bot login or rewrite earlier history.

docs.title: Documentation and free hosting
docs.text:
The Markdown guides are readable directly in GitHub. Each Documentation workflow build also provides a searchable Material site and a single HTML guide that opens directly in a browser, with navigation, search and a print layout. The HTML guide requires no account, server or internet connection to read its content. Download it from a matching development release or Documentation run artifact.

A separate public CTR-2-WUP-docs repository can host the generated site with GitHub Pages on the free plan while the application repository remains private. The export bundle includes the rendered site, notices, README and a pinned Pages workflow; it excludes application code, ROMs, keys and private test data. Initial creation/publication still requires repository access. A generated bundle is not proof of a published site; only link a live URL after verifying deployment. The connected integration rejected creation of CTR-2-WUP-docs with HTTP 403 Resource not accessible by integration. The ready export can be uploaded to a public repository created by the owner, or published after granting the required repository creation/Pages access. The HTML guide is usable immediately. Private-source Pages is unavailable on the user's current plan and is not enabled.

python3 -m venv artifacts/docs-build-venv
artifacts/docs-build-venv/bin/python -m pip install -r docs-requirements.txt
artifacts/docs-build-venv/bin/python tools/build-docs-site.py
artifacts/docs-build-venv/bin/python tools/package-docs-site.py

The strict build validates rendered links, anchors, search and assets. The site is in artifacts/docs-site/site/; the HTML guide and public-repository bundle are in artifacts/docs-publication/. Their JSON receipts and checksums identify the source commit. Source links stay commit-specific and require repository access. The site and HTML guide preserve the product goal, progress and acceptance limits.

docs.title: Maintenance on GitHub Free
docs.text:
The private source repository uses topic branches and reviewable pull requests. Check the latest Required CI and Documentation build on the PR before merging; keep source and evidence together. Preserve history and use a new version for changed published artifacts. Dependencies/actions are pinned, CODEOWNERS identifies the maintainer, and contributor/security/result guides provide the review context.

The user explicitly declined branch protection because the repository is private on GitHub Free. No protection rule or administration setup tool is incorporated. These maintenance practices are team conventions; GitHub does not enforce them.

docs.title: Board setup
docs.text:
The owner-selected Project #2 is the tracking source of truth. Setup resolves that exact board and all 42 managed issues. It fails before writes on inaccessible/ambiguous data and never creates a replacement board. Existing title, notes, option IDs, manual items, nonempty field values and existing view filters/layouts are preserved.

The detailed overview explains the seven deliverables and acceptance boundaries, status policy, private evidence and next console handoff. Work type and Priority supplement Status, Milestone and Waiting resource. New filtered views cover Delivery gates, Implementation work, Evidence handoff and Pull requests. Source requirements initialize empty fields only; Accepted is reserved for reviewed full milestone overviews. See the overview template.

python3 tools/flesh-github-project.py --output artifacts/github-project-plan.json
python3 tools/flesh-github-project.py --apply --output artifacts/github-project-result.json

applied, live_project_verified, completed operations and partial-change flags state what actually happened. A denied read cannot establish a live board. As of this source increment the personal secret requirement is saved, but the environment reports has_saved_binding:false; its Project read still uses the limited integration and returns Resource not accessible by integration.

docs.title: Project-backed progress
docs.text:
Project #2 is the authority for Status, Waiting resource and full-gate acceptance. Its seven overview issues and 35 focused tasks, detailed overview, work-type/priority fields and filtered views are populated and verified through the repository Actions secret. Existing owner values and notes are preserved. GitHub's default Todo option is shown as Planned in the aggregate without changing the option or its ID.

The tracking workflow reads Project fields hourly and on request, then publishes an allowlisted JSON snapshot, stacked milestone chart and interactive dashboard. Bars show five work items per milestone; completed children never automatically accept a full gate. Chart timestamps are visible; the dashboard marks snapshots older than two hours stale and preserves the previous update time on read errors. GitHub can cache README images; open the dashboard for current freshness.

The public docs publisher runs reviewed immutable main source, requires a strict searchable documentation build and verifies the docs-only archive before any write. It can explicitly create only Jdiller-86/CTR-2-WUP-docs as public, configure free workflow-based Pages and publish its generated site. Application visibility never changes. Both publishers preserve existing tree contents and update main without force. Progress lives in site/progress/, inside the Pages upload root. The prepared site URL is https://jdiller-86.github.io/CTR-2-WUP-docs/; live publication is established by deployment receipts and HTTP checks.

Only seven documented milestone names, aggregate counts, accepted-gate counts, fixed waiting-resource categories, freshness and the Project link enter the public snapshot. No private issue title/body/number, item ID, owner note, ROM, key or trace is exported. Unknown custom status/resource values remain in fixed Other buckets.

Configure CTR2WUP_GITHUB_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN in repository Actions secrets with Project and the required repository/Pages permissions. Cloud-environment secrets are separate; the Actions route is verified, while cloud Project calls still use a limited integration. Tokens are never requested in chat or copied into reports. Use trusted-main Project tracking for setup/export and Publish public documentation for docs-only publication. Neither runs untrusted PR code with the management token. Dry-run tools are available for reviewing mutations.

docs.title: Settings requiring additional access
docs.text:
The connected integration can push code, work with issues/milestones and read Actions runs, but GitHub rejected createProjectV2 and repository administration/ security-setting writes as Resource not accessible by integration. These are GitHub access denials, not failed source checks or an automatic approval review.

The prepared desired setup is:

  • Private project CTR2WUP Development, linked to this repository, containing seven overviews plus 35 work issues, with Planned / In progress / Awaiting evidence / Blocked / Ready for review / Done / Closed / Accepted columns and fields for milestone and waiting resource. Accepted remains reserved for explicitly reviewed full milestones.
  • About description/topics reflecting early development; optional Discussions, delete merged topic branches and free dependency-alert settings.

Grant the GitHub connection the relevant Projects write and repository Administration/security-setting and public docs-repository/Pages write access to finish those protected operations, or apply them in repository/account settings.

For this cloud environment, an optional secure personal secret requirement named CTR2WUP_GITHUB_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN has been saved for api.github.com only. The Projects API documentation specifies a classic personal access token with project scope; private repository issues/settings additionally need repo access. Enter the credential in environment settings, review/save the draft and publish the environment changes. Saving the requirement alone does not grant access or create a board. Keep the existing connection for normal Git/issue/Actions work; use the optional credential only for the management operations. No token value should be pasted into chat. The desired configuration is concrete and reviewable; the live milestone/issues view works while board access is pending. Repository visibility and paid entitlements have not been changed.

Maintained source: docs/github-development.md · 1b14ea67cba6. GitHub source and issue links may require repository access.

docs.title: CTR2WUP Development
docs.text: Product: a Windows GUI that turns an owned 3DS game into its own installable Wii U WUP. Select a game, configure its title/artwork, Inject, install, and play from Wii U Menu. Super Mario 3D Land is the first candidate. Current releases are original diagnostics; commercial gameplay, the draw renderer and the GUI remain unfinished.

docs.title: Tracking authority
docs.text:
This Project is the source of truth for task status, blockers and full milestone acceptance. Change Status and Waiting resource here. Issue descriptions hold scope, prerequisites, acceptance criteria and evidence; source files hold versioned implementation receipts. Source JSON is an evidence/initialization record and cannot overwrite an existing Project status.

The dashboard reads this Project and publishes aggregate counts. A publication error must leave the last successful timestamp visible; it never invents a fresh status or turns missing evidence into completion. Task completion is separate from the rough engineering estimate toward a playable injector.

docs.title: Delivery gates
docs.text:
Gate Deliverable and acceptance boundary M1 · Wii U platform Native displays, controls/audio, repeat launch/exit, verified SD results/save recovery, and an installed original WUP. M2 · CPU translation Required ARM/Thumb/VFP and ABI/memory behavior, bounded visible fallback, and measured Espresso execution. M3 · Homebrew runtime Original compiled guests on console, required services/modules/audio, and repeatable save/asset access. M4 · PICA → GX2 Vertex/shader/fragment execution, textures and coherency, original reference scenes, and console measurements. M5 · First game Privately identified Mario revision, boot/gameplay/audio/save/reload and measured performance. M6 · Automated WUP conversion Reproducible Windows conversion and packaging, actual installation/Menu launch, rebuild cache and save continuity. M7 · Windows injector GUI A responsive packaged Select → Configure → Inject workflow backed by the verified engine, useful diagnostics and clean-PC acceptance.

Each gate has an overview and five focused tasks. Dependencies describe what is needed to accept a task; independent fixtures and shared runtime development can continue while a prerequisite awaits evidence.

docs.title: Status and review
docs.text:
• Planned: scoped work has not started.
  • In progress: implementation exists but its criteria remain open.
  • Awaiting evidence: an artifact is ready for the named console/input/Windows check.
  • Blocked: a recorded prerequisite prevents completion.
  • Ready for review: the scoped change and required checks are ready to assess.
  • Done: a task's criteria have been reviewed; this never accepts its parent gate.
  • Closed: work was closed without representing accepted delivery.
  • Accepted: reserved for a full milestone overview after all its criteria and physical/title/Windows evidence have been reviewed. A merged PR cannot set it.

Keep the gate open until that review is complete. Archive only after preserving the acceptance record; archived managed items make synchronization fail visibly. Use Priority for ordering, and Waiting resource for the concrete next handoff. Record evidence in issue comments or maintainer notes; retain failures and verbal reports separately from versioned logs.

docs.title: Console handoff
docs.text:
The current focused round is Save/result persistence, embedded RomFS, GX/PICA setup and optional SD assets. Original diagnostics require no ROM or key. Upload their named TXT reports and retained snapshot siblings privately in the Codex chat, with observed exit/pictures and exact environment versions when available. Do not publish game dumps, decryption keys, retail saves or commercial traces.

Requirements · Acceptance criteria · Build evidence · Development releases

Maintained source: docs/github-project-overview.md · 1b14ea67cba6. GitHub source and issue links may require repository access.

docs.title: Standard direct GSP framebuffer display (0.10.0)
docs.text:
The shared runtime advertises gsp::Gpu. This original implementation supports single-process direct framebuffer submission through checked TLS IPC:

Request Checked behavior AcquireRight 00160042 flags0, one copy descriptor0 and current-process pseudo-handle ffff8001; acquires the local process's display right ReleaseRight 00170000 Releases the acquired right SetLcdForceBlack 000b0040 flags0/1; actually controls decoded output SetBufferSwap 00050200 screen0/1 and seven framebuffer words; validates source range before changing state

Replies have one normal result word and the requested command ID, e.g. 00050040/result0 for SetBufferSwap. Duplicate session handles retain ownership; closing the last GSP session drops the right. Descriptors remain for display after release, until guest close or a later submission. Unsupported commands and malformed/unsupported modes fault visibly, with endpoint/header recorded. Invalid source memory records a precise memory fault before any display-state change. These are scoped HLE policies, not retail error-code/timing conformance.

Framebuffers are fixed 2D top 400x240/bottom 320x240. Active index and display-select must be equal 0/1, the unknown word 0, and the secondary address 0 or equal to primary. Supported mode bits are formats 0..4, top 2D bit 6 and local-memory bit 8. Top requires bit 6; bottom must clear it. Stereo, wide800, VRAM bit 9 and other mode bits fail. Column stride must contain all 240 pixels and be at most 4096 bytes; padding is permitted. The reader uses base + x*stride + (239-y)*bytes_per_pixel and checks the entire source extent, including adjacent mappings, before writing host output. It revalidates on every presentation, so freed/reprotected backing fails safely. No guest address becomes a host pointer and no native-endian pixel cast is used.

The five formats are ABGR-byte RGBA8, BGR8, little-endian RGB565, RGB5A1 and RGBA4. Channels expand by bit replication; alpha is preserved. Host output is numeric RRGGBBAA, which the existing GX2 copy backend writes as explicit RGBA bytes. Force-black output is opaque black. Tests use independent golden channels, four distinct corners, padded strides, split mappings, overflow/permission faults and unchanged output on failed preflight. CPU cache/GX2 surface synchronization remains in the native presentation backend; this is not PICA cache emulation.

The original ARM program in host/gsp_fixture.py acquires SRV/HID/GSP, waits for standard HID input, writes RGB565 CPU framebuffers and submits both screens. A makes the top green, release makes it blue. Valid touch makes the bottom magenta with one white pixel; release makes it cyan. The top's corners are white, red, green and blue (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right). Two frames and cleanup execute 1382865 instructions and 27 SVCs, with zero fallback and matching full state/memory through interpreter/original/external AOT. The fixture also checks unsigned ARM LDRH/STRH with immediate preindexing and no writeback; other ARM halfword forms remain unsupported in the bounded original backends.

make -C tests/gsp check sanitize runs 362 API assertions and the original interpreter/AOT display self-test. tools/validate-upstream.py --gsp-api --output artifacts/my-display-checks executes all nine external probes and writes gsp/frame-{1,2}-{top,bottom}.ppm reference images. The external display test has 3603 assertions when writing all four images. Host, sanitizer, Clang and emulated PPC results establish portable behavior, not Wii U execution or usable speed.

All three Wii U builds embed gsp_selftest; native mode displays HID/GSP RGB565 DISPLAY PASS CODE 0. Y cycles native → original custom-I/O ARM fixture → standard HID/GSP fixture. The GSP fixture uses original AOT in all builds; v0.11 replaces the live direct guest with the shared-queue variant described in gsp-queues.md. The existing external-AOT build still uses the actual external lifter for its custom-I/O fixture. External HID/GSP execution is separately tested on desktop/emulated PPC. The GSP status overlay is in the middle of the top image, leaving all four corner markers visible. Plus resets both graphics guests, B requests the current graphics guest's exit and Minus exits the application. Input latency includes bounded 50,000-instruction host slices and complete CPU frame fills. SD logs contain swaps, state, fallback, fault and shutdown outcomes.

Interface facts were checked against libctru 9b55eda44cf80b971503991e0c78f9bc8fe50425, gspgpu.h, gspgpu.c, gfx.c, and the audited Zakuro display/format descriptions. No upstream implementation was copied. Version 0.11 adds interrupt relay registration, shared framebuffer queues and diagnostic VBlank; see gsp-queues.md. GX command queues, DMA/display transfers, VRAM/physical-address translation, PICA registers/draws/shaders/textures/TEV and graphics thread scheduling are absent. Stock libctru graphics initialization needs several of these and is not claimed to boot. This bridge is a reusable display foundation for the injector.

The next planned acceptance gate is physical Wii U input/display/stability and the selected Mario revision's private executable intake. Without that evidence, M3/M4/M5, commercial conversion, installer acceptance and the GUI remain open.

docs.title: GSP shared framebuffer queues and VBlank relay (0.11.0)
docs.text:
This shared runtime increment uses standard GSP wire layouts to present the original ARM graphics probe. It supports one local guest/client slot, two screens, CPU framebuffer memory and a deterministic diagnostic clock. It does not enable commercial conversion or stock libctru graphics initialization.

RegisterInterruptRelayQueue (00130042) accepts flags1, copy descriptor0 and a live event handle, after AcquireRight. The successful 00130082 reply contains result0, client ID0, copy descriptor0 and an owned read/write 4096-byte shared-memory handle. Result0 means this HLE display is already configured; the hardware-init result path and GPU register programming are unsupported. Typed resource/stale-handle errors return a service result. Malformed wire layouts and unsupported commands fault visibly. Duplicate registration fails.

The device retains the shared page and event independently of returned handles. Mappings and waits also retain their objects. Closing the last copy of the registering session or UnregisterInterruptRelayQueue (00140000) releases the device references; an existing mapped page stays valid. Another session cannot unregister the owner. Last-GSP-session close releases display rights.

The slot0 interrupt record has index/count/error/reserved bytes at offset0, with 52 interrupt bytes at offset 0x0c. Framebuffer headers are at 0x200 and 0x240: bit0 selects one of two seven-word entries, bit8 marks an update. Queue entry selection is independent of the displayed buffer's active index. The format/range checks and rotated decoders are described in gsp-display.md. Other header bits and unsupported display modes are rejected.

At a due host scheduling entry, both dirty descriptors and readable source extents are checked before either screen changes. Successful publication clears only dirty bits, commits the latest pending descriptors, appends VBlank0/1 IRQs 2/3, and signals the retained event through the normal wait mechanism. Ring wrap preserves pending entries. A full ring sets the error byte and records dropped IRQs; it never overwrites pending interrupts. Invalid headers, source permissions or modes leave the page and display unchanged and fault the guest. Nonzero queued-GX headers at 0x800 fault rather than discard unimplemented work.

The interval is 16,666,667 ns. This is a diagnostic 60 Hz clock, not measured 3DS/Wii U timing. A late host call coalesces missed intervals into one IRQ pair and the latest display update, while recording missed intervals. A repeated call at the same time cannot deliver another pair. Deadline overflow faults. Releasing display rights pauses processing; registration stays owned until unregistered. Device writes invalidate the CPU exclusive monitor and executable aliases.

The original ARM probe (host/relay_fixture.py) maps the page, writes rotated RGB565 screens, uses word LDREX/STREX to publish and drain queues, waits for the relay, reads both interrupt IDs, then unregisters/unmaps/closes/exits. The same instruction stream runs in interpreter, original AOT and the real pinned external recompiler. The comparison deliberately inserts a second VBlank between LDREX and STREX, ensuring a failed store retries without losing interrupts. Two frames plus that interleaving execute 1,383,167 instructions and 34 SVCs per path with zero fallback. The external comparison has 11,541 assertions. All state, mapped/shared bytes and pixel references are compared. Generated original sources reproduce from the checked generator.

make -C tests/relay check sanitize passes 762 API assertions covering timing, atomic two-screen updates, ring wrap/full cases, source failures, resource rollback, session ownership and handle lifetime, alongside the original interpreter/AOT self-test. python3 tools/validate-upstream.py --relay-api --output artifacts/my-relay-check runs nine external probes plus relay API checks and exports four relay/frame-{1,2}-{top,bottom}.ppm reference images. Compiler/target checks include Clang and emulated big-endian PPC Linux; none is physical Wii U evidence.

All Wii U builds embed direct-display and relay self-tests. Y's standard HID/GSP mode now runs the original queued guest. SD logs record relay registration, VBlank, coalesced intervals, dropped IRQs, faults and clean shutdown. See console-testing.md for physical checks and reference images.

Public interface facts were checked against pinned libctru 9b55eda44cf80b971503991e0c78f9bc8fe50425 (gspgpu.h/c, gfx.c). No upstream implementation was copied. Later runtime work supplies the scoped service threads, address arbitration and standalone graphics startup used by the original compiler-built applications. Version 0.17 adds synchronous GX DMA, fills, display transfers and raw texture copies; see gx-transfers.md. Physical/VRAM address translation, PICA rendering and guest DSP/audio remain unimplemented. Private diagnostic saves are described in filesystem.md. Wider shared runtime development can continue without a ROM; exact Mario requirements and physical acceptance still need private intake and console results.
