docs.title: Controlled NCCH guest execution (0.2.0)
docs.text: This original, redistributable ARM fixture is the first executable guest pipeline: NCCH inspection and hash checks → checked segment extraction → original generated C → portable guest loader/SVC runtime → raw TV/GamePad framebuffer presentation. Desktop execution and Wii U cross-compilation pass. Physical Wii U execution is awaiting testing. This fixture uses an explicit harness I/O contract; it is not a stock 3DS graphical application and does not implement HID, GSP or PICA.

docs.title: Reproduce from source
docs.text:
Use Python 3.12+, native GCC for desktop execution, and the installed official devkitPPC/WUT SDK for console builds. Run from the complete source root:

python3 -m host make-fixture --output "artifacts/original guest"
python3 -m host run-fixture "artifacts/original guest/ctr2wup-guest.cxi" --output "artifacts/guest AOT" --frames 2 --buttons 1 --touch --touch-x 100 --touch-y 80
python3 -m host run-fixture "artifacts/original guest/ctr2wup-guest.cxi" --output "artifacts/guest interpreted" --frames 2 --buttons 1 --touch --touch-x 100 --touch-y 80 --mode interpreter
python3 -m host build "artifacts/original guest/ctr2wup-guest.cxi" --target guest-fixture --output "artifacts/guest console"

Each output directory must be new. Failure preserves compiler/execution logs and removes incomplete staging. run-fixture writes real guest-generated top.ppm (400×240), bottom.ppm (320×240), generated C, the native runner, logs and a JSON report. The installed wheel includes the bounded translator, but C compilation requires the full source; set CTR2WUP_PROJECT_ROOT to that source root.

tools/generate-guest.py deliberately regenerates the tracked original fixture sources after fixture changes. Console builds compare these sources against the inspected input and reject stale results. Setup does not regenerate source. Only the exact original code, segment layout and program ID are execution-enabled. Unknown commercial/homebrew profiles fail before publishing an output.

docs.title: Guest loading and I/O contract
docs.text:
The unsigned, decrypted NCCH v2 has program ID 000400000ff00f02, 340 bytes of ARM text at 0x00100000, one 4 KiB data page at 0x08000000, and 691,200 bytes of BSS for framebuffers. Text is read/execute, rodata is read-only, data/BSS and stack/TLS are read/write. Padding/BSS, the 16 KiB stack below 0x10000000, and the TLS page at 0x1ff82000 are zeroed. Initial SP is 0x10000000; entry uses user ARM mode. No guest pointer becomes a host pointer. Allocation is bounded to 64 MiB; page alignment, descriptor sizes, permissions, overlaps and wraparound are checked. Non-page-aligned data/BSS layouts are explicitly rejected for now. The TLS page exists; v0.6.0 implements its user read-only CP15 access and a separate original SRV/CFG startup probe. See shared-services.md; the framebuffer contract below still uses harness input and is not HID/GSP.

Data-page offset Harness/guest meaning 0 Host supplies buttons; bit0 changes the top framebuffer color 4, 8, 12 Host supplies touch X, Y and active flag; guest checks bounds 16 Guest increments completed-frame count after writing both buffers 20 Host requests exit; guest calls ExitProcess at its next loop entry 32 Original debug message for OutputDebugString

Top pixels begin at 0x08001000; bottom pixels follow 400×240 RGBA8 pixels. The ARM program fills both images with STR loops, writes a white touch pixel, increments its frame count, sleeps for 1 ms and repeats. Presentation reads little-endian pixels through checked mappings and converts them to the host's RGBA representation. These addresses are a fixture contract, not emulated 3DS shared-memory/HID/GSP addresses. No GPU draw commands are executed.

docs.title: Implemented SVC subset
docs.text:
One guest CPU/thread runs under instruction quotas; callers supply monotonic virtual time in nanoseconds. No host thread is created for a guest thread.

SVC Implemented behavior/register contract 03 ExitProcess Guest enters exited state 0a SleepThread r0:r1 nanoseconds; zero yields, positive sleeps; negative/overflow faults 17 CreateEvent Reset type r1: OneShot0 or Sticky1; result r0, handle r1; Pulse unsupported 18 SignalEvent Handle r0, result r0; wakes the controlled waiter 19 ClearEvent Handle r0, result r0 23 CloseHandle Handle r0, result r0; retains objects owned by other handles/waiter 24 WaitSynchronization1 Handle r0, timeout r2:r3; zero polls, positive times out, negative waits indefinitely 27 DuplicateHandle Input handle r1, result r0, new handle r1 28 GetSystemTick Virtual time scaled to 268,111,856 Hz; low/high r0:r1 2d ConnectToPort Bounded srv: name at r1; result/typed session handle r0/r1 32 SendSyncRequest Checked TLS IPC; restricted SRV registration/CFG configuration reads 3d OutputDebugString Checked pointer r0, length r1, maximum 256 bytes; success result r0=0

There are 32 event objects and 64 generation-tagged handles. Stale/closed handles, timeouts and exhaustion return explicit results. Unknown SVCs fault visibly. v0.6.0 adds 16 session objects sharing the handle table; event/session operations are type checked. Multi-thread scheduling, timers, memory-control SVCs, general IPC and FS/APT/HID/GSP remain unimplemented. Only the CFG reads in shared-services.md are implemented. Interface facts were checked against audited research sources and the public libctru SVC header; their implementation was not copied.

docs.title: Console controls and expected evidence
docs.text:
Launch ctr2wup-guest-fixture.wuhb with a compatible Aroma setup or the RPX with an RPX-capable launcher. It starts in guest mode. The native diagnostic also contains this guest; Y toggles modes. Plus restarts the guest; B asks the guest to exit; Minus exits the host application. A changes the next guest top color and plays the native test tone. A calibrated touch changes the bottom color and draws one white guest pixel. Hold A/touch through a completed guest frame.

The TV has a small host status overlay; the remaining image and GamePad image come from guest ARM memory writes. Quotas allow 50,000 guest instructions per display iteration, so a full guest frame spans multiple display iterations. This deliberately bounded correctness test does not measure game performance. Record both outputs, increasing guest frame count, successful color/touch/exit/ restart, and sd:/ctr2wup/native-*.log; follow console-testing.md.

docs.title: Verified desktop evidence
docs.text:
Two AOT frames with button1 and touch(100,80) execute 1,382,534 guest instructions, zero fallback instructions, four SVCs and one debug message, then exit normally. Top RGB is 10 bb 22; bottom RGB is 77 22 bb, with a white touch pixel. Interpreter and AOT frames have identical SHA-256 values:

top.ppm     267878f6f7665b30bf43465c48d9b55094e8fe7d8fc694585e1afe74c30bae81
bottom.ppm  6cadca972cf65a4842d8d8a73bd6a4b806bf1706a2c5b826cd136d21a371d06d

The original fixture SHA-256 is 004d03a5a0eca2679f2efbf6f887590fbf51ed984649056e78702c43af968210. The separate executable revision is 38820d9091dcf0eb863b5c74c04536c9e765aaf39f4719f017205298015a3472. Kernel/loader tests cover faults, events, sleeps, ticks and actual interpreter/AOT guest state/memory matches, both normally and under ASan/UBSan. All hardware, stock 3DS homebrew, commercial gameplay, saves and WUP claims remain open.

The separate v0.7.0 original heap lifecycle probe exercises real memory SVCs without extending this framebuffer harness contract. All three RPXs embed its original interpreter/AOT self-test; external AOT is also verified on desktop and emulated PPC. See guest-memory.md and collect the additional native-mode result per console-testing.md. GPU/DSP physical memory and broader boot remain pending.

Maintained source: docs/guest-fixture.md · 1b14ea67cba6. GitHub source and issue links may require repository access.

docs.title: Shared guest memory management
docs.text:
v0.13 places BSS directly after initialized DATA, including its last page's unused tail, and copies no ExeFS padding into BSS. A separate read-only synthetic kernel configuration page at 1ff80000 supplies documented HLE policy; it counts toward backing limits. Thread stacks pin owned allocations until their guest context exits, and eight 512-byte TLS slots share the original TLS page. See guest-threads.md; no retail firmware image or cross-process mapping is supplied.

v0.14.6 adds a separate read-only shared time page at 1ff81000. Its double-bank milliseconds/tick-frequency/tick-offset reference advances with the guest clock from an explicitly synthetic Unix-zero epoch. Ordinary unmodified libctru time queries can run; actual RTC/timezone/full firmware config is not supplied. This page adds 4 KiB to loader backing/quota accounting; the minimal thread fixture now owns 36 KiB rather than 32 KiB. Both host and portable loaders reject segment collisions and include the allocation in their bounds.

Version 0.7.0 advances M3/P3 with ControlMemory (SVC 1) and QueryMemory (SVC 2). It does not enable a commercial profile. This is original C11 code with checked little-endian accesses and no guest-to-host pointer casts. Public interface values/register conventions were checked against libctru 9b55eda44cf80b971503991e0c78f9bc8fe50425 (svc.h/svc.s); the already-audited Azahar source supplied semantic comparisons. No upstream implementation was copied.

docs.title: Supported contract
docs.text:
ControlMemory receives operation in r0, address in r1, source address in r2, page-aligned size in r3 and permissions in r4. It returns Result in r0 and the allocated/affected guest address in r1. Errors clear r1 and leave mappings and owned backing unchanged. Other registers remain intact.

Operation Supported behavior ALLOC 3 Zero-filled owned heap allocation; address 0 selects the first free page range, or use a specified free address ALLOC_LINEAR 0x10003 Same checked CPU allocation in the Old-family linear window; reports Continuous state FREE 1 Remove a fully owned mapped range, including a subrange or adjacent owned allocations; permissions must be 0 PROT 6 Enforce permissions on an owned range, splitting mappings at page boundaries Application region flag 0x100 Accepted with the supported operations

Heap addresses occupy [0x08000000,0x10000000) and Old-family linear addresses [0x14000000,0x1c000000). Allocation skips existing image/stack mappings. Addresses and sizes must be page aligned; sizes must be nonzero. Source address must be zero. Permissions 0/1/2/3 mean inaccessible/read/write/read-write; execute and other flags return an error. Reads/writes enforce permissions in every backend. FREE/PROT cannot mutate loader-owned image, stack or TLS mappings, even inside the heap window. Partial operations preflight the full range and fragment capacity before publishing a change.

QueryMemory receives address in r2 and returns r0 Result, r1 base, r2 size, r3 permissions, r4 state and r5 page flags. It reports the containing logical region, merging adjacent regions with equal state and permissions. A region may include immutable loader pages and mutable heap pages: its query result does not authorize FREE/PROT of the entire extent. Gaps report Free state 0/permissions 0. Image text/rodata report Code 4, data/heap Private 5, linear Continuous 7, stack/TLS Locked 11. Page flags are 0; physical-page attributes are unavailable. Queries outside [0,0x40000000) return an address error and clear r1-r5. No host pointer is returned.

Misaligned address/size, invalid combination, invalid address/state and resource exhaustion return nonzero Result codes (e0e01bf1, e0e01bf2, e0e01bee, e0e01bf5, e0a01bf5, d86007f3). Exact precedence and unsupported combinations are a scoped HLE contract, not full retail-kernel conformance. Request/failure counts and last operation/address/result remain in ctr_guest for diagnosis.

docs.title: Capacity, ownership and translation
docs.text:
There are 16 owned allocations and 32 mapping fragments, with a combined 64 MiB retained-backing limit including image/BSS/stack/TLS. Partial free retains the original host allocation until its last mapped byte is removed; all its backing remains charged. Removed pages can be allocated again with new zeroed storage. Final free and guest close release ownership. Fragment exhaustion fails atomically. These limits need revisiting against actual title requirements and Wii U costs.

Non-executable mapping changes advance the memory/exclusive generation without invalidating unchanged executable snapshots. Adding/removing executable mappings, changing execute protection and writes through executable aliases still invalidate AOT. Dynamic heap management therefore preserves normal translated execution.

Linear backing is contiguous for checked CPU accesses only. FCRAM physical addresses, GPU/DSP allocation, cache/coherency support and the GX2 memory bridge are absent. MAP/UNMAP aliases, RESERVE, system/base regions, New-family linear windows and unknown flags stop visibly as unsupported. Image reprotection, multi-thread ownership, physical accounting and broader kernel behavior remain unfinished.

docs.title: Original execution evidence
docs.text:
host/heap_fixture.py generates an original NCCH with 151 ARM instructions. It allocates three heap pages, writes little-endian values, queries the region, protects the middle page read-only, reads it, restores permissions and frees it. It queries/reallocates that hole, verifies zeroed memory, allocates/queries linear memory and frees all backing before exit: 14 memory requests plus ExitProcess. Independent expected SVC outputs accompany full state/memory comparisons.

make -C tests/heap check sanitize checks the real ARM lifecycle, guard/write-only permissions, static-page ownership, overlap/overflow, holes, retained-backing budget, slot/fragment exhaustion and atomic failures. tests/recomp/test_heap.c compares actual external AOT, original AOT and interpreter CPU/mapping/backing state at 1/7/23 instruction budgets. It also checks guest-store fault PCs on protected/freed pages, zero fallback and preserved executable generations.

All three Wii U builds embed the original interpreter/AOT self-test. Native mode displays GUEST HEAP LIFECYCLE PASS CODE 0; SD logs record heap_selftest PASS result=0, or an exact FAIL code. The external-AOT heap probe is a desktop/emulated-PPC test, separate from the console guest program. Physical behavior/timings, native Windows and conventional 3DS homebrew boot remain pending. STATUS.md records current report paths.

v0.8.0 pins source allocations used by shared-memory objects; FREE/PROT rejects those allocations until final release. Owned shared backing uses the combined budget. See kernel-objects.md.

Maintained source: docs/guest-memory.md · 1b14ea67cba6. GitHub source and issue links may require repository access.

docs.title: Single-core guest threads
docs.text:
Version 0.13 adds eight process-local thread slots, including the initial thread. Each holds ARM registers/CPSR, 32 raw VFP words/FPSCR, a separate 512-byte TLS slot, waits and deadlines. One emulated CPU executes strict priorities 0x18..0x3f; equal priorities rotate after 32 instructions. Host budget changes do not restart the quantum. Context switches invalidate the exclusive monitor. This is not SMP, priority inheritance, complete affinity or a full 3DS kernel.

Implemented thread SVCs are CreateThread (08), ExitThread (09), GetThreadPriority (0b), SetThreadPriority (0c) and GetThreadId (37). Core 0/default -2/any -1 use the single emulated CPU; other explicit cores are rejected. Entry permissions, alignment, stack and capacity are checked before allocation. Heap stack backing is pinned until exit. IDs and handle generations prevent stale slot reuse. Closing a handle cannot kill a running thread. Terminated objects survive retained handles and waiters; waits can join them. ExitProcess terminates every thread.

Mutexes track their owning thread and recursive depth. Wrong-owner releases fail; closing a locked handle retains its object, and owner exit releases its locks. Events, mutexes, semaphores and thread joins support existing wait-one/any/all and timeouts across contexts. Process-local address arbiters (21/22) support signal, signed wait/decrement and timed forms; wait references survive handle closure. No cross-process arbitration or kernel priority inheritance is claimed.

The local process resource-limit object (38/39/3a) exposes the runtime's actual bounded memory/thread/object quotas for IDs 0..8. Query lists are fully checked before any output writes. Timers remain unavailable (quota zero); CPU-time quota and other processes are unsupported. A synthetic read-only kernel configuration page at 1ff80000 supplies compatibility version 2.58.0, application budget and single-system-core fields needed by libctru startup. These values are HLE policy, not measurements or a firmware image. Other configuration fields remain zero.

The checked loader places BSS immediately after initialized DATA, including the unused tail of its last page. ExeFS padding never overwrites BSS. Tests cover non-page-aligned DATA, allocation bounds and conflicts with reserved mappings.

CPU additions required by compiled startup are ARM UADD8/USUB8/SEL and GE flags, SMLAxy with signed halfwords/sticky Q, VMRS/VMSR FPSCR transport, checked scalar VLDR/VSTR for S0..31/D0..15, ARM STM's PC+8 source value and user CP15 ARMv6 DMB/DSB ordering. Interpreter and original AOT transport floating-point words; they do not implement general VFP arithmetic. External AOT preserves FP contexts and rejects unsupported arithmetic/control modes before effects. Cache-maintenance operations and unimplemented forms still fail visibly. Barriers order checked CPU backing; they do not complete PICA work.

make -C tests/threads check sanitize tests context ownership, scheduling across host budgets, joins, failure rollback, stack pins, references, address arbitration and quota output preflight. The original three-thread fixture executes 345 instructions, 22 SVCs and eight switches with three-backend state/memory parity. All diagnostic RPX/WUHB variants embed its interpreter/original-AOT self-test. Separate external AOT probes check media instructions/barriers and two threads' VFP arithmetic/FPSCR isolation. compiled-homebrew.md records real libctru tests. Every physical Wii U result remains pending.

Maintained source: docs/guest-threads.md · 1b14ea67cba6. GitHub source and issue links may require repository access.

docs.title: Windows GUI and injection workflow
docs.text: Final product specification, finalized 2026-10-07. The user explicitly selected UWUVCI AIO as the workflow reference. The shipped product is a Windows GUI named CTR2WUP.exe. The CLI is the internal/testable build engine; the standard user flow runs entirely through the GUI.

docs.title: Reviewed reference
docs.text:
Reviewed UWUVCI AIO WPF at commit d03b559bbac53642506557519108e5967d5fbd25. The source shows:

  • System navigation in UI/Windows/MenuWindow.xaml.
  • Three groups in UI/Frames/InjectFrame.xaml: BaseRom, Configuration, Packing; packing exposes a “WUP Installable” button after injection.
  • ROM selection, game name, icon/TV/GamePad artwork, image creation and an “Inject” action in UI/Frames/InjectFrames/Configurations/OtherConfigs.xaml.
  • Configuration import/export, output-path settings, asynchronous injection and packing, progress and completion UI.

This was a source/workflow review, not a Windows execution test. Its README lists DS/GBA/N64/SNES/NES/TurboGrafx/MSX/Wii/GCN, without 3DS support. Its source is GPLv3; no code, artwork or binary was imported into CTR2WUP. It supplies the interaction reference. CTR2WUP supplies the new 3DS AOT/HLE/GX2 runtime and uses its own original Wii U title template instead of a commercial VC donor base.

docs.title: Main user flow
docs.text:
1. Open CTR2WUP → 3DS Inject. The injector page is the default destination; navigation also provides saved projects, settings and help.
  2. Choose the game. Browse for a .3ds/.cxi or supported base-application .cia. Accept already-decrypted input, or offer Import keys from your 3DS when the detected encryption needs local material. The setup wizard explains supported console-export steps, imports selected files and shows missing requirements. Decrypt locally and validate before continuing. Display detected title, icon, region/revision and supported/experimental/unsupported status. Provide an actionable reason when the input cannot be injected. Automatically select the supported compatibility preset for the exact revision.
  3. Configure the injection. Edit the Wii U Menu title; preview or choose icon, TV boot and GamePad boot artwork. Use original default artwork when needed. Default to top screen on TV, bottom screen/touch on GamePad, native resolution and aspect-preserving scaling. Offer only implemented display options.
  4. Choose WUP output. Select a destination and review readiness. The app detects/provisions documented prerequisites through a first-run setup flow. Routine injection requires no manual compiler commands or shell session.
  5. Click Inject. One primary action runs game preparation, translation, compilation, runtime/assets staging, metadata creation, WUP packing and validation. Display the actual stage, elapsed time, progress and Cancel. Detailed logs and technical settings live in expandable diagnostics/settings. Decryption runs as a preparation stage; it does not require a separate game conversion action. Console key values never enter reports or WUP output.
  6. Receive the finished WUP. Show the completed package directory, title information, build report and installation guide. Offer Open output folder and an explicit Copy to SD action if implemented. Publish success only after the real package pipeline passes its checks.
  7. Install and launch on Wii U. The user installs with the documented compatible homebrew installer/environment and launches the new per-game title from the Wii U Menu. The Windows app creates the WUP; installation remains a console step with recorded test evidence.

The visible term Inject includes all of CTR2WUP's conversion work. A user selecting a supported game should receive its installable per-game WUP through that action. RPX diagnostics, generated C and intermediate staging are development artifacts, distinct from the completed user output.

docs.title: State and persistence
docs.text:
The injector follows: Choose game → Configure → Ready → Injecting → Complete, with actionable Failed/Cancelled states. Unsupported games remain visibly unsupported; experimental status requires an actual available conversion path. Readiness includes the input/profile, toolchain, output space and required local packaging configuration. Progress and cancellation come from the shared engine.

Save/import/export an injection project containing selected input identity, settings, artwork paths and destination, keeping user-derived data private. Rebuild uses the same per-game identity and preserves existing saves. Auto-assigned title identities are stable and collision-checked; advanced overrides are validated. Installation instructions identify the supported console environment.

Implement the GUI in C# WPF on a supported .NET LTS release. Its engine interface uses versioned requests, stage events and reports. Document/provision all real Windows dependencies, and keep keys in local settings with redacted diagnostics.

docs.title: GUI acceptance
docs.text: A clean Windows machine can open CTR2WUP.exe, select the supported commercial revision, configure title/artwork/output, click Inject, cancel/retry when needed, and obtain a validated WUP without undocumented tools or hand-editing files. That WUP installs and launches from the Wii U Menu and passes the agreed gameplay, input/touch/audio/save/reload/rebuild test. The app stays responsive during the entire conversion. Its completion message distinguishes validated package output from previously recorded physical-console compatibility evidence.

docs.title: October 12 encrypted-input amendment
docs.text:
The user asks for both decrypted input and local decryption using their own 3DS material. The shared engine now implements the scoped preparation/import path in encrypted-input.md. The eventual GUI includes import/remove/reselect key storage and guided export help, with optional on-console companion integration only after hardware/tool validation. The Windows app cannot read keys directly from a stock console over USB. An imported key set may need title keys/seeds; one console-specific SD key is not a universal standalone-ROM key.

Acceptance adds real locally exported keys plus an owned encrypted fixture, recovered-code/asset integrity, missing/wrong-key messages, cancellation/cleanup, protected Windows storage and redacted diagnostics. No key is bundled, fetched, uploaded, included in exported projects or shipped in WUPs. Preparation success does not override a game's unsupported profile or physical compatibility gate. The GUI remains unimplemented until the underlying commercial pipeline works.

Maintained source: docs/gui-workflow.md · 1b14ea67cba6. GitHub source and issue links may require repository access.

docs.title: Guided Wii U tests and TXT results (0.14.6)
docs.text: The kit contains five original homebrew diagnostics, supplied as WUHB and RPX. No ROM is required. The current round is the short save and result-file check, followed by Compiled RomFS. The user reports that Native, Guarded AOT and Compiled AOT completed on 0.14.5; their ten-minute guides need not be repeated for this round.

docs.title: Launch
docs.text:
For Aroma, copy the kit's sd-card/ contents to the SD root. Apps belong in sd:/wiiu/apps/. An RPX-capable launcher can use the matching rpx/ files. Keep the existing sd:/ctr2wup/ folder and saves. Use your current launcher.

Each app displays BUILD 0.14.6, RESULT VERIFIED and its new filename. VERIFIED means the current 4 KiB TXT was closed and compared byte for byte after reopening. It does not prove survival of sudden power loss. The separate TRACE SAVING / FAILED status describes the longer trace, not the result file. A trace failure is captured in the result. RESULT STORAGE FAILED / SD ERROR pauses the guest; exit with Minus and report the operation/number and any files.

docs.title: Prompts
docs.text:
• Button/stick/touch inputs, guest PASS/exit and save reload are checked automatically.
  • R confirms the displayed picture, alignment, sound or stability observation; L marks a problem. These are labeled user evidence.
  • ZL skips a step as NOT TESTED; ZR marks a problem and advances.
  • Minus ends the test and writes the available summary. Unfinished steps stay NOT TESTED. Results are also written at startup and throughout execution.
  • Use Plus when prompted for guest restart/save reload. Y/unscheduled Plus remain reserved while a guide is active.

Only Native plays the platform tone on A. Compiled apps use A as guest input and implement no guest audio. The interactive A prompt waits for a fresh decoded green frame before allowing R and records latency separately from confirmation. Native and interactive full guides include a ten-minute observation interval; its completion is separate from the user's final stability confirmation.

Compiled Save preserves the existing diagnostic snapshot, checks its own guest save/reload and asks for Plus. It may request one exit/relaunch for a fresh-process check. Compiled RomFS automatically checks original asset reads and exits after one step. No photo is needed to report these software checks.

docs.title: Files to return
docs.text:
All reports are under sd:/ctr2wup/:

result-native-0.14.6-<ticks>-<suffix>.txt
result-compiled-interactive-0.14.6-<ticks>-<suffix>.txt
result-compiled-guarded-0.14.6-<ticks>-<suffix>.txt
result-compiled-save-0.14.6-<ticks>-<suffix>.txt
result-compiled-romfs-0.14.6-<ticks>-<suffix>.txt

These fixed-size plain-text results contain named PASS / FAIL / NOT TESTED guide outcomes and their evidence, build/session identity, embedded-check status, guest instructions/PC/fault/fallback, input counters, green-response latency, diagnostic frame timing, save load/commit status and full-trace errors. Trailing space padding is intentional. Later updates verify the reserved file identity; missing or replaced reports are not silently recreated. Per-launch exclusive names preserve older results.

The separate longer traces use native-*.txt, compiled-interactive-*.txt, compiled-guarded-*.txt, compiled-save-*.txt and compiled-romfs-*.txt. Their successful commits sync/close/flush the SD volume. Neither a cleanup marker nor a saved result proves that the launcher finished returning; add that observation.

Upload the new result TXT and any matching full trace in this chat, directly or in a ZIP below 32 MiB. For save testing, include the snapshot and any .pending / .previous siblings, preserving the originals. If nothing exists, say so and include the short on-screen storage error. See console-retest.md for this round. The console environment, launcher version, SD format/capacity and TV resolution help when diagnosing failures; do not resend already supplied details.

Local tests verify report write/read-back, failed/missing/replaced-file handling, interrupted process evidence, guide outcomes and lifecycle ordering. Builds use the actual Wii U SDK. v0.14.6 result persistence and save updates are awaiting physical evidence. These diagnostics do not verify PICA, guest audio, retail saves, Mario gameplay or WUP installation.

Maintained source: docs/guided-testing.md · 1b14ea67cba6. GitHub source and issue links may require repository access.

docs.title: GSP command queue and CPU-backed GX transfers (0.18.0)
docs.text: This M3/M4 foundation lets ordinary libctru GX calls clear/copy/convert buffers through the standard shared command ring. It supplies no PICA draw renderer or native GX2 transfer acceleration. No game patch or commercial data is involved.

docs.title: Supported boundary
docs.text:
Client ID0 uses the retained 4 KiB relay page, 15 32-byte command slots at 0x820 and the header at 0x800. TriggerCmdReqQueue requires the owning registered GSP session and GPU right. Commands commit synchronously in order, advancing index/ count only after successful execution. A failed command and its later entries remain pending, with a visible guest fault; any successful prefix stays committed. Documented stop/should-stop states are retained, not silently erased.

Command Supported behavior Current limits DMA (0) Staged byte copy and DMA completion Nonempty, at most 4 MiB Memory fill (2) 16/24/32-bit LE repeating pattern, either/both banks Trigger required; 8-byte endpoints; whole patterns; at most 4 MiB per bank Display transfer (3) All five display formats, linear/tiled/same layout, vertical flip Equal dimensions in 1..1024; tiled multiples of 8; no scaling/crop/raw-display copy Texture copy (4) Raw copy with independent 16-byte-unit line widths/gaps Flags8, lengths in whole 16-byte units; bounded spans; gaps preserved Cache regions (5) Checked coherent CPU-backed ranges and barrier No asynchronous GPU/DSP cache model PICA command list (1) Finalized raw viewport/scissor configuration and P3D completion All draws, shaders/uploads and other register state remain unsupported; see the contract

DMA accepts the virtual addresses defined by the GSP command wire. This is not a general physical/VRAM translator. All source/destination spans, permissions, alignment, arithmetic and allocations are checked before each command changes bytes. Staging makes guest overlap safe. Device output may not alias relay backing, including through another mapping. Bulk byte APIs validate complete ranges across adjacent mappings and update exclusive/code generations, including executable storage aliases; caller-owned host buffers cannot alias guest storage.

PSC0/PSC1/PPF/DMA completions use the standard relay interrupt ring. A two-bank fill sends one PSC0, following the pinned Azahar behavior; Zakuro's two-IRQ variant is not assumed equivalent. Full rings retain drop/error accounting and do not signal an event for an interrupt that was not enqueued. CPU-backed timing is synchronous; actual hardware latency, cache/coherency and scheduling accuracy remain unverified.

docs.title: Original application and verification
docs.text:
tests/homebrew/transfer.c uses stock CRT/libctru GX APIs. It checks both/single fill banks, raw copy with asymmetric gaps and untouched gap bytes, cache regions, DMA bytes, tiled RGBA8 -> linear RGB565 conversion, and green/red/green top with blue bottom images. It waits through standard PSC/PPF/DMA/VBlank events, then unmounts/exits through ordinary library code.

Its checked AOT run exits after 1,489,172 instructions, zero fallback, 17 GX operations (3 DMA, 8 fill, 3 display, 1 texture copy, 1 cache, 1 PICA setup), and exact three-frame pixel checks. Three deliberately unavailable startup services remain recorded. C normal/sanitizer checks cover failure atomicity, permissions, aliases, generations, queue wrap/stop/prefix behavior, malformed headers and full interrupts. The image matrix compares 400 original vectors across C/Python and pinned external color/Morton primitives; emulated big-endian PPC hashes match. The external full transfer engine and physical Wii U were not executed by those reference comparisons. Required checks and WUT builds are recorded separately.

docs.title: Optional console round
docs.text:
The 0.18.0 kit places ctr2wup-libctru-transfer.wuhb in sd-card/wiiu/apps/. Copy the contents of sd-card to SD root and launch CTR2WUP GX Transfers 0.18.0 in Aroma. This test needs no ROM, key or extra blob.

  1. Watch the TV change green/red/green with a blue GamePad image. The guide asks R for the observed picture or L for a problem. Do not confirm a picture you did not observe; faults/skips stay distinct.
  2. The app checks the guest's own GX PASS and exit automatically. Press Minus when complete and separately report whether it returned to Menu/launcher.

Results are under sd:/ctr2wup/, named result-compiled-gx-transfer-0.18.0-*.txt, plus any full trace. They include operation counts and the last GX command/fault. ZIP those TXT files together and attach the ZIP to a console-result issue or the development conversation. Preserve existing saves/reports. Completed long native/input guides need not be repeated. Actual SD/lifecycle/pictures and console timings remain pending until that round.

The v0.18 fixture also submits an original libctru-built no-draw PICA configuration list and waits for P3D. Its TXT report includes PICA list/write/finalizer counts and parser diagnostics. Picture and launcher confirmations remain separate; these pictures still come from fills/transfers, not a PICA draw renderer.

Maintained source: docs/gx-transfers.md · 1b14ea67cba6. GitHub source and issue links may require repository access.

docs.title: Standard HID input subset (0.9.0)
docs.text:
The reusable runtime advertises hid:USER through SRV. GetHandles request 000a0000 replies with header 000a0047, result0, copy descriptor 14000000 and six typed handles: one shared page and Pad0/Pad1/accelerometer/gyroscope/debug events. The latter three events have no producer. Motion enable/disable and all other HID commands fail visibly. hid:SPVR, IRRST and New-family input are absent.

The device owns six internal handles for its lifetime; requests return independent copies. Initialization and copy exhaustion roll back allocations. The shared page has read-only guest rights; its mapping, copies and waiters obey the checked kernel lifetime rules. Closing a returned handle cannot destroy the device's backing.

ctr_hid_update publishes Old-family physical button bits 0..11, signed Circle Pad axes in -156..156, and valid touch coordinates in 320x240. Circle Pad direction bits 28..31 use a radius40 threshold and diagonal sectors. Touch bit20 is derived by the client from the touch entry, as in the public interface. ZL/ZR, C-stick, accelerometer, gyro, raw analog calibration and slider are unsupported. Invalid buttons, axes, touched coordinates and nonincreasing timestamps cause no update.

The eight-entry little-endian pad ring has index at 10, current buttons at 1c and 16-byte entries from 28: held, added, removed, packed signed XY. The touch index is at b8; eight-byte entries from c8 contain packed unsigned XY and validity. Both indexes advance together. On index0 wrap, current/previous reset timestamps at 0/8 and a8/b0 use the 268111856 Hz guest tick scale. Pad0 and Pad1 one-shot events signal after publication. The single guest runs on the same host thread, so publication has no concurrent partial reader. Multi-thread device timing and physical 3DS equivalence require further evidence.

The original ARM consumer in host/hid_fixture.py reads TLS, registers SRV, acquires HID handles, maps the page read-only, waits for Pad0, reads the standard rings and writes a diagnostic snapshot. Two controlled updates followed by unmap/handle cleanup/exit execute 185 instructions and 18 SVCs. Interpreter, original AOT and actual external AOT match registers, mapped memory, shared bytes, object references and event state at uneven instruction budgets, with zero fallback. The external comparison has 858 assertions; 336 API assertions check wire replies, read-only rights, transitions, wrap timestamps, validation and resource rollback. GCC/sanitizer, Clang and emulated big-endian PPC results do not prove console input.

All three Wii U builds embed hid_selftest and a separate live original-AOT ARM consumer. VPAD buttons map to physical 3DS bits, the left stick scales to ±156, and calibrated touch passes through the checked bottom-screen viewport. In native mode, ARM HID, ARM CIRCLE, ARM TOUCH and sample counts show values read by ARM through shared memory, rather than direct host input. SD logs contain HID live state=... and hid_live_shutdown. Diagnostic Y/Plus/Minus remain host controls; Minus exits before publishing its press. The right stick is displayed by native diagnostics but is not exposed as a New-family C-stick.

Reproduce with make -C tests/hid check sanitize, tools/generate-hid-fixture.py and tools/validate-upstream.py --hid-api --output artifacts/my-hid-checks. Interface facts were checked against devkitPro/libctru commit 9b55eda44cf80b971503991e0c78f9bc8fe50425, services/hid.h, services/hid.c and IPC descriptor definitions. The implementation and fixture are original. This does not claim conventional graphical homebrew boot or Mario compatibility.

Maintained source: docs/hid-input.md · 1b14ea67cba6. GitHub source and issue links may require repository access.

docs.title: Shared memory and synchronization
docs.text:
Version 0.8.0 adds original C11 objects needed by HID/GSP-style startup. Public SVC register interfaces were checked against pinned libctru svc.h/svc.s; no upstream implementation is copied. The original v0.8 fixture is single-thread; v0.13 extends ownership/waits to eight process-local contexts (guest-threads.md). This remains a single-process subset, not full retail-kernel behavior or a commercial profile.

Interface Implemented behavior CreateMemoryBlock 1e r0 other rights/r1 source/r2 size/r3 own rights; r0 Result/r1 handle. Zero source creates local zeroed backing; nonzero pins one contiguous owned RW heap allocation MapMemoryBlock 1f r0 handle/r1 destination/r2 own rights/r3 other rights; checked local aliases in [10000000,14000000) UnmapMemoryBlock 20 r0 handle/r1 exact mapped address; removes mapping/releases reference CreateMutex 13 / ReleaseMutex 14 Initially locked/unlocked; recursive acquisition by the sole thread; checked release CreateSemaphore 15 / ReleaseSemaphore 16 Nonnegative initial count, positive signed maximum, bounded release and old count in r1 WaitSynchronization 24 Event/mutex/semaphore acquisition, consumption, timeout/deferred wait WaitSynchronizationN 25 Up to 16 checked handles; wait-any index/atomic wait-all. r0 timeout low/r1 array/r2 count/r3 all/r4 timeout high

Typed objects share the existing 64-slot generation-tagged handle table. Pools allow 8 shared objects, 16 mutexes, 16 semaphores and the existing events/sessions. Shared objects allow four mappings each within the 32-fragment memory limit. Owned shared backing shares the combined 64 MiB budget; pinned heap is charged once. Guest close frees owned shared backing and heap storage.

Shared aliases enforce rights: own permissions must be a subset of object rights; other permissions must match policy or DONTCARE 10000000. Only none/read/write/ read-write are supported. Failed mapping changes neither published memory nor references. Mapped objects survive closing their last handle until unmapping or process close. A source allocation cannot be freed/reprotected while an object pins it; final release removes the pin. This conservative rule pins the whole original allocation. Aliases report QueryMemory Shared state 6. Foreign processes, rights transfer and GPU/DSP physical backing remain absent.

Waits retain objects independently of handle closure. Wait-any consumes the first ready object in caller order. Wait-all preflights every object before acquiring any and returns index ffffffff; timeout returns the same index. Duplicate objects in wait-all are rejected explicitly; wait-any duplicates are accepted. Invalid handles/arrays/counts fail without consuming objects. Polling/external event signals resume the sole waiter deterministically. Negative timeout values are infinite; finite deadline overflow is rejected. Mutex ownership belongs to the sole guest thread, so acquisition while owned is recursive. Priority inheritance, other-thread ownership, pulse events, address arbitration and multi-thread scheduling remain unfinished.

host/kernel_fixture.py generates 148 original ARM instructions using 27 SVCs. It allocates/pins heap memory, maps/reads a read-only shared alias, duplicates/ closes handles, acquires/releases a mutex, consumes/releases a semaphore, checks timeout and wait-any indexes, then releases all backing/objects and exits. Expected outputs and interpreter/original/external AOT state/memory are checked. make -C tests/kernel check sanitize covers lifetimes, pins, permissions, wrong/ stale handles, wake/timeout/close while waiting, atomic wait-all and exhaustion/ rollback. External validation adds the real lifter probe; --kernel-api adds the API suite to a compiler/target run.

All three Wii U builds embed the original interpreter/AOT self-test: native mode SHARED/SYNC LIFECYCLE PASS CODE 0, SD log kernel_selftest PASS result=0, or a specific FAIL code. Console/native Windows evidence is still required. See STATUS.md for current reports.

Maintained source: docs/kernel-objects.md · 1b14ea67cba6. GitHub source and issue links may require repository access.

docs.title: Launch music check (0.20.0)
docs.text:
The latest Save, RomFS, SD asset and GX tests passed their scoped checks. The follow-up Save trace confirms persistence across closing and reopening the app. Those checks do not need repeating. See the evidence review.

The Wii U launch sound continued throughout the apps. This build takes a fresh native AX audio context on launch and releases it on exit/foreground changes. Compiled guests do not acquire a tone voice or implement 3DS audio. Host checks and Wii U cross-builds verify the code; hearing silence needs this short round.

docs.title: Run these two apps
docs.text:
1. Copy the ZIP's sd-card/ contents to your SD root. Keep sd:/ctr2wup/ and all its reports and saves. Launch from Aroma as before; no WUP installation or ROM/key is needed.
  2. Open CTR2WUP Audio Check 0.20.0. Turn up TV and GamePad volume. At the launch-music prompt press R if it is quiet, or L if the launch sound still plays. At the next prompt press A for the short native tone, then R if it plays through both TV and GamePad, or L to record a problem. Press Minus to exit.
  3. Open CTR2WUP GX Transfers 0.20.0. At the two picture prompts confirm with R, or report an incorrect picture with L. The TV should show green, then red, then green; the GamePad stays blue. No test tone should play. Press Minus to exit.

If an app hangs or displays an audio/storage error, stop that run and return any files it saved. Repeating a failure is not needed to produce a report.

docs.title: Send the results here
docs.text:
The apps display RESULT VERIFIED and the result filename. Plain-text files are in sd:/ctr2wup/:

  • result-native-audio-0.20.0-*.txt
  • result-compiled-gx-transfer-0.20.0-*.txt
  • Matching native-audio-*.txt and compiled-gx-transfer-*.txt full traces, if present.

Upload those new files in this chat, together or as a ZIP below 32 MiB. Add one short note stating whether launch music stopped in both apps and whether Minus returned normally in both. Pictures are optional. The completed Save/RomFS checks need no new upload.

docs.title: Purpose and limits
docs.text:
Audio Check records launch-music silence and the native tone on both outputs. GX confirms that the same startup does not disrupt a compiled original guest or its transfer pictures. Reports record AX initialization, inherited-context resets and cleanup counters. An initialized AX context alone cannot prove audible silence. These tests do not establish 3DS guest audio, PICA draws, commercial gameplay or an installed WUP.

Maintained source: docs/launch-audio.md · 1b14ea67cba6. GitHub source and issue links may require repository access.

docs.title: Milestones and remaining work
docs.text:
Updated October 13, 2026 for v0.20.0. The product is an UWUVCI-style Windows GUI: Select owned 3DS ROM → configure title/artwork → Inject → install its WUP → play from the Wii U Menu. The CLI is the shared engine. Super Mario 3D Land is the first candidate; its exact revision remains unverified.

Approximately 20% implemented; 0/7 full milestones accepted. The estimate is a rough engineering judgment, not a percentage of issues, tests or commits. These 35 remaining work items make the work actionable; creating or closing an issue does not automatically accept a milestone or raise the completion estimate.

The project brief defines requirements, the product plan defines execution order, and STATUS.md records current results. Historical version details and receipts remain in development history.

docs.title: How to use the roadmap
docs.text:
The existing seven GitHub milestone issues remain overview trackers. Each work item below is a separate implementation or evidence task feeding its milestone. Project #2 is the authority for status, blockers and reviewed full acceptance. milestone-status.json records versioned scope/evidence and initial seed values; it cannot overwrite existing Project values. The states below are a dated evidence snapshot. Manual issue notes and acceptance checkmarks remain reviewable.

State Meaning Planned Defined remaining work; implementation has not begun. In progress Partial implementation exists; acceptance remains open. Awaiting evidence The scoped implementation/test artifact exists, but the required physical or user evidence is missing. Blocked An identified input or acceptance prerequisite prevents completing this task.

needs-console, needs-input and needs-windows identify required evidence or resources, independently of the work state. Dependencies describe prerequisites for accepting a task; independent original fixtures, interface review and preparation may proceed while prerequisites remain open. A task is complete only when its stated criteria have evidence. Milestone closure requires its full exit criteria and reviewed console/Windows/title evidence, never an automatic checklist.

Commercial ROMs, code, assets, saves, keys, traces and packages stay in the documented private workflow. GitHub issue evidence uses original fixtures or redacted reports; never attach a game or key. Desktop/sanitizer/emulated-PowerPC passes establish their stated boundaries, not physical-console execution.

docs.title: Milestone overview
docs.text:
Milestone State Remaining acceptance M1: Native Wii U platform Awaiting evidence Launch-audio regression, platform lifecycle/recovery and installed original WUP evidence M2: CPU translation and performance In progress Exercised CPU/ABI/fallback coverage and actual Espresso timing M3: Homebrew execution runtime In progress Stable physical compiled guest plus broader services/modules/audio M4: PICA to GX2 rendering In progress Real PICA/GX2 draws/shaders/TEV/coherency and measured scenes M5: Super Mario 3D Land revision Blocked Owned exact-revision intake and Mario gameplay/audio/save/performance M6: Automated ROM to WUP conversion In progress Full Windows conversion, installer acceptance and rebuild/save continuity M7: Windows GUI injector Planned Responsive packaged Windows GUI Inject-to-playable-WUP workflow

The implementation sequence is P1–P5 in the product plan: resolve portable translation and original WUP packaging early; identify the selected revision; implement its execution/renderer requirements; prove Windows conversion; then implement the GUI. Milestones track acceptance boundaries, so independent work can overlap without claiming downstream completion.

docs.title: M1: Native Wii U platform
docs.text:
State: Awaiting evidence. Full acceptance: open.

Entry: Versioned original Native/guest diagnostics build with WUT/devkitPPC, and the tester can run them under the documented Wii U environment. A diagnostic RPX/WUHB is distinct from an installed WUP.

Deliverables: A reproducible native platform build, checked result/save paths, a short guided console kit, an installed original diagnostic and a versioned platform acceptance record.

Exit criteria: Physical evidence establishes both screens, required controls/touch, native audio, reliable launch/exit, SD persistence/recovery and a documented stability session. An original WUP installs and launches/exits from the Wii U Menu.

Verified desktop/earlier evidence: Older native reports and the confirmed Minus exit are retained. The user reports Native/Guarded/Compiled completed without errors on v0.14.5; supplied text logs have older headers. A valid visit-1 snapshot proves initial persistence, while a later Save update failed and no new reports appeared. Current independent TXT read-back and save publication/recovery have desktop/sanitizer checks, not new console acceptance.

Reviewed physical follow-up: Named TXT collection, original fresh-launch save reload, embedded/SD assets and GX transfers pass their scoped checks; pictures and Minus return have user confirmation. Looping launch music remains an open defect.

Still needs external evidence/input: Focused audio regression, exact firmware/Aroma/installer versions and native/installed lifecycle/recovery evidence require the Wii U. No game dump is needed for the original diagnostics.

References: Console evidence · Short follow-up · Guided tests · Console guide.

docs.text:

docs.title: M2: CPU translation and performance
docs.text:
State: In progress. Full acceptance: open.

Entry: The audited external lifter generates C through a checked portable ABI; original interpreter/AOT/reference fixtures and an emulated big-endian PowerPC correctness route are available.

Deliverables: Documented exercised ARM/Thumb/VFP support, checked generated-code/memory behavior, observable fallback and private trace handling, plus actual Espresso timing/memory reports.

Exit criteria: Original exercised workloads have independently supported state/fault parity, explicit unsupported behavior and reviewable real Wii U performance limits. The selected title must separately demonstrate useful gameplay performance in M5.

Verified desktop/earlier evidence: Current original CPU/reference and external AOT checks cover a bounded subset, eight single-core contexts, scoped synchronization and independent ARM1176 cases. GCC/Clang sanitizers and emulated big-endian PowerPC are supporting correctness evidence. No actual Espresso benchmark or full ARM/VFP coverage is claimed.

Still needs external evidence/input: Original benchmarks can proceed without a ROM. Real timing requires the Wii U; title-driven coverage and fallback analysis need the private exact-revision executable/trace.

References: CPU subset · Stack semantics · External lifter ABI · Threads.

docs.title: m2-instruction-coverage: Complete exercised ARM, Thumb and VFP correctness
docs.text:
Close concrete CPU gaps with independent references and original fixtures, preserving visible errors for unsupported behavior.

State: In progress · Needs: none for original-fixture development.

New 3DS exclusives, stereoscopic TV, online services, cameras, microphone, DLC/update merging, save import/export and broad arbitrary-ROM compatibility remain deferred. Titles that require them need separate implementation/evidence.

Public documentation delivery is separate from gameplay acceptance. The private source repository remains private: private Pages is unavailable on the user’s free plan, while the generated offline HTML and public docs-only export support free publication. The user declines private-repository branch protection; topic branches, reviewable PRs and passing CI remain the development convention. No paid subscription or administrative setting is assumed enabled. See GitHub development for actual access limits.
