docs.title: Original encrypted homebrew packaging
docs.text: Version 0.4.0 implements an original, scoped encrypted writer and a separate decrypting verifier. No package has been installed or launched on a physical Wii U. The offline test uses invented test certificates and a synthetic key; it cannot produce an installable title. Commercial conversion remains disabled.

docs.title: Implemented profile
docs.text:
host.package_writer packs original code/content/meta staging into four encrypted 0x2001 contents: FST, code, content and meta. It supports application IDs beginning 00050000, explicit version/group/OS fields, UTF-8 names, nested and empty directories, empty files and at most 1 GiB per content group. Files start at 32-byte boundaries; contents are padded with zeros to 32 KiB.

AES-128-CBC uses the content index followed by zero bytes as its IV. A fresh random title key is wrapped with the locally supplied common key using the title ID as IV. TMD content records contain SHA-1 of padded plaintext plus 12 zero bytes; SHA-256 protects the content-record group and content-info tables. The ticket contains one content-access bitmap. Common-key index 0, unpersonalized tickets, RSA-2048/SHA-256 header layouts and absent signatures are the only implemented profile. Hashed 0x2003/H3 writing, disc/update/shared contents, authentic signatures and retail-console installation are unsupported.

The writer checks RPX structure and XML identity, rejects symlinks and unsafe or case-colliding paths, refuses existing outputs, detects changed inputs, checks disk space and keeps unfinished output in a temporary directory. It streams content with 1 MiB buffers; bounded FST/name metadata is held in memory. FST logical cluster placement, ownership, COS permissions/resources and metadata/ artwork are research settings awaiting installer/console evidence.

host.package_integrity independently reads the result without calling the writer's FST, inventory or serialization functions. It unwraps the key, verifies every padded plaintext hash, bounds/tree/parents/names/content assignments/file ranges and zero padding, checks decrypted XML against TMD identity and launch entry, and optionally compares every file hash and directory with source staging. Certificate layout and CP/XS issuer agreement are checked; a trusted root and signature authentication are not established. The existing structural validator still works without a key, with an explicitly narrower result.

docs.title: Local inputs and commands
docs.text:
Install the licensed crypto dependency in your Python environment:

python -m pip install '.[packaging]'

Copy packaging/local-inputs.example.json into an ignored private configuration directory. Its paths resolve relative to the configuration file:

{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "signature_policy": "homebrew_unsigned",
  "common_key_file": "common.key",
  "certificate_file": "title.cert"
}

The common-key file must contain exactly 16 raw bytes. The certificate file is a user-managed binary chain with its parents and one RSA-2048 CP and XS signer. Establish its provenance locally. No key, certificate or donor is downloaded or provided by CTR2WUP. Keep these files outside the staged folders; their paths and values are omitted from packaging reports. Do not paste keys into command-line arguments or conversations. The explicit policy acknowledges unsigned homebrew; it does not establish which patched installer/environment will accept the result.

python -m host stage-title PATH.rpx --title-id YOUR_APPLICATION_ID --name "My title" --output private/my-staging
python -m host pack-title private/my-staging --config private/packaging/local-inputs.json --output private/my-package
python -m host verify-package private/my-package --common-key-file private/packaging/common.key --expected-staging private/my-staging
python -m host validate-package private/my-package

stage-title creates original XML/checker artwork and an empty content/; it produces staging, not a WUP. pack-title publishes the .app, TMD, ticket, certificate and report only after successful independent decrypted/file checks. Its installable_wup field explicitly awaits installer and console validation. The report separates decrypted integrity, unauthenticated signatures and unrun installation. It never claims an authentic or proven installable title.

docs.title: Title identity
docs.text:
IDs are explicit; no globally safe homebrew range is assumed. Staging/packing does not reserve an ID or inspect installed console titles. Check your console inventory and local projects before using an ID. The existing explicit local registry command remains available after structural validation:

python packaging/validate.py PATH --registry private/title-registry.json --reserve "my project identity"

The registry covers only this user's local allocations. Same-owner rebuilds may update the package revision while retaining the title ID; a different owner cannot take it. Serialize concurrent registry writes. TMD digests and randomized ciphertext are package revisions; title/save identity remains the explicit ID. Rebuild/save continuity, installation, Menu launch, exit and uninstall await physical-console tests. No installation is automated.

docs.title: Evidence and dependency audit
docs.text:
20 new offline tests exercise streaming across chunk boundaries, empty/Unicode paths, OpenSSL independently decrypting the ticket and all contents, wrong keys, ciphertext corruption, malicious FSTs with repaired hashes, source mutation, unsafe inputs, cancellation and output preservation. tools/validate-packaging.py also packages the real WUT-built RPX, verifies all staged files and exercises both CLI paths. Its synthetic inputs/package exist only in a temporary directory; the retained report records that they cannot authenticate a console title.

The encryption dependency is cryptography 50.0.0, Apache-2.0 OR BSD-3-Clause; CTR2WUP selects the BSD-3-Clause grant and preserves its notice in docs/licenses/cryptography-LICENSE.BSD. The library and its native dependencies remain external Python packages; no crypto binary is bundled here.

Binary layout/alignment/hash facts were reviewed against makefst's fst.h, tmd.h, tik.h, certs.h at e363897e29109e6f1125d60376822c3768d3c2d4 and the previously audited Java/C# packer format descriptions. The writer/reader are original implementations; no source, binary, XML template, certificate or key from those packers is adopted. This is a scoped research profile, not a full Wii U package-format implementation.

The MIT-root makefst candidate bundles GPLv2-or-later PolarSSL, MIT ezxml and Unlicense miniz. Its plaintext 0x2000 route, test signing and production certificate output did not supply the required encrypted profile or certificate provenance; it was not incorporated or executed. The nuspacker/CNUS_Packer checkouts have no identified license grant and remain research references only. See foundation-audit.md for pins and licensing constraints.

Maintained source: docs/packaging.md · 1b14ea67cba6. GitHub source and issue links may require repository access.

docs.title: PICA command front end (0.18.0)
docs.text: The native runtime can now process a small no-draw configuration command list through the standard GSP queue. It stores raw viewport/scissor register values, applies byte masks and recognizes the finalization emitted by libctru. This is a step toward M4. It produces no pixels, runs no shader and submits no GX2 draw.

docs.title: Wire inspection
docs.text:
renderer.pica.decode_commands and runtime/core/ctr_pica.c inspect explicit little-endian bytes. A record contains its first parameter, header, extra parameters and padding to an eight-byte boundary. The header contains:

Bits Meaning 0–15 Identifier; this implementation accepts wire IDs 0x000–0x3ff 16–19 Four byte-enable bits 20–27 Extra parameter count; one record has 1–256 parameters 28–30 Unused; unsupported encodings are rejected 31 Increment register for each parameter, otherwise repeat it

Inspection supports the wire range without claiming those registers can execute. Padding is skipped and never becomes a write. Nonzero padding tolerance is our inspection contract; the audited libctru producer writes zero padding. It is not physical hardware evidence. Native/host budgets are at most 4 MiB and 65,536 writes; callers may choose smaller budgets. Range overflow, truncated records, unused header bits and exceeded budgets fail visibly.

Facts were checked against GBATEK's command-list description and clean libctru commit 9b55eda44cf80b971503991e0c78f9bc8fe50425, gpu.h, gpu.c and registers.h. Its builder splits API arrays into records of at most 256 parameters. Its implementation is compiled only into a separate reference test binary; no emulator or external GPU implementation is embedded in the native front end.

docs.title: Supported execution
docs.text:
ctr_pica_execute starts with a software snapshot initialized to zero; this does not model hardware reset values. Its supported ordinary registers are:

IDs Raw configuration 0x41–0x44 Viewport width/inverse width/height/inverse height 0x65–0x67 Scissor mode/position/dimensions 0x68 Viewport origin

The stored words retain byte-mask semantics. Numeric float decoding, clipping and raster behavior are not implemented. A submitted list must have a length divisible by sixteen bytes and end with one or two single-parameter, full-mask FINALIZE (0x10) writes of 0x12345678, matching GPUCMD_Split alignment. Finalization is handled as a completion marker and never stored as an ordinary register. Configuration after a marker, missing/invalid markers, streamed marker parameters and more than two markers fail.

All other registers fail, including with a zero byte mask. Draw triggers, shader/uniform/table uploads, command jumps, caches, textures and render-target state are not treated as generic successful register writes.

The whole list and counters are checked before committing any register change. Input/state/output/report aliases fail before mutation. The commit pass cannot change unread input. This avoids a 4 KiB automatic state copy; the current devkitPPC compiler reports a 176-byte ctr_pica_execute stack frame. That is a compiler observation, not a measurement of the full Wii U call stack.

docs.title: Standard guest queue
docs.text:
GX command 1 stages the checked guest command-buffer bytes before processing. Its address must be eight-byte aligned; length must be nonzero, a multiple of sixteen and within the bounds above. Unimplemented GSP state flags and nonzero reserved words fail. The cache-request bit uses the existing coherent CPU-backed memory contract; asynchronous GPU coherency remains unfinished.

A successful no-draw list emits one synchronous P3D completion (IRQ 5). The counter of tail-marker writes is separate from that command completion. This does not model physical interrupt timing or assert that hardware emits the same interrupt count. Failure preserves the pending queue entry, subsequent work and PICA register snapshot. Successful earlier queue entries remain committed.

The TXT report records completed lists, writes, markers and the last parser's result/register/offset. Guest-memory failures retain the existing memory-fault report. These observations are distinct from picture/launcher confirmations.

docs.title: Evidence and next work
docs.text:
• make check includes the PICA C suite and integrated GSP rejection/completion tests, normal and with ASan/UBSan. The standalone suite exercises capacity, aliases, counter overflow, the full wire-ID boundary and maximum write budget.
  • tools/validate-pica.py --sanitize --output <new-directory> compares 353 original cases, including real pinned libctru construction, native inspection, the independent Python decoder and checked no-draw state expectations. All 353 vector receipts match an emulated big-endian PowerPC Linux run; this does not establish physical Espresso execution.
  • The original normal-CRT/libctru GX application now sends a builder-produced finalized configuration list and waits for P3D. Its AOT execution exits after 1,489,172 instructions, with zero fallback, 17 GX commands and the expected masked viewport word. Its green/red/green pictures still come from CPU-backed fills/transfers, not PICA draws.

Native/GX RPX and WUHB cross-builds are available. Physical completion/report/exit behavior remains pending. The optional short GX guide is still the same picture test; no completed long input guide must be repeated for this increment.

Actual draw inputs/resources, vertex/shader execution, TEV/raster behavior, GX2 submission and reference scene/performance evidence remain open. Task m4-pica-commands is in progress, and M4 is not accepted.

Maintained source: docs/pica-commands.md · 1b14ea67cba6. GitHub source and issue links may require repository access.

docs.title: Project completion assessment
docs.text:
Updated October 13, 2026, against version 0.20.0 and the product plan.

The live Project owns current task states, waiting resources and reviewed acceptance. This article is a dated engineering assessment and evidence record. Its rough implementation estimate is independent of the Project's task counts.

docs.title: Estimated implementation: approximately 20%
docs.text:
The completion target is a Windows GUI that converts one verified commercial 3DS revision into a WUP, followed by successful Wii U installation, Menu launch, interactive gameplay, audio, and save/reload. Clean Windows operation, rebuild/save continuity, stability, and measured useful performance are part of acceptance. Broad game compatibility is a later goal.

About 20% is a rough engineering judgment about implementation toward that target. It is not calculated from tests, commits, version numbers, or subsystem counts. The remaining work includes large, uncertain areas, so this estimate does not predict a release date or mean that 80% of the time remains.

The earlier estimate was roughly 15% at v0.12. Subsequent work added normal compiler-built homebrew execution, guest thread/context support, standard input and CPU-framebuffer applications, private filesystem save/reload, and standalone application lifecycle support. These advance a reusable runtime needed by the injector. They do not yet demonstrate commercial game execution.

Full milestone acceptance: 0 of 7. This separate measure tracks complete requirements and required hardware evidence. Partial implementation can exist while every full acceptance checkbox remains open. See the milestone checklist for each verified portion and missing gate.

docs.title: What supports the estimate
docs.text:
Area Verified implementation Limits for the finished product Host preparation Container inspection, optional local key/seed import and decryption, executable loading, private intake, external code generation, static builds, original metadata/artwork staging Original encrypted execution fixture passes; no complete commercial conversion, actual user-key import or clean Windows execution CPU and shared runtime Bounded ARM/Thumb/VFP support, checked AOT boundary, memory, eight single-core guest thread contexts, scoped services Incomplete CPU/HLE coverage; actual game and Wii U timing requirements unknown Homebrew execution Eight original normal-CRT/libctru applications, input/exact CPU-written frames, save/reload, standalone lifecycle and read-only RomFS assets Desktop/sanitizer/emulated PPC checks plus physical original fresh-launch save, embedded/SD assets and GX results; broader runtime acceptance remains open Packaging Original encrypted writer and independent decrypt/hash/FST/file verification, including real diagnostic RPX payloads Synthetic credentials; no installer acceptance or retained installable package Wii U platform Named TXT read-back, fresh-launch save reload, current pictures/Minus return and earlier controls evidence Launch-music regression, exact platform versions, recovery and installed-WUP acceptance remain open

v0.14.6 passes 184 Python tests and fourteen C suites normally and with ASan/UBSan, including 1,892 FS and 574 report/guide assertions in each mode. Fourteen external AOT probes pass 28 compile/execute checks; 944 independent ARM1176 cases verify the scoped CPU additions. The new RomFS program passes normally, under sanitizers and on emulated big-endian PowerPC with zero fallback. The compiled save/interactive regressions and guarded/live-input replays pass. These are supporting checks, not a measurement of product completion.

Current reports are under artifacts/reports/console-results-v0146/; the five-app kit and matching source are under artifacts/delivery/console-results-0.14.6/. Private uploaded logs/snapshots are excluded. STATUS.md records validation and the remaining gates. These local artifacts are not a published playable-game release.

docs.title: Largest unfinished work
docs.text:
• PICA-to-GX2 renderer: actual game draws, shaders, textures, transfers, and coherency. Displaying CPU-written pixels does not implement this renderer.
  • Commercial runtime integration: Retail asset integration, required services/modules, guest DSP/audio, retail saves, and any CPU behavior exercised by the first game.
  • Selected-title proof: exact Mario revision analysis, boot, menu, gameplay, audio, save/reload, stability, and useful Wii U performance.
  • Finished injection engine: commercial end-to-end orchestration, caching, cancellation/rebuild behavior, native Windows execution, and real WUP installation.
  • Windows GUI: the specified UWUVCI-style workflow is designed but not implemented. Its Inject action will use the proven conversion engine.

docs.title: Evidence and inputs still needed
docs.text:
The supplied Mario CIA has not been inspected: it exceeds the attachment tool's 32 MiB transfer limit. The CIA intake helper can export a small private executable view for revision and code analysis when the user's computer is available. An encrypted executable can now be prepared locally with the new optional decryption stage, using locally obtained material. Real console export and native Windows acceptance remain pending. That export excludes game assets; commercial asset integration will require access to those separately.

The native guide and later Minus exit have user-provided console evidence. The user now reports Native/Guarded/Compiled completed without errors on 0.14.5. No new logs were saved; supplied logs have older build headers. Save failed, though a valid two-record visit-1 snapshot was received. v0.14.6 supplies an independent named TXT result with closed-file read-back and portable save publication/rollback/recovery. The exact prior console failure causes remain unconfirmed. The follow-up requests Save, then a quick original RomFS test, with no long native/input repetition.

Actual WUP installation also needs the documented console environment and local packaging prerequisites. Native Windows tests remain pending.

Missing inputs block those acceptance checks and title-specific decisions. Further reusable runtime work remains possible; it does not substitute for the missing evidence. Reassess progress after title boot/rendering, physical diagnostic tests, successful installation, and GUI-driven conversion provide new evidence. The next steps are maintained in current-roadblock.md.

v0.15.0 advances the same approximately-20% foundation: local encrypted main-content preparation and support-file import have original fixture/known-vector checks and an actual AOT/RPX/WUHB pipeline proof. The reported U.S. latest-firmware/Aroma/ WUP Installer GX2 setup and earlier successes allow continued independent work; exact versions/hard logs remain pending. Commercial rendering/runtime, installed WUP gameplay and GUI proof still dominate remaining work, so no full acceptance gate or percentage increase follows from the decryption increment.

v0.16.0 adds full canonical RomFS IVFC/metadata verification, private asset blob preparation, a SHA-256 checked file provider and all 14 base texture formats. These advance reusable M3/M4/M6 foundations while the user is away. They do not establish game rendering, Mario gameplay, Wii U file I/O acceptance or installed WUP behavior. The approximately-20% estimate and 0/7 full gates remain unchanged. Current validation/delivery: artifacts/reports/assets-textures-v016/ and artifacts/delivery/assets-textures-0.16.0/.

v0.17.0 adds standard CPU-backed GX queue operations and a stock-libctru transfer application with exact frame checks. GitHub now exposes seven tracked milestone issues, CI/artifacts, review templates and agent guidance. These improve shared runtime foundations and development visibility. They do not supply the missing PICA draws, actual Mario/console/Windows/installed-WUP/GUI acceptance, so the approximately-20% estimate and 0/7 full gates remain unchanged.

v0.18.0 adds a bounded PICA command front end, transactional raw viewport/scissor configuration and standard queue/P3D completion, verified by original pinned libctru command construction and a compiled guest. Draw/shader/GX2 scene work and console acceptance remain open, so the rough estimate remains 20% and 0/7 full gates. The owner supplied Project #2; automated population still requires Projects access, and the tool cannot create a duplicate after an access failure.

v0.20.0 records reviewed physical TXT collection, original save fresh-launch reload, embedded/SD assets and GX transfer/configuration evidence. The looping launch music remains an open regression with a short Audio Check/GX handoff. Project #2 is populated through Actions; its task fields remain authoritative. These scoped successes do not accept a full gate or materially change the approximately-20% implementation estimate.

Maintained source: docs/progress.md · 1b14ea67cba6. GitHub source and issue links may require repository access.

docs.title: CTR2WUP — Work Mode development brief
docs.text: Paste this entire brief into Work Mode, or attach it and say: “Use this brief as the project requirements. Begin implementation and continue through the milestones that can be verified in this environment.”

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Develop CTR2WUP, a Windows desktop application that accepts a user-provided, decrypted Nintendo 3DS game dump and produces a per-game Wii U installation package.

The intended user experience is:

  1. Select a supported decrypted ROM.
  2. Review detected title information and compatibility.
  3. Choose an output folder and press Build.
  4. Receive an installable WUP directory.
  5. Install it on a suitably configured homebrew Wii U.
  6. Launch the game from the Wii U Menu, with the 3DS top screen on the TV and bottom screen and touch input on the GamePad.

Internally, use ahead-of-time ARM11-to-portable-C/C++ translation, devkitPPC compilation, a reusable Wii U 3DS HLE runtime, and a PICA200-to-GX2 graphics backend. The Windows PC performs analysis and compilation; the console executes the resulting PowerPC application and supplies compatibility services.

This is a staged research and development project. Producing a WUP is one milestone; proving a game runs correctly and at useful speed is another. Do not promise broad compatibility or full-speed gameplay before measurements exist.

docs.title: Scope and development rules
docs.text:
• Begin with Old 3DS application software, 2D output, native guest resolution, offline play, and one validated game revision.
  • Accept decrypted NCSD .3ds and NCCH .cxi when the parser actually supports them. Reject encrypted input with a clear explanation. Add other formats later.
  • Use open-source homebrew toolchains. Do not depend on Nintendo's proprietary SDK, a donor Virtual Console title, or bundled commercial assets.
  • Keep user ROMs, extracted assets, translated game code, saves, generated packages, and credentials out of source control and public artifacts.
  • Start with a CLI and a working Wii U prototype. Add the polished Windows GUI after the execution pipeline is demonstrated.
  • Reuse suitable existing implementations after checking licenses and architecture. A publicly visible repository without a license is not automatically reusable.
  • Proceed through routine implementation decisions without asking for repeated confirmation. Ask for a game dump, console results, or a material product decision only when needed.
  • Continue useful independent work while external testing is pending. Keep externally dependent milestones marked unverified.
  • Never replace missing core functionality with mock success. Unsupported instructions, services, and GPU states must be observable.
  • Do not report console success from a desktop test, cross-compilation, emulator screenshot, or package validation alone.
  • Maintain a Git repository, reproducible build instructions, dependency versions, a milestone checklist, and a concise STATUS.md so later Work Mode sessions can continue reliably.
  • On a blocked dependency, record the actual error, implement a supported alternative where feasible, and identify the smallest user action needed. Do not repeatedly retry unavailable infrastructure.

docs.title: First actions: establish the actual foundation
docs.text:
Inspect any existing workspace and its instructions before creating a new project. Inventory the available compiler, Windows build tools, devkitPPC/WUT, network access, test fixtures, and console access.

Audit these candidate projects from their current source, recording commit hashes:

  • https://github.com/fearkov/3dsrecomp
  • https://github.com/fearkov/zakuro
  • https://github.com/mtrdrgz/3ds_recompiler
  • https://github.com/devkitPro/wut
  • https://github.com/devkitPro/wut/tree/master/samples
  • https://github.com/azahar-emu/azahar
  • https://github.com/ihaveamac/nuspacker
  • https://github.com/NicoAICP/CNUS_Packer

Treat this list as candidates, not approved dependencies. Verify each repository's existence, license, build process, CPU semantics, runtime dependencies, actual compatibility evidence, and suitability for 32-bit big-endian PowerPC.

The checked README of mtrdrgz/3ds_recompiler describes ARM-to-C++ lifting with HLE, interpreter fallback, and desktop/Web targets. It also lists gaps including dynamic CRO loading and some services. Its success claims are author reports, not Wii U benchmarks. Source access to the fearkov repositories was not fully verified when this brief was prepared; inspect them directly before relying on their claimed coverage.

Select the smallest viable foundation based on a reproduced build and code inspection. Prefer adapting a proven lifter and HLE implementation over writing every subsystem from scratch. Do not assume desktop-specific SIMD, Rust runtime dependencies, floating-point control, pointer casts, or host threads will port unchanged.

Deliver docs/foundation-audit.md with a reuse/license matrix, the chosen architecture, measured build results, and unresolved risks. Then immediately begin the first executable prototype.

docs.title: Proposed architecture
docs.text:
Keep these components independently buildable:

Component Responsibility Windows host CLI Input inspection, build orchestration, manifests, logging, profiles, packaging ROM/container tools NCSD/NCCH parsing, ExeFS/code decompression, RomFS access, metadata Translator adapter ARM/Thumb/VFP lifting, block discovery, code generation, missing-code feedback Portable runtime core Guest memory, registers, dispatcher, interpreter, kernel/HLE interfaces Wii U platform backend GX2 output, VPAD input, audio, timing, threads, files, saves PICA backend Commands, state, shader processing, textures, rendering, synchronization Packaging adapter Wii U executable metadata and validated WUP generation Windows GUI A usable front end over the same build pipeline

Suggested source layout: host/, translator/, runtime/core/, runtime/wiiu/, renderer/, packaging/, profiles/, tests/, docs/.

Initially link translated code and the runtime into a single RPX. Consider RPL splitting only if executable size or loading measurements justify it. CRO relocation and guest module behavior still need their own implementation; making an RPL does not solve them.

Use a versioned manifest with input identity, executable/module hashes, runtime version, translator version, profile, display settings, toolchain versions, package identity, and stage results. Separate stable title/save identity from executable hashes used to invalidate compilation caches.

docs.title: Milestone 1 — Native Wii U platform and packaging smoke test
docs.text:
Build a minimal WUT/devkitPPC application before involving 3DS execution.

Implement:

  • Separate TV and GamePad output with different diagnostic images.
  • GamePad buttons, sticks, calibrated touch, and an orderly exit.
  • A simple audio sample.
  • Timing, logging, and allocation diagnostics.
  • A minimal host build command and dependency doctor command.
  • A packaging investigation using an original homebrew title and metadata.

Target top-screen presentation at 400 × 240 and bottom-screen presentation at 320 × 240. At a 1280 × 720 TV output, a centered 1200 × 720 top image is a useful default. For the GamePad, compute the viewport from the actual rendering buffer and calibrated input coordinates; do not assume physical panel pixels are identical to GX2 surface coordinates. Ignore touches in borders.

Acceptance: produce a valid RPX and record successful physical-console dual-screen, input, audio, and exit tests. Independently attempt a WUP smoke package, documenting the installer and homebrew environment required. WUP installation is not supported on an unmodified retail console merely because packaging succeeds.

docs.title: Milestone 2 — Portable CPU translation correctness and benchmarks
docs.text:
Translate small, reproducible ARMv6K/Thumb/VFP test programs and compile the generated code for desktop and Wii U.

Implement explicit guest little-endian memory access. Guest addresses remain 32-bit guest addresses; translate them through validated mappings rather than casting them into host pointers. Handle permissions, aliases, shared memory, overflow, alignment, and access failures deliberately.

Verify:

  • ARM condition flags, conditional execution, shifts, carry/overflow, ARM/Thumb transitions, indirect branches, and exception behavior.
  • Load/store ordering, exclusive access semantics where required, and code invalidation.
  • VFP register layout, rounding modes, denormals, NaNs, signed zero, and integer conversion.
  • Defined C/C++ behavior without unsafe aliasing or signed-overflow assumptions.
  • A dispatcher and interpreter fallback that preserve guest state across calls, waits, interrupts, and yields.
  • Missing-block logs keyed by executable/module hash and ARM/Thumb state.

Use trusted instruction-reference behavior and differential tests where available. Include tests running on PowerPC; a little-endian desktop pass cannot establish big-endian correctness.

Measure arithmetic, memory, branch-heavy, VFP, and dispatch workloads on real hardware, including generated-code size, link time, peak memory, and elapsed time. Measure fallback execution time as well as instruction counts. A tiny fraction of interpreted instructions can still consume substantial runtime.

Acceptance: documented correctness results and actual PowerPC timings. These benchmarks inform feasibility; they do not establish game performance. Fix semantic failures before expanding game coverage.

docs.title: Milestone 3 — Boot a recompiled 3DS test application
docs.text:
Create or reuse a redistributable 3DS homebrew fixture in the executable/container format this pipeline supports. A .3dsx fixture may require its own loader; do not silently treat it as NCCH.

Implement the minimum guest environment the fixture actually exercises:

  • Executable layout, initial register state, stack, TLS, and memory regions.
  • SVC handling and a deterministic guest scheduler.
  • Handles, events, waits, timers, synchronization, and IPC transport.
  • Required service discovery and minimal APT, FS, HID, CFG, and GSP behavior.
  • Guest framebuffer presentation, frame timing, and touch/button state.

Start with controlled guest scheduling instead of assuming one Wii U core per 3DS subsystem or mapping every guest thread to a host thread. Preserve observable synchronization behavior.

Acceptance: the recompiled fixture executes guest code on Wii U, updates both framebuffers, responds to GamePad input and touch, and exits or runs a documented stability session. Distinguish a framebuffer demo from a working PICA renderer.

docs.title: Milestone 4 — PICA200-to-GX2 renderer
docs.text:
Implement and test incrementally:

  1. PICA command/state decoding and draw submission.
  2. Guest framebuffer formats, rotation, display transfers, and clears.
  3. Vertex formats, attributes, uniforms, and vertex shader execution.
  4. Texture formats, ETC decoding, swizzling, samplers, and caching.
  5. Fragment combiner/TEV behavior, blend, depth, stencil, and alpha tests.
  6. Render-to-texture, aliasing, readback, and CPU/GPU coherency.
  7. Lighting LUTs, geometry processing, procedural textures, and other features required by the selected title.

Use software rendering or software vertex processing as temporary correctness references where useful. Do not assume a full software renderer is fast enough for the final Wii U build.

Investigate available Latte shader assembly/compilation tooling and its licenses before choosing a shader pipeline. Offline compilation may require runtime traces and title profiles. Scanning ROM assets cannot guarantee discovery of every shader or dynamic PICA state.

Build a versioned shader/state cache and explicit handling for misses: supported generic translation, slower correctness fallback, or a diagnostic failure. Never silently render unsupported states incorrectly.

Acceptance: fixture scenes compare against a trusted reference using defined tolerances and visual inspection; console timing includes CPU submission, GPU work, transfers, and synchronization. Expand features according to observed requirements.

docs.title: Milestone 5 — One commercial Old 3DS title
docs.text:
Request one user-owned decrypted dump when needed. Choose the initial title using reproduced upstream compatibility, required services, renderer features, module complexity, and a short repeatable gameplay test. Do not select a demanding title solely because it is popular.

For the exact revision supplied:

  • Complete required services and kernel behaviors.
  • Add CRO loading/relocations and translated-module dispatch if exercised.
  • Implement required DSP/audio behavior and Wii U output.
  • Implement RomFS reads and correct save/extdata archive behavior.
  • Preserve saves across application exit and later rebuilds.
  • Add missing-block trace import and cache invalidation.
  • Use narrowly scoped, documented profiles matched by hashes.
  • Log unimplemented IPC with enough context to implement it accurately; generic success responses are acceptable only when their behavior is explicitly justified.

Acceptance: boot, menu, interactive gameplay, working input and required touch, synchronized audio, a successful save/reload, and a repeatable stability run on physical Wii U.

Record game revision, settings, console environment, test route, frame-time distribution, memory peak, fallback time, graphical/audio issues, and logs. Use the title's intended frame rate: a 30 fps title has a 33.3 ms frame budget; a 60 fps title has 16.7 ms. Preserve guest timing rather than speeding up the game to improve a counter.

If useful performance remains out of reach, identify measured bottlenecks and attempt targeted optimizations. Document the resulting limits before broadening scope.

docs.title: Milestone 6 — Automated ROM-to-WUP CLI
docs.text:
Expose real commands such as doctor, inspect, build, rebuild, import-trace, and validate-package. Use machine-readable results and nonzero exit codes for failures.

The build pipeline must:

  1. Validate the container and detect executable revision.
  2. Resolve a supported profile or report experimental status.
  3. Extract/analyze code and required modules.
  4. Generate and compile PowerPC code.
  5. Prepare available shader/state caches.
  6. Link the runtime and stage content.
  7. Generate original Wii U metadata and title artwork.
  8. Package the staged title through the validated packer.
  9. Validate identities, sizes, metadata consistency, and content integrity.
  10. Emit the package, build report, and installation requirements.

WUP generally means a directory of installable files, not a single executable. Distinguish it from RPX launch and WUHB/menu shortcuts.

Assign application title IDs using a documented homebrew policy, collision registry, and override validation. Hashing a ROM is insufficient to guarantee a safe, collision-free Wii U title ID. Keep IDs stable for rebuilds and saves; reject system/reserved identities and mismatches among metadata and package files.

Where packaging needs user-supplied credentials or keys, use a documented local configuration and redact them from logs. Do not bundle them. Validate signature/installer requirements separately from package structure.

Support cancellation, paths with spaces and Unicode, sufficient-disk-space checks, interrupted builds, and cached stages keyed by all relevant inputs. Publish final output atomically so incomplete builds cannot be mistaken for finished packages.

Acceptance: a clean Windows machine with documented prerequisites builds and validates the test title through the CLI. Confirm installation, Wii U Menu launch, separate saves, rebuild behavior, and uninstall behavior on the supported console environment. Never automate installation or overwriting console titles without the user's direction.

docs.title: Milestone 7 — Windows desktop application
docs.text:
Build a native Windows desktop front end, preferably C# with a supported .NET LTS release and WPF unless the repository provides a better justified choice.

Include:

  • ROM picker and detected title, region, revision, and platform information.
  • Compatibility state: untested, unsupported, experimental, or console verified.
  • Output folder, artwork preview, and simple display settings.
  • Dependency checks and actionable errors.
  • Real per-stage progress, elapsed time, cancellation, and exportable diagnostics.
  • Build reports and an Open output folder action.
  • Rebuild from runtime updates and imported fallback logs.
  • Advanced settings behind an expandable panel.

Default to top on TV, bottom on GamePad, native rendering, and aspect-preserving scaling. Add screen swapping if straightforward. Mark unsupported features unavailable rather than letting users select ineffective options.

Acceptance: the GUI invokes the same proven pipeline, remains responsive during builds, and completes the supported-title conversion on Windows. Package the application's actual dependencies; do not advertise a self-contained one-click converter while requiring undocumented shells or tools.

docs.title: Completion and continuation
docs.text:
The first MVP is complete only when one supported Old 3DS revision is converted by the Windows app, installed as a Wii U title, and verified through the agreed gameplay/save test. Broad compatibility is a later release.

For every milestone, provide:

  • Source changes and reproducible build commands.
  • Automated test results where they establish correctness.
  • Physical-console checks with actual evidence, or a precise “awaiting console test” status.
  • Current supported features, known failures, and the next concrete task.

Maintain docs/architecture.md, docs/build-windows.md, docs/console-testing.md, docs/compatibility.md, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES, STATUS.md, and versioned build reports.

When console access is unavailable, provide a ready-to-run diagnostic RPX or package plus a short test checklist and requested logs. Continue other verifiable tasks, but leave dependent feasibility and performance gates open. Do not end after generating a skeleton or a GUI mockup.

Defer New 3DS exclusives, stereoscopic TV output, online services, cameras, microphone support, DLC/update merging, save import/export, and broad arbitrary-ROM claims until the initial title works. Track each deferred feature so titles requiring it are identified accurately.

Begin now with the source/license audit and executable Wii U platform prototype.

docs.title: Renderer foundation
docs.text:
renderer.pica.decode_commands inspects complete little-endian PICA command records, byte masks, repeated/consecutive register writes, and eight-byte padding. It bounds input, output count, and the 1,024 wire identifiers, and rejects extended/reserved header encodings rather than guessing. Inspection returns records; it does not mark those records supported for execution.

This is original code. The documented basic command layout was checked against the pinned Azahar command-header/processing behavior recorded in the dependency audit; no Azahar implementation is copied or linked.

v0.18 adds the native PICA command front end, explicit raw viewport/scissor configuration and finalized standard queue processing. It is verified against original pinned-libctru command construction and a compiled guest; actual draws, shaders and GX2 submission remain unsupported.

renderer.framebuffer tests little-endian RGB565 decoding, RGB8 PPM export, aspect-preserving viewport calculation, and border touch rejection. The native Wii U backend has its own compiled display/input implementation; Python results do not establish GX2 behavior.

v0.10 implements direct GSP framebuffer submission, rotated portable decoding of all five linear display formats, and an original ARM HID-to-RGB565 display guest in all Wii U builds. See gsp-display.md for scope and desktop reference images. Console behavior remains pending. This does not execute PICA draws.

Pending: asynchronous GPU transfer/coherency, vertex and geometry processing, shaders, texture sampling/mips/resource lifetime, lighting, TEV, draw submission, caching, trusted reference scene comparisons, and console timings. execute_draw raises an explicit unsupported error. Milestone 4 is incomplete.

v0.16.0 adds an original portable base-texture decoder in runtime/core/ctr_texture.c and a Python reference in renderer/texture.py. All 14 PICA format IDs are implemented, including RGBA/RGB packed formats, luminance/alpha, RG8/HILO, ETC1 and ETC1A4. Base dimensions are powers of two in 8..1024; 8×8 Morton tiles decode into explicit row-major RGBA bytes without an implicit display-origin flip. Little-endian source words do not depend on host byte order. Compressed differential blocks and buffer ranges are validated before output changes; invalid ETC2-style modes, truncation and overlap fail. Mip tails, texture filtering/wrapping, caches, GPU allocation and draw submission remain unfinished. No PICA renderer or commercial compatibility is enabled.

Golden layouts/selectors/alpha/clamping and failure atomicity have C normal/ sanitizer and Python checks. tools/validate-textures.py compares 42 original images with the independent Python decoder and 39 with the clean audited Zakuro texture module at 76f17bf76cd9ea238a94f37d389fe701ab05a673. Format 6 follows Azahar's RG8 convention [byte1, byte0, 0, 255]; Zakuro's [0, byte1, byte0, 255] differs and is explicitly excluded from that comparison. External emulator code is test-only in separate checkouts, never copied into or linked with the runtime/delivery. Actual PICA sampling/render scenes and GX2 resource/coherency/performance checks still need Wii U/reference evidence.

v0.17.0 implements a bounded standard GSP GX ring and CPU-backed DMA/fill/display conversion/raw texture copy/cache checks. Equal-sized unscaled transfers support all five display formats, layout/swizzling and flip. Stock libctru produces exact three-frame outputs with zero fallback. PICA lists/draws remain unsupported; GPU resource/sampling/TEV/shader/coherency work and actual console scene/timing proof are still required. See gx-transfers.md.

Maintained source: docs/renderer-status.md · 1b14ea67cba6. GitHub source and issue links may require repository access.

docs.title: Current-process read-only RomFS assets (0.16.0)
docs.text: This shared M3 foundation lets ordinary libctru romfsInit and newlib code read an explicitly supplied decrypted Level-3 RomFS view. No game patch or host path exposure is involved. The original fixture contains three tiny files and no commercial content.

docs.title: Implemented boundary
docs.text:
The platform initializes a zeroed ctr_fs_romfs with a borrowed read callback, context and 64-bit byte length, then mounts it before guest execution. It owns the provider until all mounts and retained file handles close; active views cannot be reinitialized/closed. The callback must read the requested range or return failure. The runtime stages reads before publishing guest bytes so a failed/partial provider cannot leak partially written output.

FSUSER OpenFileDirectly (0x08030204) recognizes archive 3, the empty archive path, 12-byte all-zero binary current-process file selector and read-only flags. It validates static descriptors and guest buffers. FSFILE supports Read, GetSize, Flush and Close. Writes/resizes are denied. Handles retain ownership across copies; whole-buffer permissions, IPC physical aliases, EOF and overflowing 64-bit offsets are checked. Requests are bounded to 1 MiB, while the provider's file size may exceed 4 GiB. Unmounted/unknown archives fail visibly.

Unmodified libctru resolves directories, filenames and Unicode inside guest code by reading Level-3 metadata. This is not a new implementation of generic FSUSER directory commands. tools/generate-romfs-fixture.py creates the original 322-byte image, SHA-256 C header, manifest and synthetic IVFC wrapper. Hash consistency does not establish signature authenticity.

docs.title: Original application and checks
docs.text:
tests/homebrew/romfs.c runs normal CRT/APT/FS/newlib startup and checks:

  • root file bytes;
  • nested binary reads, seek and EOF;
  • a Japanese filename;
  • directory listing through opendir/readdir;
  • rejection of a write-open, then ordinary unmount and process exit.

It emits CTR2WUP compiled RomFS PASS only after all checks. Desktop and ASan/UBSan runs exit after 49,550 instructions with zero interpreter fallback. The same original generated program also passes in QEMU emulated big-endian PPC Linux. The Compiled RomFS RPX/WUHB is built for Wii U; physical execution is pending. The portable FS suite adds lifetime, copied-handle, sparse >4 GiB, malformed-descriptor, read-failure atomicity and permission/alias checks.

source /workspace/ctr2wup-tools/environment/activate.sh
python3 tools/validate-libctru.py --application romfs --wiiu \
  --output artifacts/reports/my-romfs
make -C tests/filesystem check sanitize

Normal libctru filename/time handling exposed three shared prerequisites: a read-only shared time page, the defined ARM STM writeback form with its base lowest in the list, and ARMv6 U=1/A=0 unaligned single-data accesses. These were implemented in the runtime and checked against ARM1176 references, without changing the program's library implementation. Time starts at an explicitly synthetic Unix-zero epoch and advances with the guest clock; no real console RTC or timezone accuracy is claimed. See cpu-stack.md.

docs.title: Host asset preparation
docs.text:
prepare-rom now verifies the complete canonical three-level IVFC tree whenever RomFS exists. prepare-assets performs the same full verification after checked decrypted container inspection, validates Level-3 metadata, and exports a private blob and manifest:

python3 -m host prepare-assets "private/prepared/game.cxi" \
  --output "private/mario-assets"

The output contains romfs.bin (Level-3 bytes) and asset-manifest.json, including source/code revision, full-tree integrity, blob SHA-256 and virtual file offsets, sizes and hashes. Directory parents/siblings/hash chains, Unicode components, cycles/orphans, duplicate names, ranges, alignment and bounded budgets are checked. Virtual names never become host extraction paths. Unsupported IVFC layouts and corruption outside the old NCCH superblock check fail explicitly. All declared physical blocks are checked, including zero final-block padding. NCCH's checked superblock must cover the complete master table. This establishes hash consistency, not authentic signatures or commercial compatibility. Output publication is atomic and refuses replacement; sources remain unchanged.

docs.title: File-backed provider and optional Wii U test
docs.text:
ctr_romfs_file opens an explicitly configured immutable blob, streams its SHA-256 and requires the expected manifest hash before mounting. It lends the same read-only callback contract to guest FS; libctru still resolves filenames. It closes after guest mounts/handles release and creates no extra SD mount/client. The current standard-C fseek/ftell provider is limited to LONG_MAX on the target (2 GiB minus one byte on 32-bit PPC), despite the abstract provider's 64-bit/sparse-file support. Backing must remain immutable while mounted; this is an open-time hash check, not per-read authenticated storage. Actual SD startup cost, file access and lifecycle behavior still require console evidence.

Build the optional original Asset Files diagnostic with:

python3 tools/validate-libctru.py --application romfs --wiiu --romfs-file \
  --output artifacts/reports/my-romfs-file

The validator checks identical complete guest results for RAM/file providers and rejects a corrupted blob before execution. tools/validate-asset-pipeline.py reuses its romfs/ directory to prove original encrypted CIA -> local preparation -> full IVFC -> private asset blob -> actual compiled libctru file access, with transient synthetic keys and zero interpreter fallback.

The delivery ZIP places its WUHB in sd-card/wiiu/apps/ and the tiny original blob in sd-card/ctr2wup/romfs-test.bin. Copy the contents of sd-card to SD root when available, launch CTR2WUP Asset Files 0.16.0 in Aroma, and follow its short existing RomFS guide. It reads root/nested/Unicode files, lists/seeks, denies writes and exits. This test needs no ROM or key. A missing/changed blob fails visibly and is preserved.

Reports appear under sd:/ctr2wup/, using result-compiled-romfs-file-0.16.0-*.txt plus any full trace. Return those TXT files together in a ZIP; include the observed exit result if it was not recorded. No new physical success is claimed, and the earlier Save/RomFS result round in console-retest.md remains pending. Completed long native/ input guides do not need to be repeated for this asset test.

docs.title: Remaining work
docs.text:
Actual Mario asset/revision integration, other cartridge/archive selectors, extdata/retail saves, console SD behavior and Windows conversion integration remain unfinished. Signature authenticity is unverified. This diagnostic does not enable a retail profile, render PICA scenes or establish console speed.

Maintained source: docs/romfs-assets.md · 1b14ea67cba6. GitHub source and issue links may require repository access.

docs.title: Shared TLS and SRV/CFG startup support (0.6.0)
docs.text: This is a reusable runtime foundation for the planned GUI injector. It needs no commercial ROM. An original ARM program exercises standard TLS/SVC/IPC interfaces and reads configuration through the same C runtime used in the Wii U builds. It does not establish conventional homebrew boot or commercial compatibility.

docs.title: Supported interfaces
docs.text:
ARM MRC p15,0,Rd,c13,c0,3 reads the current CPU's user read-only TLS address. The interpreter, original translator and external ABI agree, including condition skips and instruction budgets. Rd=PC, writes, other CP15 registers and cache operations are unsupported. The external adapter refreshes TLS at every execution entry; an attach-time value cannot become stale after the thread context changes. This does not implement thread creation/scheduling or hardware cache maintenance.

Interface Exact request Behavior SVC ConnectToPort 2d r1: checked NUL-terminated srv: name r0: result; r1: generation-tagged SRV session handle SVC SendSyncRequest 32 r0: session handle; command at TLS+80 Synchronous validated request/reply; SVC result is separate from service result SRV RegisterClient Header 00010002, current-PID descriptor 20, one placeholder word Records registration for this session; reply 00010040/result0 SRV GetServiceHandle Header 00050100, name[8], length, flags0/1 cfg:u, v0.9 hid:USER, v0.10 gsp::Gpu; reply 00050042, result, move descriptor 10, handle CFG SecureInfoGetRegion Header 00020000 Reply 00020080, result, configured region CFG GetSystemModel Header 00050000 Reply 00050080, result, configured Old-family model CFG GetModelNintendo2DS Header 00060000 Reply 00060080, result, 0 for Old2DS and 1 otherwise CFG GetConfigInfoBlk2 Header 00010082, size1, language block 000a0002, mapped descriptor 1c/1e, guest output pointer Writes one language byte; returns 00010042, result, descriptor/pointer

ctr_guest_configure accepts region0..6, language0..11 and Old-family models 0 (Old3DS), 1 (Old3DS XL), 3 (Old2DS) before execution/service access. Diagnostic defaults are USA1, English1, Old3DS0. These are explicit emulated settings; they are not read from the physical Wii U or inferred from an uninspected ROM. Future injection profiles must supply their chosen settings. New-family models 2, 4 and 5 remain outside this execution profile. The libctru enum corrects swapped 2DS/New3DS IDs in a Zakuro comment.

Unavailable service names return a permanent SRV NotFound result d88067fa, without allocating a session. This bounded directory does not wait for services to register asynchronously, even for flags0. It permits library fallback from absent cfg:i/cfg:s to cfg:u; those privileged interfaces are not advertised. Unknown commands, unsupported config blocks and malformed request layouts fault with the endpoint/header recorded. There are no generic-success service stubs. Notifications, subscriptions, user/server IPC, arbitrary descriptors, process identity/permission isolation and cross-process mappings are unimplemented.

docs.title: Bounds and ownership
docs.text:
The transport checks little-endian words, reserved header bits and total word counts within the 64-word (100-byte) command buffer. It preflights read/write permissions for the whole buffer before registration, allocation or replies. Mapped language output is checked before any write; adjacent bytes remain intact. Read/write descriptors require both permissions. Output cannot overlap or alias the command buffer's backing storage, even through a different guest mapping. Unknown handles and event handles cannot be used as sessions. Session handles share the existing 64-slot generation table, with 16 reference-counted session objects alongside the separate event pool. Duplicate/close/stale handles and allocation rollback are tested. Closing SRV does not destroy acquired CFG sessions.

Failures retain IPC endpoint, requested directory target, raw header, result and request/failure counts. Those diagnostics are available in the runtime and SD log. They do not imply that a service in a ROM's allowlist was actually executed. The runtime still owns one CPU/process; this is not a complete 3DS kernel.

docs.title: Reproduction and original program
docs.text:
python3 tools/generate-service-fixture.py
make -C tests/services check sanitize
python3 tools/validate-upstream.py --output artifacts/my-service-integration

The tracked probe is generated from host/service_fixture.py, not a game dump. It reads TLS, connects/registers SRV, opens CFG, reads region/model/language, closes both handles and exits: 89 executed ARM instructions, five IPC requests and nine SVCs. A private synthetic NCCH built from those bytes also passes the normal checked loader and real pinned external lifter. The CLI commercial profile gate and framebuffer fixture profile remain unchanged.

The C service suite covers wire replies, configured values, duplicate/stale/wrong handles, malformed headers/descriptors, permissions, missing services and both session/handle exhaustion. Its interpreter/original-AOT probe matches complete guest state and memory at uneven quotas. External integration compares the same program through all three paths, including a TLS address changed after attach. A separate CP15 probe prevents cache operations from disappearing as emitter NOPs. It also checks unsupported DMB/DSB/ISB barriers instead of silently accepting them. --service-api adds the full malformed-input suite to an external validation run.

All three Wii U diagnostic builds embed the original interpreter/AOT startup self-test. Native mode displays TLS/SRV/CFG STARTUP PASS CODE 0 after success; the SD log records service_selftest. Physical console results remain required. Emulated big-endian PowerPC Linux results do not establish Wii U execution/speed.

Final v0.6.0 reports: validation-v1-20261008T135953Z/report.json (135 Python tests; 27 full checks; 1,001 service API assertions normally and with sanitizers), services-clang-final-v6/report.json, services-ppc-final-v6/report.json (10 checks each, including 566/34/297/35 integration assertions and the service API). All report paths are under artifacts/reports/.

docs.title: Interface sources
docs.text:
No upstream implementation was vendored. Interface facts were checked against:

  • devkitPro/libctru 9b55eda44cf80b971503991e0c78f9bc8fe50425: source/svc.s, source/srv.c, source/services/cfgu.c, include/3ds/ipc.h, include/3ds/services/cfgu.h and thread TLS helpers.
  • The audited Zakuro 76f17bf76cd9ea238a94f37d389fe701ab05a673 kernel IPC/SVC and SRV/CFG interfaces, and the pinned lifter's CP15 emitter.
  • Audited Azahar's documented result-code fields and service-result descriptions; no GPL implementation is incorporated.

Hardware equivalence and broader CFG/Mii/save identity behavior await the selected Mario revision and appropriate reference/console tests. FS/APT/GSP/PICA, multi-thread kernel behavior, audio, saves and CROs remain implementation work. HID pad/touch support is now defined in hid-input.md; motion remains absent. The restricted direct GSP display interface is defined in gsp-display.md; shared framebuffer/relay support is defined in gsp-queues.md. Stock graphics startup and the scoped synchronous GX commands are implemented; see gx-transfers.md. PICA rendering remains absent.

v0.11.0 extends GSP with one local retained relay event/shared page, checked framebuffer queues and diagnostic VBlank/IRQ delivery; see gsp-queues.md. This does not supply stock libctru service threads, address arbitration, barriers or GPU register/command initialization. Those remain explicit unsupported paths.

Maintained source: docs/shared-services.md · 1b14ea67cba6. GitHub source and issue links may require repository access.

docs.title: Testing and evidence
docs.text: Tests must establish the behavior named in their result. Use original fixtures for shared development; keep commercial files and credentials under ignored private directories. Unsupported CPU/services/GPU states must fail visibly.

docs.title: Desktop regression checks
docs.text:
make check
make prototype

make check runs Python and portable C suites, including ASan/UBSan. Separate CI targets are make check-python, make check-c and normal-only make check-c-portable. The latter is appropriate for native Windows GCC, where the Linux sanitizer runtime is not assumed available.

Targeted graphics checks include:

make -C tests/gx check sanitize
python3 tools/validate-transfers.py --output artifacts/my-transfer-matrix
python3 tools/validate-libctru.py --application transfer --wiiu \
  --output artifacts/my-compiled-transfer

The compiled test uses pinned external libctru and the audited AOT toolchain. Optional external color/layout references use a clean pinned Zakuro checkout; that code remains test-only. Full console rendering is not inferred from it.

docs.title: Continuous integration
docs.text:
Automatic CI runs Python 3.12/3.14, GCC/Clang normal/sanitizer fixtures, native Windows host/portable-C checks, workflow lint and an immutable-SDK Wii U build. Required CI summarizes those results; a failed dependency cannot become a successful aggregate. Artifacts include logs and original diagnostic binaries, with source commits, hashes and notices. Read the actual run status and logs.

Manual Windows development validation adds the external AOT execution and WPF SDK probe. WPF tooling readiness is not a finished GUI. Optional manual CodeQL requires existing repository scanning eligibility; it does not enable a paid plan and is not part of the required regression gate.

docs.title: Wii U evidence
docs.text:
Each diagnostic guides its needed inputs and records a TXT result independently of the full trace. Collect the release/commit, app version, launch route, console firmware/Aroma/installer versions where available, observed output, exit behavior and named report files. The console-result issue form accepts this evidence.

Keep automatic observations, user confirmations, failures, skips and unrun checks distinct. A saved result does not prove successful Menu return. A valid visit-1 snapshot does not establish later update/reload. A reported pass can guide continued development while hard logs remain pending.

No new long test is requested while the current tester is away. The existing Save/RomFS follow-up, optional Asset Files and new GX Transfers round await availability. See getting started and each kit's guide.

docs.title: Acceptance
docs.text:
A full milestone closes only when its complete criteria have recorded evidence. Commercial acceptance requires the exact selected revision, boot/menu/gameplay/input/audio/save/reload/stability, actual WUP install/Menu launch, useful Wii U timings and the final Windows GUI conversion workflow. Passing unit tests and creating more diagnostics are partial implementation.

Maintained source: docs/testing.md · 1b14ea67cba6. GitHub source and issue links may require repository access.

docs.title: Diagnostic troubleshooting
docs.text:
Use the application and guide from the same release. Record the displayed build version, WUHB or RPX launch route, and firmware/Aroma/launcher versions when known. Keep existing reports and snapshots while investigating a failure.

Symptom What to check and return App missing from Aroma Copy the kit's sd-card/ contents to SD root. WUHB files belong in sd:/wiiu/apps/; a source ZIP or RPX is a different download. No new TXT result Check the displayed build and RESULT VERIFIED / RESULT STORAGE FAILED footer. Return any displayed SD operation/error number, plus available matching files. A missing report is useful evidence. Save/reload failure Preserve filesystem-test.snapshot, .pending and .previous. Follow the versioned Save/result check; do not delete the files to force a pass. Wii U Menu splash never finishes Record which app/version and launch route were used, and whether music continued. Report the observed return behavior separately from saved test results. System freezes during a guide Record the last prompt/action and approximate delay. After recovery, return any files already written. Do not repeat a known failing run solely to obtain a screenshot or log. GX picture differs or never appears Mark the picture step with L and return the GX result. A desktop reference image cannot substitute for what the console displayed. Console guide passes but injector rejects a game Commercial execution and the final GUI remain unfinished. Read compatibility and current status for the supported boundary. Desktop build cannot find devkitPPC/WUT Follow Contributing or Windows setup. Linux SDK executables require Linux; select the native Windows toolchain on Windows.

Diagnostic results are under sd:/ctr2wup/. ZIP the new result-*.txt files and requested original diagnostic traces, then attach them to the console-result issue form or the current development conversation. Include a brief observation of the picture and exit behavior. Check files for private paths/data before posting. Share commercial dumps, keys or saves only through the separately agreed private intake process; they do not belong in GitHub issues.

The older Native/Guarded/Compiled successes are already recorded. The pending 0.14.6 Save/RomFS round and optional 0.16 Asset Files / 0.17 GX round have different purposes; testing explains which evidence each provides.

Maintained source: docs/troubleshooting.md · 1b14ea67cba6. GitHub source and issue links may require repository access.

docs.title: Checked external AOT integration
docs.text: Version 0.3.0 uses the pinned external lifter's C generation, then statically links the translated executable with an original CTR2WUP ABI/runtime on desktop and Wii U. It no longer stops at analysis. The commercial conversion command remains gated; this integration does not enable arbitrary game execution.

docs.title: Reproduction
docs.text:
bash tools/install-translator.sh
python3 -m host make-fixture --output artifacts/original-input
python3 -m host translate artifacts/original-input/ctr2wup-guest.cxi --output artifacts/lifted-code
python3 -m host run-fixture artifacts/original-input/ctr2wup-guest.cxi --backend upstream --output artifacts/lifted-frames
python3 -m host build artifacts/original-input/ctr2wup-guest.cxi --target guest-fixture --backend upstream --output artifacts/lifted-console
make upstream-check
python3 tools/validate-upstream.py --sanitize --output artifacts/my-upstream-sanitizers

On Windows use tools/install-translator-windows.ps1 after installing official Rust/rustup and Git; native GCC is required for execution. The generation receipt binds the clean audited source pin, current original driver and binary hashes. Source/header/driver changes require rebuilding or regeneration. Configure CTR2WUP_GENERATOR only with a corresponding receipt; this is local build provenance checking, not cryptographic authentication of an untrusted tool. For a source archive extracted elsewhere, CTR2WUP_LIFTER_SOURCE selects the clean pinned checkout and CTR2WUP_GENERATOR selects the existing external driver. For external analysis from that location, CTR2WUP_LIFTER selects the audited 3dsrecomp executable.

The driver calls upstream public discovery/generation APIs and exposes every discovered instruction as a resume point. It discards the emitted upstream recomp.h. The Python adapter removes register-local/page-table/budget optimizations from the pinned emitter's C and inserts an original instruction boundary. Unexpected grammar fails the build. The replacement header is an original implementation of interface facts, under this project's MIT license. The lifter executable/source are external and are not bundled. Its missing complete permission/copyright notice still blocks bundling its implementation.

docs.title: Runtime contract
docs.text:
v0.13 additionally preserves CPU/TLS/raw VFP/FPSCR contexts across real guest threads, implements checked user ARMv6 CP15 DMB/DSB, byte media/SMLAxy and scalar FP word transport, and allows integer work with nondefault FPSCR controls. Unsupported FP arithmetic/control modes still fail before effects. Normal devkitARM CRT/libctru/newlib applications exercise actual thread/C TLS/LightLock, standard HID and shared-GSP CPU framebuffers; see compiled-homebrew.md. The original three-thread, FP-context and media probes bring the external suite to 14 probes. The independent ARM1176 reference has 870 cases and a nested-call trace. Emulated PPC Linux is not a Wii U or performance acceptance result.

v0.6.0 refreshes user read-only TLS from the CPU context on every execution entry. Its original 89-instruction SRV/CFG startup probe matches interpreter/original/ external AOT state and memory (297 boundary assertions). It also rejects unsupported CP15 cache operations and ARMv7 DMB/DSB/ISB, including emitter no-ops; 35 dedicated assertions cover executed faults and condition skips. --service-api adds the 1,001-assertion malformed IPC/handle/resource suite to a compiler/target run. All four integration probes pass on GCC/sanitizers, Clang and emulated big-endian PPC Linux. See shared-services.md for exact interfaces and limits; this does not provide a complete guest kernel or commercial profile.

v0.7.0 adds the original 151-instruction heap lifecycle probe. All three backends match CPU/mapping/backing state at 1/7/23 instruction budgets, with zero fallback and unchanged executable generations. Guest stores fault identically on protected/freed pages. The 1,778 boundary assertions and 307 heap API assertions pass GCC/sanitizers, Clang and emulated PPC Linux. --heap-api adds the latter suite; combine it with --service-api for a 14-check run of all five probes and both API suites. See guest-memory.md for exact supported memory semantics.

  • Registers and guest addresses are uint32_t; page pointers remain unused. Every memory access takes the checked little-endian callback path; span bypasses are disabled. No 4 GiB host address reservation is required.
  • The attach step checks ABI 4, generation 3, entry ordering and FNV code-piece hashes against executable mappings. CRO/module attachment is rejected.
  • State is visible at every instruction. Exact budgets resume mid-function; SVCs unwind to the existing guest scheduler, which owns sleep/events/exit.
  • Callback failures stop immediately through a bounded host setjmp/longjmp boundary. Fault diagnostics retain the instruction PC and failing address; no following instruction or store executes. Multi-transfer instructions may retain earlier transfers if a later access faults. The external instruction counter includes an attempted faulting instruction; successful execution matches the interpreter's count.
  • Executable mapping/protection changes and code writes, including writable aliases, invalidate the snapshot. Ordinary data mappings preserve it. Guest writes clear the single-guest exclusive monitor. Multi-core/multi-thread exclusive semantics are not implemented.
  • Missing blocks and emitted interpreter requests fail visibly by default. Opt-in C attachment fallback executes only the existing bounded interpreter and records every fallback instruction. It cannot supply general ARM/VFP HLE.
  • Scalar VFP words/double assembly are endian-safe. Only basic default-control arithmetic/moves/compare are currently exercised. Non-default FPSCR controls and vectors fail. Complete NaN/denormal/exception/rounding/conversion behavior is unverified; absent helpers cause compilation failure rather than success stubs. Builds disable contraction/fast math. This is not full VFP support.
  • Native guest call depth is limited to 64; deeper calls unwind to dispatch.

docs.title: Verified evidence
docs.text:
The original 85-instruction framebuffer guest produces two touched/button frames, 1,382,534 executed instructions, four SVCs and an orderly exit with zero fallback. Full registers/flags and all loaded memory regions agree with the interpreter after uneven budgets; framebuffer files match byte-for-byte. The separate original 30-instruction ARM/Thumb probe verifies scalar single and double arithmetic, compare/flags, stack transfer, state switch and one-instruction resume. Its register/VFP results also match Unicorn 2.1.4.

The external integration suite passes 566 framebuffer/boundary assertions and 34 ARM/Thumb/VFP assertions with GCC, ASan/UBSan, Clang and statically linked 32-bit big-endian PowerPC Linux GCC under QEMU's 750 model. This is emulated Linux evidence, not Espresso performance or Wii U execution. Real devkitPPC/WUT RPX/WUHB linking also succeeds; physical input/rendering/exit tests are pending.

For this guest the generated C is about 24 KiB, with one function and 85 resume entries. There is no 4 GiB reservation or million-entry page table. The checked desktop run uses roughly 0.02 seconds of CPU for two frames on this machine; this is a regression measurement, not a game or console speed claim. Code-size, memory, compiler peak RSS and fallback timings for the selected commercial revision remain awaiting its private analysis and hardware measurements.

Versioned reports are under artifacts/reports/upstream-* and the main validation report. Emulated PowerPC/Clang checks can be repeated from the cloud host with:

python3 tools/validate-upstream.py --cc powerpc-linux-gnu-gcc --cc-prefix 'bash /workspace/ctr2wup-tools/environment/dev-container.sh' --run-prefix 'bash /workspace/ctr2wup-tools/environment/dev-container.sh qemu-ppc -cpu 750' --static --output artifacts/my-ppc-check

Source tests/recomp/abi.s generated abi.arm.bin with Clang 19's --target=arm-none-eabi -mcpu=arm1176jzf-s -mfpu=vfp -mfloat-abi=softfp and llvm-objcopy -O binary --only-section=.text; the object has no relocations.

v0.8.0 adds the 148-instruction original shared/sync probe (639 assertions) and --kernel-api (197 assertions). All six probes pass GCC/sanitizers, Clang and emulated PPC; the compiler/target runs include the kernel API (14 checks). See kernel-objects.md for exact lifetime rules; v0.13 adds the separate single-core guest-thread scheduler described in guest-threads.md.

v0.9.0 adds the standard-HID consumer (185 instructions, 18 SVCs, 858 boundary assertions) and --hid-api (336 assertions). The validator runs seven probes; compiler/target runs with HID API contain 16 checks. See hid-input.md for the shared-ring contract and live original-AOT Wii U input consumer.

v0.10.0 adds an original standard-HID/GSP RGB565 graphics probe: 1382865 instructions, 27 SVCs, zero fallback; 3603 assertions including four reference PPMs. --gsp-api adds 362 format/rights/bounds assertions. All eight probes plus that API give 18 compiler/target checks. The original ARM halfword subset is exercised in the graphics program. See gsp-display.md for exact limits.

v0.11.0 adds the ninth external probe, relay: 1,383,167 instructions and 34 SVCs per path, zero fallback, full-state/pixel parity including a VBlank between LDREX/STREX. It exports four relay/frame-{1,2}-{top,bottom}.ppm images. --relay-api adds timing, ring, lifetime, rejection and resource rollback checks. Nine probes plus this API produce 20 compiler/target checks. See gsp-queues.md for the single-client diagnostic timing and remaining stock startup/GX/PICA gaps.

v0.12 adds stack and stack_reject, bringing external probes to eleven. The original nested ARM/Thumb program takes 47 instructions/one SVC; 352 assertions compare normal execution and six partial-word fault paths across external/original AOT and interpreter. The 48-assertion rejection probe checks six empty/unpredictable Thumb forms, including ones the emitter erases. --multiple-api adds the stack/transfer API suite (24 compiler/target checks total). An ARM LDM abort restores an early-emitter writeback; prior successful loads remain visible. See cpu-stack.md for constraints and independent evidence.
